title: checkpoint API
text: Klaleus / defold-checkpoint checkpoint Checkpoint is a library for reading from and writing to files in a Defold game engine project.

title: checkpoint.exists
text: exists(path: string): boolean Whether a saved file exists. Returns a real boolean rather than the underlying file attributes, so it reads directly as a condition. Goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency. path — Path relative to project_save_path.

title: checkpoint.list
text: list(): string[] Every saved file, found by walking the save directory breadth-first. Directories are descended into rather than listed. Goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency. The file paths, relative to project_save_path.

title: checkpoint.project_save_path
text: project_save_path: string The absolute path of the project's save directory, resolved once when the module loads. Every path the other members take is relative to it, and list returns paths relative to it. Ends with a separator, e.g. /home/klaleus/.local/share/defold-checkpoint/.

title: checkpoint.project_title
text: project_title: string The project.title from game.project, read once when the module loads. It is the name the save directory is derived from.

title: checkpoint.read
text: read<T = unknown>(path: string): LuaMultiReturn<[ T | false, string | undefined ]> Loads a saved file. A path ending in .json is read as text and decoded with json.decode; anything else is loaded with sys.load. On success the loaded value is returned alone, so the error slot is absent; on any failure — the file missing, unreadable, or holding invalid content — the first value is false and the second is the error string. Name the saved shape through the type parameter to avoid casting at the call site. path — Path relative to project_save_path. The loaded value, or false and the error that stopped it.

title: checkpoint.write
text: write(path: string, data: unknown): LuaMultiReturn<[ boolean, string | undefined ]> Saves a value, creating any missing directories along the path first. A path ending in .json is encoded with json.encode and written as text and flushed immediately; anything else is written with sys.save. Creating the directories goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency; this corpus does not type it. path — Path relative to project_save_path. data — The value to save. true, or false and the error that stopped it.

title: shutter API
text: Klaleus / defold-shutter shutter Shutter is a library for 2D camera functionality in a Defold game engine project. ShutterCamera

title: shutter.activate
text: activate(object: Hash): Matrix4 Installs a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix into the render context. Call it from a render script before drawing the world. object — The game object the camera lives on. The camera's frustum, for passing to render.draw.

title: shutter.camera_table
text: camera_table: LuaMap<Hash, ShutterCamera> Every live camera, keyed by the id of the game object it lives on. The shutter.script file writes to it; read from it rather than manipulating it directly.

title: shutter.cancel_shake
text: cancel_shake(object: Hash, parent?: boolean) Stops a running camera shake and returns the shaken object to where it started. Does nothing if no shake is running. object — The game object the camera lives on. parent — Whether the shake was started against the camera object's parent.

title: shutter.center_behavior
text: center_behavior: Hash Keeps the projection fixed and shrinks the viewport to preserve the display ratio, letterboxing or pillarboxing the remainder.

title: shutter.deactivate
text: deactivate(): Matrix4 Restores the viewport and matrices Defold's GUI system expects, sized to the current window. Call it before drawing GUI. The frustum matching the restored matrices.

title: shutter.expand_behavior
text: expand_behavior: Hash Keeps the viewport filling the window and widens the projection as the window grows, showing more of the game world rather than scaling it.

title: shutter.force_update
text: force_update(object: Hash) Recalculates a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix immediately. The shutter.script game object already does this once per frame; call it directly only after changing a camera property mid-frame. object — The game object the camera lives on.

title: shutter.get_distance
text: get_distance(object: Hash, distance: Vector3, absolute?: boolean): Vector3 Converts a screen distance into the world distance an object must travel to cover it, accounting for the camera's zoom and, under center and stretch behavior, for the viewport no longer mapping to physical screen coordinates. object — The game object the camera lives on. distance — The screen distance to convert. absolute — Skip rotating the result by the camera's rotation.

title: shutter.get_frustum
text: get_frustum(object: Hash): Matrix4 Returns the camera's frustum, the product of its last calculated projection and view matrices. object — The game object the camera lives on.

title: shutter.get_projection
text: get_projection(object: Hash): Matrix4 Calculates the camera's orthographic projection matrix, sized from the display under center and stretch behavior and from the window under expand behavior. object — The game object the camera lives on.

title: shutter.get_view
text: get_view(object: Hash): Matrix4 Calculates the camera's view matrix from the inverse of its game object's world transform. object — The game object the camera lives on.

title: shutter.get_viewport
text: get_viewport(object: Hash): LuaMultiReturn<[ number, number, number, number ]> Calculates the camera's viewport in window coordinates, scaled from the game.project display size and, under center behavior, shrunk and centered to preserve the display ratio. object — The game object the camera lives on. The viewport's x, y, width and height.

title: shutter.screen_to_world
text: screen_to_world(object: Hash, x: number, y: number, visible?: boolean): Vector3 | undefined Converts a screen position to its world position through the inverse of the camera's frustum. object — The game object the camera lives on. x — The screen position's x coordinate. y — The screen position's y coordinate. visible — Return nil instead when the position falls outside the camera's view. The world position, or nil if visible filtered it out.

title: shutter.shake
text: shake(object: Hash, parent: boolean, count: number, duration: number, radius: number, duration_scalar?: number, radius_scalar?: number) Starts a camera shake animation, cancelling and restarting any shake already running on this camera. object — The game object the camera lives on. parent — Shake the camera object's parent instead of the camera itself. count — How many times to displace the camera before stopping. duration — Seconds each displacement takes. radius — How far each displacement moves the camera. duration_scalar — Multiplies the duration after each displacement. Defaults to 1. radius_scalar — Multiplies the radius after each displacement. Defaults to 1.

text: behavior: Hash One of center_behavior, expand_behavior or stretch_behavior.

title: shutter.world_to_screen
text: world_to_screen(object: Hash, position: Vector3, visible?: boolean): Vector3 | undefined Converts a world position to its screen position through the camera's frustum. object — The game object the camera lives on. position — The world position to convert. visible — Return nil instead when the position falls outside the camera's view. The screen position, or nil if visible filtered it out.

title: dicebag API
text: 8bitskull / dicebag dicebag Dicebag is a Defold extension containing probability functions designed specifically for games.

title: dicebag.bag_create
text: bag_create(id: string | number | Hash, num_success: number, num_fails: number, reset_on_success: boolean) Create a marble bag of green (success) and red (fails) 'marbles'. This allows you to, for example, make an unlikely event more and more likely the more fails are accumulated. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag. num_success — The number of success marbles in the bag. num_fails — The number of fails marbles in the bag. reset_on_success — Whether or not the bag should reset when a successful result is drawn. If false or nil the bag will reset when all marbles have been drawn.

title: dicebag.bag_draw
text: bag_draw(id: string | number | Hash): boolean Draw a marble from a previously created bag. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag. True or false

title: dicebag.bag_reset
text: bag_reset(id: string | number | Hash) Manually reset a marble bag. Will also be called when a marble bag is empty, or a success is drawn in a bag where reset_on_success is true. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag.

title: dicebag.bags
text: bags: LuaMap<string | number | Hash, { success: number; fail: number; full_success: number; full_fail: number; reset_on_success: boolean; }> Every marble bag bag_create has made, keyed by its identifier. bag_draw reads and decrements the counts here; bag_reset restores them from the full pair.

title: dicebag.flip_coin
text: flip_coin(): boolean Flip a coin. true or false (50% chance).

title: dicebag.roll_custom_dice
text: roll_custom_dice(num_dice: number, sides: Array<[ number, number ]>): number Roll custom dice. The dice can have sides with different weights and different values. num_dice — How many dice to roll. sides — A table describing the sides of the die in the format [[weight1, value1], [weight2, value2], ...]. The sum of the values as specified in the table sides.

title: dicebag.roll_dice
text: roll_dice(num_dice: number, num_sides: number, modifier: number): number Roll a number of dice, D&D-style. An example would be rolling 3d6+2. Returns the sum of the resulting roll. num_dice — Number of dice to roll. num_sides — Number of sides on the dice. modifier — Number to add to the result. Sum of rolled dice plus modifier.

title: dicebag.roll_special_dice
text: roll_special_dice(num_sides: number, advantage: number, num_dice: number, num_results: number): number Roll a number of dice and choose one (or more) of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) results. Returns the sum of the relevant dice rolls. num_sides — Number of sides on the dice. advantage — If true, the highest rolls will be selected, otherwise the lowest values will be selected. num_dice — Number of dice to roll. num_results — How many of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) dice to sum up. Sum of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) dice rolls

title: dicebag.set_up_rng
text: set_up_rng(seed?: number): number Sets up the randomseed and clears the first number of random rolls. seed — optional seed, if not specified a seed will be generated using socket.gettime(). the number used to seed the random function.

title: dicebag.table_create
text: table_create(id: string | number | Hash, rollable_table: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>) Create a rollable table. This is similar to a marble bag, except each entry can have a different weight, and can return any value (not just a boolean). id — A unique identifier for the rollable table. rollable_table — A table of weights, values and reset flags.

title: dicebag.table_reset
text: table_reset(id: string | number | Hash) Manually reset a rollable table. Will also be called when the rollable table is empty, or a drawn value where reset_on_roll is true. id — A unique identifier for the rollable table.

title: dicebag.table_roll
text: table_roll(id: string | number | Hash): any Draw a random value from the rollable table created in table_create. The value will be removed from the table. If reset_on_roll is true, the table will reset. Otherwise, the table will reset when all values are drawn. id — A unique identifier for the rollable table. The value specified in table_create.

title: dicebag.tables
text: tables: LuaMap<string | number | Hash, { active: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>; original: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>; }> Every rollable table table_create has made, keyed by its identifier. active is what table_roll draws from and removes as it goes; original is the untouched copy table_reset restores from.

title: detour API
text: abadonna / defold-detour detour Recast/Detour navigation meshes: path queries and crowd agents. NavMesh PathPoint Crowd CrowdAgent

title: detour.Crowd.add_agent
text: add_agent(position: Vector3, radius: number, height: number, max_acceleration: number, max_speed: number, update_flags: number): number Adds an agent at a position on the mesh. position — Where the agent starts. radius — Radius of the agent. height — Height of the agent. max_acceleration — Largest change of velocity per second. max_speed — Largest speed. update_flags — Detour dtUpdateFlags to steer with: 1 anticipate turns, 2 avoid obstacles, 4 keep apart from other agents, 8 optimize the path by visibility, 16 optimize the path by topology. The agent id, or -1 when the crowd already holds 128 agents. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.CrowdAgent.position
text: position: Vector3 Where the agent is after the update.

title: detour.CrowdAgent.state
text: state: "walk" | "offmesh" | "invalid" "walk" on the mesh, "offmesh" on an off-mesh connection, else "invalid".

title: detour.CrowdAgent.velocity
text: velocity: Vector3 The agent's velocity after the update.

title: detour.Crowd.remove_agent
text: remove_agent(agent: number) Removes an agent from the crowd. agent — Id of the agent, as {@link Crowd.add_agent} returned it. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.Crowd.reset_target
text: reset_target(agent?: number) Stops agents moving toward their target. agent — Id of the agent to stop. When omitted, every agent is stopped. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.Crowd.set_target
text: set_target(target: Vector3, agent?: number) Sends agents toward the point of the mesh nearest to target. target — Where to go. agent — Id of the agent to send. When omitted, every active agent is sent. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.Crowd.update
text: update(dt: number): LuaTable<number, CrowdAgent> Moves every agent by one step of the simulation. dt — Time step in seconds. The active agents, keyed by agent id. Read them with get or pairs: keys start at 0 and skip inactive agents, so this is not an array. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.init
text: init(navmesh: string): NavMesh Loads a navigation mesh. navmesh — The bytes of a Recast navmesh set file, such as sys.load_resource returns. The mesh.

title: detour.NavMesh.create_crowd
text: create_crowd(max_agent_radius: number): Crowd Prepares the mesh's crowd for up to 128 agents. Calling it again resets the same crowd. max_agent_radius — Radius of the largest agent the crowd will hold. The crowd.

title: detour.NavMesh.delete
text: delete() Frees the mesh and its crowd. Neither can be used after it.

title: detour.NavMesh.find_path
text: find_path(start: Vector3, finish: Vector3, straight_path_options?: number): LuaTable<number, PathPoint> Finds a path between the points of the mesh nearest to start and finish. When finish cannot be reached, the path ends at the reachable point nearest to it; when no path is found, the table is empty. start — Where to start from. finish — Where to go. straight_path_options — Detour dtStraightPathOptions: 1 adds a corner where the path crosses into another area, 2 where it crosses any polygon edge. Default is 0. The corners of the path, in order. Read them with get or pairs: keys start at 0, so this is not an array. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

title: detour.NavMesh.set_area_cost
text: set_area_cost(costs: number[]) Sets the cost of crossing each area. The defaults are 1 for areas 0, 2 and 3, 10 for area 1, 2 for area 4 and 1.5 for area 5. costs — Cost per area: costs[0] is the cost of area 0.

title: detour.NavMesh.set_include_flags
text: set_include_flags(flags: number) Sets the polygon flags a path may cross. The default is every flag but 0x10, which marks disabled polygons. flags — Bit mask of polygon flags.

title: detour.PathPoint.area
text: area: number Area id of the polygon the corner lies on.

title: detour.PathPoint.end
text: end?: true true on the corner the path ends at.

title: detour.PathPoint.offmesh
text: offmesh?: true true on a corner that starts an off-mesh connection.

title: detour.PathPoint.position
text: position: Vector3 Where the corner lies on the mesh.

title: detour.PathPoint.start
text: start?: true true on the corner the path starts from.

title: ink API
text: abadonna / defold-ink ink The Ink language runtime implementation in Lua, an alternative to Narrator, based on parsing ink JSON files. Story Paragraph Answer StoryState SerializedStory

title: ink.Answer.tags
text: tags: string[] The tags attached to the choice, empty when it has none.

title: ink.Answer.text
text: text: string The choice text.

title: ink.create
text: create(s: string): Story Parses a compiled ink story and returns a story instance. s — The ink JSON text, for example from sys.load_resource. It must be UTF-8. The story instance.

title: ink.Paragraph.tags
text: tags: string[] The tags attached to the paragraph, empty when it has none.

title: ink.Paragraph.text
text: text: string The paragraph text, trimmed. It is empty for a paragraph that only carries tags.

title: ink.SerializedStory.globals
text: globals: LuaTable<string, unknown> The story's global variables.

title: ink.SerializedStory.root
text: root: LuaTable The visit counts of the story's containers.

title: ink.Story.add_observer
text: add_observer: (name: string, f: (this: void, value: unknown) => void) => void Assigns an observer function to a global variable. Each global variable can have multiple observers.

title: ink.Story.assign_value
text: assign_value: (name: string, value: unknown) => void Assigns a value to a global variable and calls all its observers.

title: ink.Story.bind
text: bind: (name: string, f: (this: void, ...args: any[]) => unknown) => void Binds a Lua function to an ink external function, which the story then calls with the external function's arguments.

title: ink.Story.continue
text: continue: (answer?: number) => StoryOutput Returns the next paragraphs and choices.

title: ink.Story.deserialize
text: deserialize: (data: SerializedStory, path: string, reset_observers?: boolean) => StoryOutput Restores the story's variables and visit counts from serialize, then jumps to a path and returns its paragraphs and choices.

title: ink.Story.eval
text: eval: (expression: string) => unknown Returns the result of evaluating a Lua expression, with the name of every global variable replaced by its value.

title: ink.Story.get_state
text: get_state: () => StoryState Returns the current state of the story, to save and pass to restore later.

title: ink.Story.jump
text: jump: (path: string) => StoryOutput Jumps to a named knot or stitch, and returns its paragraphs and choices.

title: ink.Story.remove_observer
text: remove_observer: (name: string, f?: (this: void, value: unknown) => void) => void Removes an observer function.

title: ink.Story.restore
text: restore: (state: StoryState, with_bindings?: boolean, ignore_errors?: boolean) => StoryOutput Restores the story from a state saved with get_state, by replaying it from the start, and returns its last paragraphs and choices. The story should be created from the same, or a similar, JSON.

title: ink.Story.serialize
text: serialize: () => SerializedStory Returns the story's variables and visit counts, an alternative to get_state that survives script changes better. Pass it to deserialize, not to restore.

title: ink.StoryState.input
text: input: LuaTable[] The player's inputs, in order: answers, jumps, flow switches and assigned values.

title: ink.StoryState.randoms
text: randoms: number[] The random values the story rolled, so a replay rolls the same ones.

title: ink.Story.switch_flow
text: switch_flow: (name?: string) => void Creates a new parallel flow or switches to an existing one.

title: ink.Story.variables
text: variables: LuaTable<string, unknown> A table of all global variables, to read and set. Use assign_value to notify observer functions about a change.

title: ink.StoryOutput
text: StoryOutput type StoryOutput = LuaMultiReturn<[ Paragraph[], Answer[] ]>

title: browser_io.copy
text: browser_io.copy(text: string, callback: function): number Copies UTF-8 text to the browser clipboard asynchronously. Call from a direct user interaction where required by the browser. text — Text to copy. callback — Called as callback(self, result). result contains success, cancelled, operation, and error when applicable. request_id — Request identifier.

title: browser_io.is_supported
text: browser_io.is_supported(): boolean Returns true when the extension is running on an HTML5 build. This is a platform check; use can functions for individual browser capabilities. supported — True on HTML5, false on other platforms.

title: browser_io.open_file
text: browser_io.open_file(callback: function): number Opens the browser file picker and asynchronously reads one file. Supported forms are open_file(callback), open_file(nil, callback), and open_file(options, callback). callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. Empty files return data as an empty string and size as 0. request_id — Request identifier. browser_io.open_file(options: table | undefined, callback: function): number Opens the browser file picker and asynchronously reads one file. Supported forms are open_file(callback), open_file(nil, callback), and open_file(options, callback). options — Optional table. accept is an HTML accept string and max_size is the maximum file size in bytes. The default max_size is 16 MiB. callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. Empty files return data as an empty string and size as 0. request_id — Request identifier.

title: browser_io.paste
text: browser_io.paste(callback: function): number Reads UTF-8 text from the browser clipboard asynchronously. Call from a direct user interaction where required by the browser. callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.data contains the clipboard text and result.size contains its byte length. request_id — Request identifier.

title: browser_io.save_file
text: browser_io.save_file(filename: string, data: string, callback: function): number Creates a browser download from a Lua string. Binary strings are supported. Supported forms are save_file(filename, data, callback), save_file(filename, data, nil, callback), and save_file(filename, data, options, callback). filename — Suggested downloaded filename. data — File bytes. callback — Called as callback(self, result) when the download has been handed to the browser. request_id — Request identifier. browser_io.save_file(filename: string, data: string, options: table | undefined, callback: function): number Creates a browser download from a Lua string. Binary strings are supported. Supported forms are save_file(filename, data, callback), save_file(filename, data, nil, callback), and save_file(filename, data, options, callback). filename — Suggested downloaded filename. data — File bytes. options — Optional table. mime_type defaults to application/octet-stream. callback — Called as callback(self, result) when the download has been handed to the browser. request_id — Request identifier.

title: browser_io.set_drop_listener
text: browser_io.set_drop_listener(callback: function): boolean Registers a persistent file drag-and-drop listener on the browser window. Supported forms are set_drop_listener(callback), set_drop_listener(nil, callback), and set_drop_listener(options, callback). callback — Called for each completed drop as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. enabled — True when the listener was enabled on HTML5, false on unsupported build targets. browser_io.set_drop_listener(options: table | undefined, callback: function): boolean Registers a persistent file drag-and-drop listener on the browser window. Supported forms are set_drop_listener(callback), set_drop_listener(nil, callback), and set_drop_listener(options, callback). options — Optional table. accept filters dropped files and max_size limits the number of bytes read. The default max_size is 16 MiB. callback — Called for each completed drop as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. enabled — True when the listener was enabled on HTML5, false on unsupported build targets.

title: illumination API
text: astrochili / defold-illumination illumination Forward shading lighting for 3D games, with ambient and directional light, point and spot lights, and linear or radial fog. Add illumination.go to the scene as the sunlight source, add light_point.go or light_spot.go for each light, and set /illumination/materials/model.material on the meshes. The lighting data reaches the shader as a texture, so no render script is needed. The module's functions toggle the debug meshes and set lights and the environment by hand. Environment Light

title: illumination.Environment.ambient_color
text: ambient_color?: Vector4 The ambient light color, its w the ambient strength.

title: illumination.Environment.fog_color
text: fog_color?: Vector4 The fog color, its w the fog's full strength. Also posted as clear_color to @render:.

title: illumination.Environment.fog_max
text: fog_max?: number The distance at which the fog reaches full strength. Values below fog_min are raised to it.

title: illumination.Environment.fog_min
text: fog_min?: number The distance at which the fog begins. Values below 0 are raised to 0.

title: illumination.Environment.fog_type
text: fog_type?: FogType The fog type. The fog fields below apply only while the fog type is not FOG_TYPE_NONE.

title: illumination.Environment.sunlight_color
text: sunlight_color?: Vector4 The directional light color, its w the sunlight brightness.

title: illumination.Environment.sunlight_direction
text: sunlight_direction?: Vector3 The direction the sunlight shines, normalized by upstream.

title: illumination.Environment.sunlight_specular
text: sunlight_specular?: number The sunlight's specular component, from 0 to 1.

title: illumination.FOG_TYPE_LINEAR
text: FOG_TYPE_LINEAR: 1 Fog along the camera's view direction.

title: illumination.FOG_TYPE_NONE
text: FOG_TYPE_NONE: 0 No fog.

title: illumination.FOG_TYPE_RADIAL
text: FOG_TYPE_RADIAL: 2 Fog around the camera's position.

title: illumination.is_debug
text: is_debug(): boolean Returns whether the debug meshes show.

title: illumination.Light.color
text: color: Vector4 The light color, multiplied with the diffuse color. Its w is the brightness.

title: illumination.Light.cutoff
text: cutoff: number The spotlight cutoff, from 0 to 1: 0.3 is like a flashlight, 0.5 half of the sphere, and 1 no cutoff.

title: illumination.Light.direction
text: direction?: Vector3 The direction a spotlight shines. Read only while cutoff is below 1.

title: illumination.Light.position
text: position: Vector3 The light's world position. Each axis is encoded within -2048 to 2048.

title: illumination.Light.radius
text: radius: number The light radius. Upstream rounds it up and caps it at 255.

title: illumination.Light.smoothness
text: smoothness?: number The light's attenuation, from 0 to 1: 0 fills the radius evenly and 1 fades from the center to the edge. Defaults to 1.

title: illumination.Light.specular
text: specular?: number The light's specular component, from 0 to 1. Defaults to 1.

title: illumination.set_debug
text: set_debug(is_enabled: boolean) Shows or hides the debug meshes of the sun and the light sources. is_enabled — Whether the debug meshes show.

title: illumination.set_environment
text: set_environment(environment: Environment) Patches the environment with the fields given and leaves the others as they are. The fog fields apply only while the stored fog type, including one set in the same call, is not FOG_TYPE_NONE, and fog_color also posts clear_color to @render:. The bundled illumination.go patches each field from its own properties on its first update and whenever that property changes, overwriting a value set here. Raises until the bundled illumination.go has run its script's init. environment — The fields to change.

title: illumination.set_light
text: set_light(light: Light | undefined, url: Url | string | Hash) Adds, updates or removes a light source by hand, for lights that are not light_point.go or light_spot.go. position, color, radius and cutoff are required, specular and smoothness default to 1, and each position axis must lie within -2048 to 2048. undefined, or a light whose color.w, radius or cutoff is 0 or below, removes the light. url keys the light, so pass the same value on every call for the same light. It receives a debug message carrying is_enabled when the light is added or removed and on every set_debug. Adding or updating a light raises until the bundled illumination.go has run its script's init. light — The light, or undefined to remove it. url — The light's key and the address of its debug messages.

title: illumination.FogType
text: FogType type FogType = typeof FOG_TYPE_NONE | typeof FOG_TYPE_LINEAR | typeof FOG_TYPE_RADIAL

title: operator.bezier API
text: astrochili / defold-operator · bezier operator.bezier Linear, quadratic and cubic bezier curves through vector or number points, with a uniform position along the curve's length. The Operator camera moves along these curves, and a project can use them for its own paths.

title: operator.bezier.Bezier
text: Bezier Bezier

title: operator.bezier.Bezier.position
text: position(time: number): P Returns the classic position along the curve at a progress. time is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. time — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.bezier.Bezier.uniform_position
text: uniform_position(time: number): P Returns the uniform position along the curve: the point at that fraction of the curve's length. time is clamped between 0 and 1, and the accuracy depends on the samples_count given to new. time — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.bezier.new
text:
new

(points: P[], samples_count?: number, length_func?: (v: P) => number, lerp_func?: (t: number, a: P, b: P) => P): Bezier

Creates a bezier instance from 2 to 4 points: 2 give a straight line, 3 a quadratic curve and 4 a cubic curve. Any other count fails an assert. The default length function is vmath.length, which rejects numbers, so number points need a length_func such as math.abs. points — The points, from the start of the curve to its end. samples_count — The number of segments uniform_position measures the curve with, a whole number. It defaults to 1, and 2 points always use 1. length_func — Returns the length of the difference of two points. Defaults to vmath.length. lerp_func — Interpolates between two points. Defaults to vmath.lerp. new(points: number[], samples_count: number | undefined, length_func: (v: number) => number, lerp_func?: (t: number, a: number, b: number) => number): Bezier Creates a bezier instance from 2 to 4 number points: 2 give a straight line, 3 a quadratic curve and 4 a cubic curve. Any other count fails an assert. The default length function is vmath.length, which rejects numbers, so a length_func such as math.abs is required; the default lerp function, vmath.lerp, takes numbers. points — The points, from the start of the curve to its end. samples_count — The number of segments uniform_position measures the curve with, a whole number. It defaults to 1, and 2 points always use 1. length_func — Returns the length of the difference of two points. lerp_func — Interpolates between two points. Defaults to vmath.lerp.

title: operator.operator API
text: astrochili / defold-operator · operator operator.operator Shared settings and math helpers for the Operator camera controller. The camera itself is driven by the properties and messages of operator/operator/operator.script (activate, follow_point, manual_control and the rest), which are not members of this module. The settings fields are plain module fields; assigning one goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only: (operator as { flight_look_easing: (this: void, x: number) => number }).flight_look_easing = (x) => x.

title: operator.operator.angle_between

title: operator.operator.camera_collisions_groups

text: clamp_angle(angle: number, min: number, max: number): number Brings an angle beyond 360 or -360 degrees back by one full turn, then clamps it between min and max. angle — The angle, in degrees. min — The smallest angle returned, in degrees. max — The largest angle returned, in degrees.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_CIRC
text: EASING_INOUT_CIRC(x: number): number Circular ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_CUBIC
text: EASING_INOUT_CUBIC(x: number): number Cubic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_EXPO
text: EASING_INOUT_EXPO(x: number): number Exponential ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUAD
text: EASING_INOUT_QUAD(x: number): number Quadratic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. It is the default flight_look_easing. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUART
text: EASING_INOUT_QUART(x: number): number Quartic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUINT
text: EASING_INOUT_QUINT(x: number): number Quintic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_SINE
text: EASING_INOUT_SINE(x: number): number Sine ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

title: operator.operator.euler_from_quat
text: euler_from_quat(quat: Quaternion): Vector3 Converts a rotation to Euler angles in degrees, about the x, y and z axes. It reads them back in the order y x z, so it reverses quat_from_euler when the z angle is 0. At an x angle near 90 or -90 degrees the z angle is 0. quat — The rotation.

title: operator.operator.flight_bezier_samples_count
text: flight_bezier_samples_count: number The number of bezier segments an operator samples a flight path with, which sets how accurate its uniform position is. Read each time an operator starts flying to the next motion point. 16 is usually enough; starts at 32.

title: operator.operator.flight_look_easing
text: flight_look_easing: (x: number) => number The easing function that turns the camera between motion points, taking the progress from 0 to 1 and returning the eased progress. Starts as EASING_INOUT_QUAD; any of the EASING_INOUT functions, or a project's own, can replace it.

title: operator.operator.get_active_operator
text: get_active_operator(): Url | undefined Returns the url of the active operator's game object, or undefined when no operator is active.

title: operator.operator.is_debug
text: is_debug(): boolean Returns whether debug mode is on. Starts false.

title: operator.operator.lerp
text: lerp(t: number, a: number, b: number): number Linearly interpolates from a to b, returning a + (b - a) t. t is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. t — The progress, 0 giving a and 1 giving b. a — The start value. b — The end value. lerp(t: number, a: Vector3, b: Vector3): Vector3 Linearly interpolates from vector a to vector b, returning a + (b - a) t as a new vector. t is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. t — The progress, 0 giving a and 1 giving b. a — The start vector. b — The end vector.

title: operator.operator.normalized_target_angle
text: normalized_target_angle(original: number, target: number): number Returns target, shifted by one full turn when that makes the turn from original no more than 180 degrees, so an animation from original takes the short way round. original — The current angle, in degrees. target — The wanted angle, in degrees.

title: operator.operator.normalized_target_euler
text: normalized_target_euler(original: Vector3, target: Vector3): Vector3 Applies normalized_target_angle to each of the x, y and z angles, returning a new vector. original — The current Euler angles, in degrees. target — The wanted Euler angles, in degrees.

title: operator.operator.project_on_plane
text: project_on_plane(plane_normal: Vector3, v: Vector3): Vector3 Projects a vector onto the plane through the origin with the given normal, returning v - plane_normal vmath.dot(plane_normal, v). The normal must have unit length for the result to lie on the plane. plane_normal — The plane's normal, of unit length. v — The vector to project.

title: operator.operator.quat_from_euler
text: quat_from_euler(euler: Vector3): Quaternion Converts Euler angles in degrees to a rotation, composed as z y x from the rotations about each axis. euler — The angles about the x, y and z axes, in degrees.

title: operator.operator.set_debug
text: set_debug(is_debug: boolean) Turns debug mode on or off for every operator and checkpoint: on, they show their camera and checkpoint meshes and draw the active bezier path. is_debug — true to turn debug mode on.

text: Balkan-Ram-Games / spriteloop-defold spriteloop SpriteLoop component playback API.

title: spriteloop.clear_tint
text: spriteloop.clear_tint(url: string | hash | url) Resets the whole-character runtime RGB tint multiplier to white. url — SpriteLoop component URL.

title: spriteloop.clear_variants
text: spriteloop.clear_variants(url: string | hash | url) Clears all part variant overrides. url — SpriteLoop component URL.

text: spriteloop.clear_variant(url: string | hash | url, part_id: string): boolean Clears one part variant override. url — SpriteLoop component URL. part_id — Part id, key, or name. Exact ids are matched before keys and names. changed — True when the part id or name exists.

title: spriteloop.consume_events
text: spriteloop.consume_events(url: string | hash | url): table Returns and clears SpriteLoop animation events collected since the previous call. url — SpriteLoop component URL. events — Array of event tables with event_name, name, data, animation_id, animation_name, frame, and source_frame.

title: spriteloop.debug_destroy_component
text: spriteloop.debug_destroy_component(url: string | hash | url): boolean Debug helper that releases one SpriteLoop component runtime instance. url — SpriteLoop component URL. destroyed — True when a live component instance was destroyed.

title: spriteloop.dispatch_events
text: spriteloop.dispatch_events(url: string | hash | url): table Consumes queued events and calls matching Lua listeners registered with listen. url — SpriteLoop component URL. events — Array of consumed event tables.

title: spriteloop.get_cache_info
text: spriteloop.get_cache_info(): table Gets shared package and texture cache diagnostics. info — Cache entries, reference counts, texture counts, and approximate texture bytes.

title: spriteloop.get_info
text: spriteloop.get_info(url: string | hash | url): table Gets debug playback and package information. url — SpriteLoop component URL. info — Package and playback information, including pending_event_count, max_pending_events, and dropped_event_count.

title: spriteloop.get_part_transform
text: spriteloop.get_part_transform(url: string | hash | url, part_id: string, options?: table): table Returns the current resolved component-local transform of an image or Empty Part. url — SpriteLoop component URL. part_id — Part id, key, or name. Exact ids are matched before keys and names. options — Optional origin setting. Use origin "pivot" (default) or "center" for the transformed base-image center. transform — Table with position, rotation, scale, skew, and opacity, or nil when the part is unavailable.

title: spriteloop.listen
text: spriteloop.listen(url: string | hash | url, event_name: string, callback: function): number Registers a Lua callback for a SpriteLoop animation event on one component. url — SpriteLoop component URL. event_name — Event name to listen for. callback — Function called with the event table when dispatch_events consumes a matching event. listener_id — Numeric listener id that can be passed to unlisten.

title: spriteloop.play_anim
text: spriteloop.play_anim(url: string | hash | url, animation_id: string, options: table): boolean Plays an animation on a SpriteLoop component. url — SpriteLoop component URL. animation_id — Animation id or name to play. Exact ids are matched before names. options — Optional table with loop and emit_events booleans. emit_events controls the full playback session and defaults to true. played — True when the animation id or name exists and playback started.

title: spriteloop.set_frame
text: spriteloop.set_frame(url: string | hash | url, frame_index: number, options: table) Sets the current frame index. url — SpriteLoop component URL. frame_index — Frame index. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to spriteloop unchanged. options — Optional table with emit_events. Destination-frame events emit by default.

title: spriteloop.set_playback_rate
text: spriteloop.set_playback_rate(url: string | hash | url, rate: number) Sets playback rate multiplier. url — SpriteLoop component URL. rate — Playback rate multiplier.

title: spriteloop.set_skin
text: spriteloop.set_skin(url: string | hash | url, skin_id: string): boolean Sets the active runtime skin. url — SpriteLoop component URL. skin_id — Skin id or name. Exact ids are matched before names. changed — True when the skin id or name exists.

title: spriteloop.set_time
text: spriteloop.set_time(url: string | hash | url, seconds: number, options: table) Sets playback time in seconds. url — SpriteLoop component URL. seconds — Playback time. options — Optional table with emit_events. Destination-frame events emit by default.

title: spriteloop.set_tint
text: spriteloop.set_tint(url: string | hash | url, r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets a whole-character runtime RGB tint multiplier. url — SpriteLoop component URL. r — Red multiplier clamped to 0..1. g — Green multiplier clamped to 0..1. b — Blue multiplier clamped to 0..1.

title: spriteloop.set_variant
text: spriteloop.set_variant(url: string | hash | url, part_id: string, variant_id: string): boolean Overrides one part variant. Pass "default" to clear the part's manual variant override. url — SpriteLoop component URL. part_id — Part id, key, or name. Exact ids are matched before keys and names. variant_id — Variant id, key, or name for the selected part. Exact ids are matched before keys and names. If a real variant matches "default", it is selected instead of clearing the override. changed — True when the part and variant resolve to a matching pair, or when "default" successfully clears the override.

title: spriteloop.set_visible
text: spriteloop.set_visible(url: string | hash | url, visible: boolean) Sets SpriteLoop component visibility. url — SpriteLoop component URL. visible — Visibility state.

title: spriteloop.stop_anim
text: spriteloop.stop_anim(url: string | hash | url) Stops playback on a SpriteLoop component. url — SpriteLoop component URL.

title: spriteloop.unlisten
text: spriteloop.unlisten(url: string | hash | url, listener_or_event_name: number | string): boolean Removes SpriteLoop event listeners for one component. url — SpriteLoop component URL. listener_or_event_name — Optional listener id or event name. Omit to remove all listeners for the component. removed — True when one or more listener entries existed.

title: wrap.wrap API
text: baochungit / defold-wrap · wrap wrap.wrap The module a project requires to use defold-wrap: node and go wrap one GUI node or game object, or a list of them, so calls on them chain, and gui_applet creates an applet that shows scenes.

title: wrap.wrap.gui_applet
text: gui_applet(root_node: string | Opaque<'node'>, scene?: GuiSceneClass<object>): GuiApplet Creates an applet on a node, from wrap.gui_applet.new, and when given a scene class shows a new scene of it. root_node — The node, or the id gui.get_node looks it up by. scene — A class wrap.gui_scene.extend returns. gui_applet<F extends object = {}>(root_node: string | Opaque<'node'>, scene: GuiSceneHooks<F>): GuiApplet Creates an applet on a node, from wrap.gui_applet.new, and shows a scene built from a plain table of hooks and fields, copied onto a fresh wrap.gui_scene.extend(). root_node — The node, or the id gui.get_node looks it up by. scene — The hooks and fields, each hook seeing the scene as this.

title: wrap.wrap.node
text: node(node: string | Opaque<'node'>, tree?: NodeTree): Node Wraps a GUI node, from wrap.node.new. node — The node, or its id. An id is looked up in tree first, then with gui.get_node. tree — A table from gui.clone_tree or gui.get_tree to look an id up in. node<const K extends string>(node: readonly K[], tree?: NodeTree): NodeList<K> node<K extends string>(node: Record<K, string | Opaque<'node'>>, tree?: NodeTree): NodeList<K> Wraps the node with each id, keyed by the id, from wrap.node_list.new. node — The node ids. tree — A table from gui.clone_tree or gui.get_tree to look each id up in first. An id it lacks, or every id when it is omitted, is looked up with gui.get_node. node<const K extends string>(node: readonly K[], tree?: NodeTree): NodeList<K> node<K extends string>(node: Record<K, string | Opaque<'node'>>, tree?: NodeTree): NodeList<K> Wraps each node, keyed by its name, from wrap.node_list.new. node — Each name, paired with a node id or a node. tree — A table from gui.clone_tree or gui.get_tree to look each id up in first. An id it lacks, or every id when it is omitted, is looked up with gui.get_node.

title: imp.convolution
text: convolution(src: Opaque<"buffer">, dst: Opaque<"buffer">, width: number, height: number, kernel: [ number, number, number, number, number, number, number, number, number ]) Applies a row-major 3x3 convolution kernel to src and writes the result into dst. Both buffers must carry a uint8 rgb stream of three or four components per pixel and hold at least width height elements. The call checks that each stream is uint8 and that the two streams' component counts match, but not either buffer's element count, so an undersized buffer is read or written past its end. src — The source buffer, read only. dst — The destination buffer the result is written into. width — Width of the image in pixels. height — Height of the image in pixels. kernel — The row-major 3x3 kernel, nine numbers.

title: png API
text: britzl / defold-png png Encode raw pixels into PNG bytes and decode PNG bytes into a Defold buffer, powered by LodePNG.

title: png.decode_rgba
text: decode_rgba(png: string, premultiply_alpha?: boolean): LuaMultiReturn<[ Opaque<"buffer"> & { length: LuaLengthMethod<number>; }, number, number ] | [ undefined, undefined, undefined ]> Decodes a valid PNG into an RGBA buffer with one uint8 pixels stream of four components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils. Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so check the buffer before reading the dimensions. png — The PNG bytes, which must be a valid PNG. premultiply_alpha — Multiply each pixel's color components by its alpha while decoding. The pixel buffer, its width and its height, or three nils when the buffer cannot be created or fails validation.

title: png.decode_rgb
text: decode_rgb(png: string, premultiply_alpha?: boolean): LuaMultiReturn<[ Opaque<"buffer"> & { length: LuaLengthMethod<number>; }, number, number ] | [ undefined, undefined, undefined ]> Decodes a valid PNG into an RGB buffer with one uint8 pixels stream of three components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils. Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so check the buffer before reading the dimensions. png — The PNG bytes, which must be a valid PNG. premultiply_alpha — Accepted for symmetry with {@link png.decode_rgba}; it only has effect in the RGBA path. The pixel buffer, its width and its height, or three nils when the buffer cannot be created or fails validation.

title: png.encode_rgba
text: encode_rgba(pixels: string, width: number, height: number): string Encodes raw RGBA pixels (4 bytes per pixel) into PNG bytes. pixels — The raw pixel data, row by row. width — Width of the image in pixels. height — Height of the image in pixels. The PNG bytes.

title: png.encode_rgb
text: encode_rgb(pixels: string, width: number, height: number): string Encodes raw RGB pixels (3 bytes per pixel) into PNG bytes. pixels — The raw pixel data, row by row. width — Width of the image in pixels. height — Height of the image in pixels. The PNG bytes.

title: png.GREY_ALPHA
text: GREY_ALPHA: number LodePNG color type: greyscale and alpha, as {@link png.info} reports it.

title: png.GREY
text: GREY: number LodePNG color type: greyscale, as {@link png.info} reports it.

title: png.info
text: info(png: string): { width: number; height: number; colortype: number; bitdepth: number; } Reads the header of PNG bytes without decoding the pixels. png — The PNG bytes. The image's dimensions, its LodePNG color type ({@link png.RGBA}, {@link png.RGB}, {@link png.GREY}, {@link png.GREY_ALPHA} or {@link png.PALETTE}) and its bit depth.

text: britzl / defold-screenshot screenshot Functions for capturing full-screen or partial screenshots.

title: screenshot.buffer
text: screenshot.buffer(x?: number, y?: number, w?: number, h?: number, callback?: function): LuaMultiReturn<[buffer, number, number]> Capture a screenshot as a Defold buffer. On native platforms this is synchronous unless a callback is provided. On HTML5, only the asynchronous callback form is supported. x — X coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. y — Y coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. w — Width for partial capture. h — Height for partial capture. callback — Called on post-render (or next frame on HTML5) with the buffer. buffer — Defold buffer containing RGBA pixels (native only, synchronous form).

title: screenshot.html5
text: screenshot.html5(callback: function) HTML5-only alias for screenshot.png(). Callback form only. callback — Called on the next frame with PNG bytes.

title: screenshot.pixels
text: screenshot.pixels(x?: number, y?: number, w?: number, h?: number, callback?: function): LuaMultiReturn<[string, number, number]> Capture a screenshot as raw RGBA pixels in a Lua string. On native platforms this is synchronous unless a callback is provided. On HTML5, only the asynchronous callback form is supported. x — X coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. y — Y coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. w — Width for partial capture. h — Height for partial capture. callback — Called on post-render (or next frame on HTML5) with the pixel data. pixels — Raw RGBA bytes as a Lua string (native only, synchronous form).

title: screenshot.png
text: screenshot.png(x?: number, y?: number, w?: number, h?: number, callback?: function): LuaMultiReturn<[string, number, number]> Capture a screenshot as PNG-encoded bytes. On native platforms this is synchronous unless a callback is provided. On HTML5, only the asynchronous callback form is supported. x — X coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. y — Y coordinate (lower-left) for partial capture. w — Width for partial capture. h — Height for partial capture. callback — Called on post-render (or next frame on HTML5) with the PNG bytes. image — PNG data as a Lua string (native only, synchronous form).

title: monarch.monarch.register_factory
text: register_factory(screen_id: ScreenId, factory: Url, settings: RegisterProxyOptions) Register a new screen contained in a collection factory. This is done automatically by the screen_factory.script. It is expected that the caller of this function is a script component attached to the same game object as the factory. This is required since monarch will acquire and release input focus of the game object where the factory is attached. screen_id — Unique id of the screen factory — URL to the collection factory containing the screen settings — Settings table for screen. Accepted values: popup - true if the screen is a popup popup_on_popup - true if this popup can be shown on top of another popup or false if an underlying popup should be closed screen_keeps_input_focus_when_below_popup - If this screen should keep input focus when below a popup others_keep_input_focus_when_below_screen - If screens below this screen should keep input focus auto_preload - true if the screen should be automatically preloaded

title: monarch.monarch.register_proxy
text: register_proxy(screen_id: ScreenId, proxy: Url, settings: RegisterProxyOptions) Register a new screen contained in a collection proxy. This is done automatically by the screen_proxy.script. It is expected that the caller of this function is a script component attached to the same game object as the proxy. This is required since monarch will acquire and release input focus of the game object where the proxy is attached. screen_id — Unique id of the screen proxy — URL to the collection proxy containing the screen settings — Settings table for screen. Accepted values: popup - true if the screen is a popup popup_on_popup - true if this popup can be shown on top of another popup or false if an underlying popup should be closed timestep_below_popup - Timestep to set on proxy when below a popup screen_keeps_input_focus_when_below_popup - If this screen should keep input focus when below a popup others_keep_input_focus_when_below_screen - If screens below this screen should keep input focus auto_preload - true if the screen should be automatically preloaded

title: monarch.monarch.show
text: show(screen_id: ScreenId, options?: ShowOptions, data?: Data, callback?: Callback) Show a Monarch screen. screen_id — Id of the screen to check if is registered options — Table with options when showing the screen (can be nil). Valid values: clear - Set to true if the stack should be cleared down to an existing instance of the screen reload - Set to true if screen should be reloaded if it already exists in the stack and is loaded. This would be the case if doing a show() from a popup on the screen just below the popup. sequential - Set to true to wait for the previous screen to show itself out before starting the show in transition even when transitioning to a different scene ID. no_stack - Set to true to load the screen without adding it to the screen stack. pop - The number of screens to pop from the stack before adding the new one. data — Optional data to set on the screen. Can be retrieved by the data() function callback — Optional callback to invoke when screen is shown

title: admob.load_appopen
text: admob.load_appopen(ad_unit_id: string) Starts loading an App Open Ad, can only be called after admob.MSG_INITIALIZATION event. This is the manual alternative to configuring admob.app_open_android or admob.app_open_ios, which automatically loads and shows App Open ads. Original docs Android, iOS ad_unit_id — Ad unit ID, for test ads use on Android "ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/9257395921", or on iOS "ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/5575463023" Original docs Android, iOS

title: admob.load_banner

title: admob.load_rewarded
text: admob.load_rewarded(ad_unit_id: string, options?: table) Starts loading a Rewarded Ad, can only be called after admob.MSG_INITIALIZATION event Original docs Android, iOS ad_unit_id — Ad unit ID, for test ads use on Android "ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/5224354917", or on iOS "ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/1712485313" Original docs Android, iOS options — ServerSideVerificationOptions Android, iOS

title: adpf API
text: defold / extension-adpf adpf Functions and constants for interacting with the Android Device Performance Framework

title: adpf.hint.initialize

title: adpf.thermal.get_headroom
text: adpf.thermal.get_headroom(forecast_seconds: number): number Provides an estimate of how much thermal headroom the device currently has before hitting severe throttling. forecast_seconds — how many seconds in the future to forecast headroom — a value greater than or equal to 0.0 where 1.0 indicates the SEVERE throttling threshold

title: adpf.thermal.get_status
text: adpf.thermal.get_status(): number Get the current thermal status of the device status — The current thermal status of the device. One of THERMAL_STATUS_XYZ.

title: adpf.thermal.initialize
text: adpf.thermal.initialize(available: boolean) Initialise thermal available — Return true if the Thermal API is available on the device

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_CRITICAL
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_CRITICAL Platform has done everything to reduce power.

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_EMERGENCY
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_EMERGENCY Key components in platform are shutting down due to thermal condition.

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_LIGHT
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_LIGHT Light throttling where UX is not impacted.

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_MODERATE
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_MODERATE Moderate throttling where UX is not largely impacted.

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_NONE
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_NONE Not under throttling.

title: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_SHUTDOWN
text: adpf.thermal.THERMAL_STATUS_SHUTDOWN Need shutdown immediately

title: extension-camera API
text: defold / extension-camera camera Provides functionality to capture images using the camera. Supported on macOS, iOS and Android. [icon:ios] [icon:android]

title: camera.CAMERA_ERROR
text: camera.CAMERA_ERROR Something went wrong when starting the capture session.

title: camera.CAMERA_NOT_PERMITTED
text: camera.CAMERA_NOT_PERMITTED The user did not give permission to start the capture session.

title: camera.CAMERA_STARTED
text: camera.CAMERA_STARTED The capture session has started.

title: camera.CAMERA_STOPPED
text: camera.CAMERA_STOPPED The capture session has stopped.

title: camera.CAMERA_TYPE_BACK
text: camera.CAMERA_TYPE_BACK Constant for the back camera.

title: camera.CAMERA_TYPE_FRONT
text: camera.CAMERA_TYPE_FRONT Constant for the front camera.

title: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_HIGH
text: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_HIGH High quality capture session.

title: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_LOW
text: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_LOW Low quality capture session.

title: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_MEDIUM
text: camera.CAPTURE_QUALITY_MEDIUM Medium quality capture session.

title: camera.get_frame
text: camera.get_frame(): buffer Get captured frame. frame — Retrieves the camera pixel buffer. This buffer has one stream named "rgb", and is of type buffer.VALUE_TYPE_UINT8 and has the value count of 1.

title: camera.get_info
text: camera.get_info(): table Gets the info from the current capture session. info — Information about the camera.

title: camera.start_capture
text: camera.start_capture(type: string, quality: string, callback: function) Start camera capture using the specified camera (front/back) and capture quality. This may trigger a camera usage permission popup. When the popup has been dismissed the callback will be invoked with camera start status. type — Which camera to use, font or back. quality — Quality of the captured image. callback — The function to call camera state has changed.

title: camera.stop_capture
text: camera.stop_capture() Stops a previously started capture session.

title: crazygames API
text: defold / extension-crazygames crazygames Functions and constants for interacting with the CrazyGames SDK APIs

title: crazygames.add_join_room_listener
text: crazygames.add_join_room_listener(callback: function) Register a listener for requests to join a multiplayer room. Registering again replaces the previous listener. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the invite parameters table.

title: crazygames.add_settings_change_listener
text: crazygames.add_settings_change_listener(callback: function) Register a listener that is called whenever the CrazyGames game settings change. Registering again replaces the previous listener. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the updated settings table.

title: crazygames.clear_all_banners
text: crazygames.clear_all_banners() Clear all banners.

title: crazygames.clear_banner
text: crazygames.clear_banner(div: string) Clear a banner. Will also hide it.

title: crazygames.clear_data
text: crazygames.clear_data() Remove all stored game data from the CrazyGames data module.

title: crazygames.clear_game_context
text: crazygames.clear_game_context() Clear the game context previously supplied with set_game_context.

title: crazygames.gameplay_start
text: crazygames.gameplay_start() The gameplayStart() function has to be called whenever the player starts playing or resumes playing after a break (menu/loading/achievement screen, game paused, etc.)

title: crazygames.gameplay_stop
text: crazygames.gameplay_stop() The gameplayStop() function has to be called on every game break (entering a menu, switching level, pausing the game, ...) don't forget to call gameplayStart() when the gameplay resumes

title: crazygames.get_environment
text: crazygames.get_environment(): string Get the CrazyGames SDK environment. SDK functionality should only be used when the result is "local" or "crazygames".

title: crazygames.get_game_settings
text: crazygames.get_game_settings(): table Get the current CrazyGames game settings, including muteAudio and disableChat. settings — The current settings table, or nil if settings are unavailable.

title: crazygames.get_invite_param
text: crazygames.get_invite_param(key: string): string Get an invite link parameter. value — The parameter value, or nil if the parameter is missing.

title: crazygames.get_invite_params
text: crazygames.get_invite_params(): table Get all invite parameters supplied when the game was opened from an invite link. invite_params — The invite parameters, or nil if the game was not opened from an invite link.

title: crazygames.get_item
text: crazygames.get_item(key: string): string Get a stored value from the CrazyGames data module. value — The stored value, or nil if the key does not exist.

title: crazygames.get_system_info
text: crazygames.get_system_info(): table Get information about the user's locale, country, device, operating system, browser, and CrazyGames application type. system_info — The current system information, or nil if it is unavailable.

title: crazygames.get_user_token
text: crazygames.get_user_token(callback: function) The user token is in JWT format and contains the userId of the player that is currently logged in to CrazyGames, as well as other useful information. You should send it to your server when required, and verify/decode it there to extract the userId. Will call the provided callback with the token. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the token

title: crazygames.get_user
text: crazygames.get_user(callback: function) Retrieve the user currently logged in CrazyGames. If the user is not logged in CrazyGames, the callback receives nil. Will call the provided callback with the logged in user account. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the user table

title: crazygames.get_xsolla_user_token
text: crazygames.get_xsolla_user_token(callback: function) Generates a custom Xsolla token that you use with the Xsolla SDK. Will call the provided callback with the token. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the xsolla token

title: crazygames.happytime
text: crazygames.happytime() Celebrate a major player achievement, such as beating a boss or reaching a high score.

title: crazygames.has_ad_block
text: crazygames.has_ad_block(callback: function) Detect if the user has an adblocker. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and a boolean indicating whether an adblocker was detected.

title: crazygames.hide_invite_button
text: crazygames.hide_invite_button() Hide the invite button when it is no longer necessary.

title: crazygames.invite_link
text: crazygames.invite_link(params: table): string Create a link to your game to invite others to join a multiplayer game.

title: crazygames.is_instant_multiplayer
text: crazygames.is_instant_multiplayer(): boolean For multiplayer games, if is_instant_multiplayer() returns true, you should instantly create a new room/lobby for the user.

title: crazygames.is_user_account_available
text: crazygames.is_user_account_available(): boolean Before using any user account features, you should always ensure that the user account system is available.

title: crazygames.left_room
text: crazygames.left_room() Notify CrazyGames that the player has left the current multiplayer room.

title: crazygames.list_friends
text: crazygames.list_friends(page: number, size: number, callback: function) Retrieve one page of the current user's CrazyGames friends. Only one list_friends request may be active at a time. The callback receives nil if the request fails. page — Page number, starting at 1. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to crazygames unchanged. size — Number of friends to retrieve, between 1 and 50. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the friends-page table.

title: crazygames.loading_start
text: crazygames.loading_start() The loadingStart() function has to be called whenever you start loading your game.

title: crazygames.loading_stop
text: crazygames.loading_stop() The loadingStop() function has to be called when the loading is complete and eventually the gameplay starts.

title: crazygames.remove_auth_listener
text: crazygames.remove_auth_listener() Remove any previously set auth listener.

title: crazygames.remove_item
text: crazygames.remove_item(key: string) Remove a stored value from the CrazyGames data module.

title: crazygames.remove_join_room_listener
text: crazygames.remove_join_room_listener() Remove the currently registered join-room listener.

title: crazygames.remove_settings_change_listener
text: crazygames.remove_settings_change_listener() Remove the currently registered game-settings listener.

title: crazygames.report_game_completed_percentage
text: crazygames.report_game_completed_percentage(percentage: number) Report the player's current game-completion percentage to CrazyGames. The value must be between 0 and 100.

title: crazygames.request_banner
text: crazygames.request_banner(div: string, width: number, height: number) Request a banner. The container will be resized to the specified width.

title: crazygames.request_responsive_banner
text: crazygames.request_responsive_banner(div: string) The responsive banners feature will request ads that fit into your container, without the need to specify or select a size beforehand.

title: crazygames.set_auth_listener
text: crazygames.set_auth_listener(callback: function) You can register a user auth listener that is triggered when the player logs in to CrazyGames. A log out doesn't trigger the auth listener, since the entire page is refreshed when the player logs out. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the user table

title: crazygames.set_game_context
text: crazygames.set_game_context(context: table) Attach JSON-serializable game state to feedback submitted by the player. Call clear_game_context when the state is no longer relevant.

title: crazygames.set_item
text: crazygames.set_item(key: string, value: string) Store a value in the CrazyGames data module.

title: crazygames.show_account_link_prompt
text: crazygames.show_account_link_prompt(callback: function) Show an account linking prompt to link a CrazyGames account to the in-game account. Will call the provided callback with a response table containing either response = "yes" or response = "no". The response is nil if the prompt fails. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the response table

title: crazygames.show_auth_prompt
text: crazygames.show_auth_prompt(callback: function) By calling this method, the log in or register popup will be displayed on CrazyGames. The user can log in their existing account, or create a new account. Will call the provided callback on log in. callback — The function takes two arguments, self and the user table

title: crazygames.show_invite_button
text: crazygames.show_invite_button(params: table): string Display a button in the game footer that opens a popup containing an invite link. This CrazyGames feature is deprecated in favor of Room Data, but remains available for existing integrations.

title: crazygames.show_midgame_ad
text: crazygames.show_midgame_ad(callback: function) Show a midgame ad.

title: crazygames.show_rewarded_ad
text: crazygames.show_rewarded_ad(callback: function) Show a rewarded ad.

title: crazygames.submit_score
text: crazygames.submit_score(encrypted_score: string, score: number) Submit an encrypted score and its plain numeric value to a CrazyGames leaderboard. Leaderboards must be enabled and configured for the game. encrypted_score — The score encrypted with the game's CrazyGames leaderboard encryption key and encoded as Base64. score — The unencrypted numeric score.

title: crazygames.track_order
text: crazygames.track_order(provider: string, order: table) Report an in-game purchase order to CrazyGames analytics. Order tracking is optional; use provider "xsolla" for Xsolla orders. order — The JSON-serializable order returned by the payment provider.

title: crazygames.update_room
text: crazygames.update_room(room: table) Update the current multiplayer room. The table can contain roomId (string), isJoinable (boolean), and inviteParams (a table of string, number, or boolean values). Only supplied fields are updated.

title: facebook API
text: defold / extension-facebook facebook Functions and constants for interacting with Facebook APIs

title: facebook.access_token
text: facebook.access_token(): string Get the current Facebook access token. This function returns the currently stored access token after a previous successful login. If it returns nil no access token exists and you need to perform a login to get the wanted permissions. Get the current access token, then use it to perform a graph API request. token — the access token or nil if the user is not logged in

title: facebook.AUDIENCE_EVERYONE
text: facebook.AUDIENCE_EVERYONE Publish permission to reach everyone

title: facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS
text: facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS Publish permission to reach user friends

title: facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE
text: facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE Publish permission to reach no audience

title: facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME
text: facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME Publish permission to reach only me (private to current user)

title: facebook.deferred_deep_link
text: facebook.deferred_deep_link(callback: function) Allows receiving deferred deep link URL and parameters. More info about Referred Deep Links Show a dialog allowing the user to share a post to their timeline callback — Callback function that is called when information is ready.

title: facebook.disable_advertiser_tracking
text: facebook.disable_advertiser_tracking() Disable advertiser tracking This function will set AdvertiserTrackingEnabled (the 'ATE' flag) to false on iOS, to inform Audience Network not to use the data to deliver personalized ads for users on iOS 14 and above.

title: facebook.disable_event_usage
text: facebook.disable_event_usage() Disable event usage with Facebook Analytics This function will disable event usage for Facebook Analytics which means that Facebook won't be able to use event data for ad-tracking. Events will still be sent to Facebook for insights. [icon:attention] Event usage cannot be controlled and is always enabled for the Facebook Canvas platform, therefore this function has no effect on Facebook Canvas.

title: facebook.enable_advertiser_tracking
text: facebook.enable_advertiser_tracking() Enable advertiser tracking This function will set AdvertiserTrackingEnabled (the 'ATE' flag) to true on iOS, to inform Audience Network to use the data to deliver personalized ads for users on iOS 14 and above.

title: facebook.enable_event_usage
text: facebook.enable_event_usage() Enable event usage with Facebook Analytics This function will enable event usage for Facebook Analytics which means that Facebook will be able to use event data for ad-tracking. [icon:attention] Event usage cannot be controlled and is always enabled for the Facebook Canvas platform, therefore this function has no effect on Facebook Canvas.

title: facebook.EVENT_ACHIEVED_LEVEL

title: facebook.EVENT_ADDED_PAYMENT_INFO

title: facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST

title: facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_REGISTRATION

title: facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_TUTORIAL
text: facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_TUTORIAL Log this event when the user has completed a tutorial in the app

title: facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT
text: facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT Log this event when the user has entered the checkout process The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the total price in the cart.

title: facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED
text: facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED Log this event when the user has completed a purchase. The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the numeric rating.

title: facebook.EVENT_RATED
text: facebook.EVENT_RATED Log this event when the user has rated an item in the app

title: facebook.EVENT_SEARCHED
text: facebook.EVENT_SEARCHED Log this event when a user has performed a search within the app

title: facebook.EVENT_SPENT_CREDITS
text: facebook.EVENT_SPENT_CREDITS Log this event when the user has spent app credits The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the number of credits spent.

title: facebook.EVENT_TIME_BETWEEN_SESSIONS
text: facebook.EVENT_TIME_BETWEEN_SESSIONS Log this event when measuring the time between user sessions

title: facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT
text: facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT Log this event when the user has unlocked an achievement in the app

title: facebook.EVENT_VIEWED_CONTENT
text: facebook.EVENT_VIEWED_CONTENT Log this event when a user has viewed a form of content in the app

text: facebook.GAMEREQUEST_ACTIONTYPE_SEND Game request action type "send" for "apprequests" dialog

title: facebook.login_with_permissions
text: facebook.login_with_permissions(permissions: table, audience: number, callback: function) Login to Facebook and request a set of publish permissions. The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions. A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the Facebook permissions documentation, as well as in their guide to best practices for login management. Log in to Facebook with a set of publish permissions Log in to Facebook with a set of read permissions permissions — table with the requested publish permission strings. audience — The audience that should be able to see the publications. Can be any of facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS facebook.AUDIENCE_EVERYONE callback — Callback function that is executed when the permission request dialog is closed.

title: facebook.login_with_tracking_preference
text: facebook.login_with_tracking_preference(login_tracking: number, permissions: table, crypto_nonce: string, callback: function) iOS ONLY. Login to Facebook and request a set of permissions. Allows developers to signal that a login is limited in terms of tracking users. The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions. A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the Facebook permissions documentation, as well as in their guide to best practices for login management. For Limited Login the list of permissions can be found in the Permissions in Limited Login documentation. Log in to Facebook with a set of publish permissions Log in to Facebook with a set of read permissions login_tracking — The tracking type for the login. Can be any of facebook.LOGIN_TRACKING_LIMITED facebook.LOGIN_TRACKING_ENABLED permissions — table with the requested publish permission strings. crypto_nonce — Nonce that the configuration was created with. A unique nonce will be used if none is provided to the factory method. callback — Callback function that is executed when the permission request dialog is closed.

title: facebook.post_event
text: facebook.post_event(event: number | string, value: number, params?: table) Post an event to Facebook Analytics This function will post an event to Facebook Analytics where it can be used in the Facebook Insights system. Post a spent credits event to Facebook Analytics event — An event can either be one of the predefined constants below or a text string which can be used to define a custom event that is registered with Facebook Analytics. facebook.EVENT_ACHIEVED_LEVEL - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_PAYMENT_INFO - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_CART - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST - facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_REGISTRATION - facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_TUTORIAL - facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT - facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED - facebook.EVENT_RATED - facebook.EVENT_SEARCHED - facebook.EVENT_SPENT_CREDITS - facebook.EVENT_TIME_BETWEEN_SESSIONS - facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT - facebook.EVENT_VIEWED_CONTENT value — A numeric value for the event. This should represent the value of the event, such as the level achieved, price for an item or number of orcs killed. params — Optional table with parameters and their values. A key in the table can either be one of the predefined constants below or a text which can be used to define a custom parameter. facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_ID - facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_TYPE - facebook.PARAM_CURRENCY - facebook.PARAM_DESCRIPTION - facebook.PARAM_LEVEL - facebook.PARAM_MAX_RATING_VALUE - facebook.PARAM_NUM_ITEMS - facebook.PARAM_PAYMENT_INFO_AVAILABLE - facebook.PARAM_REGISTRATION_METHOD - facebook.PARAM_SEARCH_STRING - facebook.PARAM_SOURCE_APPLICATION - facebook.PARAM_SUCCESS
