title: facebook.show_dialog
text: facebook.show_dialog(dialog: string, param: table, callback: function) Show facebook web dialog Display a Facebook web dialog of the type specified in the dialog parameter. The param table should be set up according to the requirements of each dialog type. Note that some parameters are mandatory. Below is the list of available dialogs and where to find Facebook's developer documentation on parameters and response data. "apprequests" Shows a Game Request dialog. Game Requests allows players to invite their friends to play a game. Available parameters [type:string] title [type:string] message [type:number] action_type [type:number] filters [type:string] data [type:string] object_id [type:table] suggestions [type:table] recipients [type:string] to On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields [type:string] request_id [type:table] to Details for each parameter "feed" The Feed Dialog allows people to publish individual stories to their timeline. [type:string] caption [type:string] description [type:string] picture [type:string] link [type:table] people_ids [type:string] place_id [type:string] ref On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields [type:string] post_id Details for each parameter "appinvite" The App Invite dialog is available only on iOS and Android. Note that the url parameter corresponds to the appLinkURL (iOS) and setAppLinkUrl (Android) properties. [type:string] url [type:string] preview_image Details for each parameter Show a dialog allowing the user to share a post to their timeline dialog — Dialog to show "apprequests" "feed" "appinvite" param — table with dialog parameters callback — Callback function that is called when the dialog is closed.

text: firebase.remoteconfig.activate() Asynchronously activates the most recently fetched configs, so that the fetched key value pairs take effect. Generates MSG_ACTIVATED or MSG_ERROR

title: firebase.remoteconfig.add_update_listener
text: firebase.remoteconfig.add_update_listener() Starts listening for real-time config updates from Remote Config. Generates MSG_CONFIG_UPDATED or MSG_ERROR. Real-time updates automatically fetch new values but do not activate them; call activate() when the updated values should take effect.

title: firebase.remoteconfig.fetch
text: firebase.remoteconfig.fetch() Fetches config data from the server. Generates MSG_FETCHED or MSG_ERROR

title: firebase.remoteconfig.fetch_and_activate
text: firebase.remoteconfig.fetch_and_activate() Asynchronously fetches and then activates the fetched configs. Generates MSG_FETCHED and MSG_ACTIVATED or MSG_ERROR

title: firebase.remoteconfig.get_string

title: fontgen.add_glyphs
text: fontgen.add_glyphs(fontc_path_hash: hash, text: string, callback: function): integer Asynchronoously sdds glyphs to the .fontc resource. fontc_path_hash — Path hash of the .fontc file in the project text — Utf-8 string containing glyphs to add to the .fontc Note No checks for duplicate glyphs is done. callback — Function to be called after the last glyph was processed. title: fontgen.unload_font
text: fontgen.unload_font(fontc_path_hash: hash) Removes the generator mapping between the .fontc and .ttf file. Decreases the ref count for both resources. Does not remove the previously generated glyphs! fontc_path_hash — Path hash of the .fontc file in the project

title: gpgs API

title: gpgs.achievement_get
text: gpgs.achievement_get() Get information about all achievement's state asynchronously. Result return to callback previously set by gpgs.set_callback with message_id == gpgs.MSG_GET_ACHIEVEMENTS. Result is an array of JSON strings. Decode each string with json.decode() to get a table containing the following fields id - achievement id (from GP console) name - achievement name description - achievement description xp - how much experience points will be added when achievement will be unlocked steps - current step of incremental achievement total_steps - total amount of steps of incremental achievement unlocked - set to true if achievement is unlocked. Otherwise field is missed. hidden - set to true if achievement is hidden. Otherwise field is missed. revealed - set to true if achievement is revealed. Otherwise field is missed.

title: gpgs.achievement_increment
text: gpgs.achievement_increment(achievementId: string, steps: number) Increments an achievement by the given number of steps. achievementId — Achievement id (from GP console) steps — The number of steps to increment by. Must be greater than 0.

title: gpgs.achievement_reveal
text: gpgs.achievement_reveal(achievementId: string) Reveals a hidden achievement to the current player. achievementId — Achievement id (from GP console)

title: gpgs.achievement_set
text: gpgs.achievement_set(achievementId: string, steps: number) Sets an achievement to have at least the given number of steps completed. achievementId — Achievement id (from GP console) steps — The number of steps to set the achievement to. Must be greater than 0.

title: gpgs.event_get
text: gpgs.event_get() Get information about all events asynchronously. Result returns to callback previously set by gpgs.set_callback with message_id == gpgs.MSG_GET_EVENTS. Result is an array of JSON strings. Decode each string with json.decode() to get a table containing the following fields id - event id formatted_value - sum of all increments have been made to this event value - the number of increments this user has made to this event description - event's description image - URI that can be used to load the event's image icon name - event's name visible - whether the event should be displayed to the user in any event related UIs

title: gpgs.snapshot_open
text: gpgs.snapshot_open(saveName: string, createIfNotFound?: boolean, conflictPolicy?: number) Opens a snapshot with the given saveName. If createIfNotFound is set to true, the specified snapshot will be created if it does not already exist. saveName — The name of the snapshot file to open. Must be between 1 and 100 non-URL-reserved characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or the symbols "-", ".", "", or ""). createIfNotFound — If true, the snapshot will be created if one cannot be found. conflictPolicy — The conflict resolution policy to use for this snapshot that can be one of the predefined constants below gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_MANUAL gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_LONGEST_PLAYTIME gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_LAST_KNOWN_GOOD gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_MOST_RECENTLY_MODIFIED gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_HIGHEST_PROGRESS Default value is gpgs.RESOLUTION_POLICY_LAST_KNOWN_GOOD

title: gpgs.snapshot_resolve_conflict
text: gpgs.snapshot_resolve_conflict(conflictId: string, snapshotId: number) Resolves a conflict using the data from the provided snapshot. conflictId — The conflict id that you want to resolve. Provided in message table with STATUS_CONFLICT message type. snapshotId — Type of the snapshot you want to use for conflict solving that can be one of the predefined constants below gpgs.SNAPSHOT_CURRENT gpgs.SNAPSHOT_CONFLICTING

title: gpgs.snapshot_set_data
text: gpgs.snapshot_set_data(data: string): LuaMultiReturn<[boolean, string]> Sets the data for the currently opened snapshot. data — The data to set. success — True if data was set for the currently opened snapshot. error_message — An error message if something goes wrong.

title: gpgs.STATUS_CONFLICT
text: gpgs.STATUS_CONFLICT The result of the calling gpgs.snapshot_open() or 'gpgs.snapshot_resolve_conflict()' is a conflict. You need to make decision on how to solve this conflict using 'gpgs.snapshot_resolve_conflict()'.

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEALLOWNULLID
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEALLOWNULLID DROPFLAGS_SOURCEALLOWNULLID Allow items such as Text(), Image() that have no unique identifier to be used as drag source, by manufacturing a temporary identifier based on their window-relative position. This is extremely unusual within the dear imgui ecosystem and so we made it explicit.

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEAUTOEXPIREPAYLOAD
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEAUTOEXPIREPAYLOAD DROPFLAGS_SOURCEAUTOEXPIREPAYLOAD Automatically expire the payload if the source cease to be submitted (otherwise payloads are persisting while being dragged)

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEEXTERN
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEEXTERN DROPFLAGS_SOURCEEXTERN External source (from outside of dear imgui), won't attempt to read current item/window info. Will always return true. Only one Extern source can be active simultaneously.

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENODISABLEHOVER
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENODISABLEHOVER DROPFLAGS_SOURCENODISABLEHOVER By default, when dragging we clear data so that IsItemHovered() will return false, to avoid subsequent user code submitting tooltips. This flag disable this behavior so you can still call IsItemHovered() on the source item.

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOHOLDTOOPENOTHERS
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOHOLDTOOPENOTHERS DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOHOLDTOOPENOTHERS Disable the behavior that allows to open tree nodes and collapsing header by holding over them while dragging a source item.

title: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOPREVIEWTOOLTIP
text: imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOPREVIEWTOOLTIP DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOPREVIEWTOOLTIP By default, a successful call to BeginDragDropSource opens a tooltip so you can display a preview or description of the source contents. This flag disable this behavior.

title: levelplay.create_banner_ad
text: levelplay.create_banner_ad(ad_unit_id: string, options?: table): number Creates a reusable banner ad view after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and all options are fixed for the view's lifetime. Create it once, then load, hide, show, and auto-refresh the same handle until it is permanently destroyed. ad_unit_id — Banner ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. options — Creation-time banner configuration. These fields apply to every load and show; changing one requires destroying the handle and creating a new banner. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

title: levelplay.create_interstitial_ad
text: levelplay.create_interstitial_ad(ad_unit_id: string, bid_floor?: number): number Creates a reusable interstitial ad object after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and optional bid floor are fixed for the object's lifetime. Create it once, then use the returned handle for multiple load/show cycles with the same ad-unit ID and creation configuration. ad_unit_id — Interstitial ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. bid_floor — Optional minimum eCPM in USD. It applies to every load by this object; changing it requires destroying the handle and creating a new object. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

title: levelplay.create_rewarded_ad
text: levelplay.create_rewarded_ad(ad_unit_id: string, bid_floor?: number): number Creates a reusable rewarded ad object after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and optional bid floor are fixed for the object's lifetime. Create it once, then use the returned handle for multiple load/show cycles with the same ad-unit ID and creation configuration. ad_unit_id — Rewarded ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. bid_floor — Optional minimum eCPM in USD. It applies to every load by this object; changing it requires destroying the handle and creating a new object. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

title: levelplay.destroy_banner_ad
text: levelplay.destroy_banner_ad(handle: number) Removes and destroys the banner view and invalidates its handle.

title: levelplay.destroy_interstitial_ad
text: levelplay.destroy_interstitial_ad(handle: number) Permanently releases an interstitial ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions or during load/display when terminal callbacks are still required.

title: levelplay.destroy_rewarded_ad
text: levelplay.destroy_rewarded_ad(handle: number) Permanently releases a rewarded ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions, and never destroy a displayed rewarded ad before its reward and close callbacks are received.

title: levelplay.set_gdpr_consent
text: levelplay.set_gdpr_consent(consent: boolean) Passes the user's GDPR consent choice to LevelPlay and supported mediated networks. It does not display a consent form or read another extension's private state. For a custom or non-compatible CMP, call it before init with the collected choice. LevelPlay SDK 7.7.0 and newer automatically reads Google UMP and compatible Google Additional Consent signals, so do not also pass the same choice with this function in that setup.

title: realtime.LOBBYTYPE_ASYNC_RANDOM_LOBBY
text: realtime.LOBBYTYPE_ASYNC_RANDOM_LOBBY This lobby does not send room lists. It is only used for Client::opJoinRandomRoom(). It keeps rooms available for matchmaking for a while even when there are only inactive users left.

title: realtime.LOBBYTYPE_DEFAULT
text: realtime.LOBBYTYPE_DEFAULT This lobby type is used unless another lobby type is specified. Room lists will be sent and Client::opJoinRandomRoom() can filter by matching properties.

title: realtime.LOBBYTYPE_SQL_LOBBY

title: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_FILL_ROOM
text: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_FILL_ROOM Fills up rooms (oldest first) to get players together as fast as possible. Default. Makes most sense with MaxPlayers > 0 and games that can only start with more players.

title: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_RANDOM_MATCHING
text: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_RANDOM_MATCHING Joins a (fully) random room. Expected properties must match, but aside from this, any available room might be selected.

title: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_SERIAL_MATCHING
text: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_SERIAL_MATCHING Distributes players across available rooms sequentially but takes filters into account. Without filters, rooms get players evenly distributed.

title: playables API
text: defold / extension-playables playables Functions for interacting with the YouTube Playables SDK.

title: playables.CONTENT_TYPE_PLAYABLE
text: playables.CONTENT_TYPE_PLAYABLE Opens another YouTube Playable.

title: playables.CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO
text: playables.CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO Opens a YouTube video.

title: playables.game_ready
text: playables.game_ready() Notifies YouTube that the loading screen is gone and the game is ready for players to interact with. The extension automatically calls firstFrameReady() during initialization.

title: playables.get_language
text: playables.get_language(callback: function) Gets the language in the player's YouTube settings as a BCP-47 language tag. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another get_language() request.

title: playables.get_sdk_version
text: playables.get_sdk_version(): string | nil Returns the loaded YouTube Playables SDK version, or nil if it is unavailable. sdk_version — The value of SDK_VERSION, or nil if the SDK or its version is unavailable.

title: playables.is_audio_enabled
text: playables.is_audio_enabled(): boolean Returns whether game audio is enabled in the player's YouTube settings. Use this to initialize the game audio state. is_audio_enabled — True when game audio is enabled.

title: playables.is_in_playables_env
text: playables.is_in_playables_env(): boolean Returns whether the SDK reports that the game is running in the Playables environment. Returns false if the SDK is not loaded. in_playables_env — True when the SDK is loaded and IN_PLAYABLES_ENV is true, otherwise false.

title: playables.load_data
text: playables.load_data(callback: function) Loads serialized game data from YouTube. Only one load request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another load_data() request.

title: playables.log_error
text: playables.log_error() Reports an error occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.

title: playables.log_warning
text: playables.log_warning() Reports a warning occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.

title: playables.on_audio_enabled_change
text: playables.on_audio_enabled_change(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube audio-setting changes. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically mutes the master sound group when audio is disabled, or unmutes it when audio is enabled and the game is not paused. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

title: playables.on_pause
text: playables.on_pause(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube pause events. The extension automatically mutes the master sound group before the callback runs. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. A paused game is not guaranteed to resume. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

title: playables.on_resume
text: playables.on_resume(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube resume events. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically unmutes the master sound group if YouTube audio is enabled, or keeps it muted if audio is disabled. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

title: playables.open_yt_content
text: playables.open_yt_content(content_id: string, content_type: number | undefined, callback: function) Requests that YouTube open a video or another Playable. The content type is optional and defaults to CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another open_yt_content() request. content_id — The YouTube video or Playable ID. content_type — CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO or CONTENT_TYPE_PLAYABLE.

title: playables.request_interstitial_ad
text: playables.request_interstitial_ad(callback: function) Requests an interstitial ad. Success does not guarantee that an ad was shown. Do not use this API to grant rewards. Only one interstitial request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_interstitial_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads.

title: playables.request_rewarded_ad
text: playables.request_rewarded_ad(reward_id: string, callback: function) Requests a rewarded ad. Grant a reward only when reward_earned is true. Only one rewarded request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_rewarded_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads. reward_id — A stable ID unique to the reward type. Reuse it for each offer of that reward and do not include user data.

title: playables.save_data
text: playables.save_data(data: string, callback: function) Saves valid UTF-8 text to YouTube, with a maximum size of 3 MiB. Invalid UTF-8 returns false and an error through the callback before the SDK is called. Base64-encode binary data such as sys.serialize() output before saving. Only one save request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another save_data() request. data — The serialized game data as valid UTF-8 text. Embedded zero bytes are supported.

title: playables.send_score
text: playables.send_score(score: number, callback: function) Sends an integer score to YouTube. Use one consistent score dimension across the game. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another send_score() request. score — An integer no greater than JavaScript's maximum safe integer.

title: poki_sdk.measure
text: poki_sdk.measure(category: string, what?: string | nil, action?: string | nil) Sends a custom analytics event to Poki. Use start/complete/fail for progress, visible/interact for offer and UI engagement, or a custom action for other events. Do not duplicate commercial or rewarded ad playback and outcomes; Poki tracks those through the ad calls. The binding defaults omitted what and action to empty strings for compatibility. what — Optional event subject. Defaults to an empty string when omitted. action — Optional event action. Defaults to an empty string when omitted.

title: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_ERROR
text: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_ERROR A rewarded break failed or the reward should not be granted.

title: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_START
text: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_START A rewarded break started.

title: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_SUCCESS
text: poki_sdk.REWARDED_BREAK_SUCCESS A rewarded break completed and the reward may be granted.

title: push API
text: defold / extension-push push Functions and constants for interacting with local, as well as Apple''s and Google''s push notification services. These API's only exist on mobile platforms. [icon:ios] [icon:android]

title: push.cancel_all_issued
text: push.cancel_all_issued() Use this function to cancel a previously issued local push notifications.

title: push.cancel
text: push.cancel(id: number) Use this function to cancel a previously scheduled local push notification. The notification is identified by a numeric id as returned by push.schedule(). id — The numeric id of the local push notification

title: push.get_all_scheduled
text: push.get_all_scheduled(): table Returns a table with all data associated with all scheduled local push notifications. The table contains key, value pairs where the key is the push notification id and the value is a table with the notification data, corresponding to the data given by push.get_scheduled(id). Table with all data associated with all scheduled notifications.

title: push.get_scheduled
text: push.get_scheduled(id: number): table Returns a table with all data associated with a specified local push notification. The notification is identified by a numeric id as returned by push.schedule(). id — The numeric id of the local push notification. Table with all data associated with the notification.

title: push.NOTIFICATION_ALERT
text: push.NOTIFICATION_ALERT Alert notification type.

title: push.NOTIFICATION_BADGE
text: push.NOTIFICATION_BADGE Badge notification type.

title: push.NOTIFICATION_SOUND
text: push.NOTIFICATION_SOUND Sound notification type.

title: push.ORIGIN_LOCAL
text: push.ORIGIN_LOCAL Local push origin.

title: push.ORIGIN_REMOTE
text: push.ORIGIN_REMOTE Remote push origin.

title: push.PRIORITY_DEFAULT
text: push.PRIORITY_DEFAULT The default notification priority. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

title: push.PRIORITY_HIGH
text: push.PRIORITY_HIGH Priority for more important notifications or alerts. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

title: push.PRIORITY_LOW
text: push.PRIORITY_LOW Priority for items that are less important. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

title: push.PRIORITY_MAX
text: push.PRIORITY_MAX Set this priority for your application's most important items that require the user's prompt attention or input. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

title: push.PRIORITY_MIN
text: push.PRIORITY_MIN This priority is for items might not be shown to the user except under special circumstances, such as detailed notification logs. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

title: push.register
text: push.register(notifications: table, callback: function) Send a request for push notifications. Note that the notifications table parameter is iOS only and will be ignored on Android. Register for push notifications on iOS. Note that the token needs to be converted on this platform. Register for push notifications on Android. notifications — The types of notifications to listen to. [icon:ios] callback — Register callback function.

title: push.schedule
text: push.schedule(time: number, title: string, alert: string, payload: string, notification_settings: table): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Local push notifications are scheduled with this function. The returned id value is uniquely identifying the scheduled notification and can be stored for later reference. This example demonstrates how to schedule a local notification: time — Number of seconds into the future until the notification should be triggered. title — Localized title to be displayed to the user if the application is not running. alert — Localized body message of the notification to be displayed to the user if the application is not running. payload — JSON string to be passed to the registered listener function. notification_settings — Table with notification and platform specific fields Unique id that can be used to cancel or inspect the notification Error string if something went wrong, otherwise nil

title: push.set_badge_count
text: push.set_badge_count(count: number) Set the badge count for application icon. This function is only available on iOS. [icon:ios] count — Badge count

title: push.set_listener
text: push.set_listener(listener: function) Sets a listener function to listen to push notifications. Set the push notification listener. listener — Listener callback function.

title: gui.add_spine_skin

title: gui.cancel_spine
text: gui.cancel_spine(node: node, options: table) cancel a spine animation node — spine node that should cancel its animation options — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged.

title: gui.clear_spine_skin

text: gui.copy_spine_skin(node: node, spine_skin_a: string | hash, spine_skin_b: string | hash) Copy a spine skin on a spine node to another skin on the same node. text: gui.get_spine_animation(node: node, options: table): hash Gets the playing animation on a spine node node — node to get spine animation from options — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged. id — spine animation id, 0 if no animation is playing

title: gui.get_spine_bone
text: gui.get_spine_bone(node: node, bone_id: string | hash): node The returned node can be used for parenting and transform queries. title: gui.get_spine_playback_rate
text: gui.get_spine_playback_rate(node: node, options: table): number This is only useful for spine nodes. Gets the playback rate of the animation on a spine node. node — spine node to get the playback rate for options — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged. rate — playback rate

title: gui.get_spine_scene
text: gui.get_spine_scene(node: node): hash Returns the spine scene id of the supplied node. This is currently only useful for spine nodes. The returned spine scene must be mapped to the gui scene in the gui editor. node — node to get texture from spine_scene — spine scene id

title: gui.get_spine_skin
text: gui.get_spine_skin(node: node): hash Gets the spine skin of a spine node node — node to get spine skin from id — spine skin id, 0 if no explicit skin is set

text: gui.new_spine_node(pos: vector3 | vector4, spine_scene: string | hash): node Dynamically create a new spine node. pos — node position spine_scene — spine scene id node — new spine node

title: gui.play_spine_anim
text: gui.play_spine_anim(node: node, animation_id: string | hash, playback: constant, play_properties: table, callback_function: function(self, node, message_id, message)) Starts a spine animation. node — spine node that should play the animation animation_id — id of the animation to play playback — playback mode - gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_FORWARD - gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_BACKWARD - gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_PINGPONG - gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_FORWARD - gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_BACKWARD - gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_PINGPONG play_properties — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged. callback_function — function to call when the animation has completed or when spine events occur. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged.

title: gui.reset_spine_ik_target
text: gui.reset_spine_ik_target(node: node, ik_constraint_id: string | hash) Resets any previously set IK target of a Spine GUI node, the position will be reset to the original position from the spine scene. The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". A player no longer has an item in hand, that previously was controlled through IK, let's reset the IK of the right hand. node — the Spine GUI node containing the object ik_constraint_id — id of the corresponding IK constraint object

title: gui.set_spine_attachment
text: gui.set_spine_attachment(node: node, slot: string | hash, attachment: string | hash) This is only useful for spine nodes. Sets an attachment to a slot on a spine node. node — spine node to set the slot for slot — slot name attachment — attachment name. May be nil.

title: gui.set_spine_cursor
text: gui.set_spine_cursor(node: node, cursor: number, options: table) This is only useful for spine nodes. The cursor is normalized. node — spine node to set the cursor for cursor — cursor value options — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged.

title: gui.set_spine_ik_target_position
text: gui.set_spine_ik_target_position(node: node, ik_constraint_id: string | hash, position: vector3) Sets a static (vector3) target position of an inverse kinematic (IK) object. The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". How to set the target IK position of the right_hand_constraint constraint object of the player object node — the Spine GUI node containing the object ik_constraint_id — id of the corresponding IK constraint object position — target position

title: gui.set_spine_ik_target
text: gui.set_spine_ik_target(node: node, ik_constraint_id: string | hash, target_node: node) Sets a GUI node as target position of an inverse kinematic (IK) object. As the target GUI node's position is updated, the constraint object is updated with the new position. The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". How to set the target IK position of the right_hand_constraint constraint object to follow the position of GUI node with id "target_node" node — the Spine GUI node containing the object ik_constraint_id — id of the corresponding IK constraint object target_node — target GUI node

title: gui.set_spine_playback_rate
text: gui.set_spine_playback_rate(node: node, playback_rate: number, options: table) This is only useful for spine nodes. Sets the playback rate of the animation on a spine node. Must be positive. node — spine node to set the playback rate for playback_rate — playback rate options — optional table with properties. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine.gui unchanged.

title: spine.resource API
text: defold / extension-spine · resource resource Functions for creating Spine resources dynamically

title: resource.create_spinescene
text: resource.create_spinescene(path: string, options: table): hash Creates a spinescene resource (.spinescenec) from runtime data. Creates a Spine scene resource dynamically at runtime. This allows loading Spine animations from data rather than pre-built assets. The atlas path must reference a compiled .texturesetc resource. The created spinescene is tracked for cleanup when the collection unloads; internal intermediate JSON is removed automatically. path — The target resource path. Must end with .spinescenec options — Table with fields path_hash — canonical path hash of the created resource

text: spine.physics_translate(url: string | hash | url, translation: vector3) Apply a physics-based translation to the Spine model. url — The Spine model component to translate. translation — The translation vector to apply to the Spine model.

title: spine.play_anim
text: spine.play_anim(url: string | hash | url, anim_id: string | hash, playback: number, options: table | nil, callback_function: function) Plays the specified animation on a Spine model. A [ref:spine_animation_done] message is sent to the callback (or message handler). Any spine events will also be handled in the same way. [icon:attention] The callback is not called (or message sent) if the animation is cancelled with [ref:spine.cancel]. The callback is called (or message sent) only for animations that play with the following playback modes go.PLAYBACK_ONCE_FORWARD go.PLAYBACK_ONCE_BACKWARD go.PLAYBACK_ONCE_PINGPONG url — The Spine model for which to play an animation anim_id — Id of the animation to play playback — Playback mode of the animation (from go.PLAYBACK) options — Playback options. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine unchanged. callback_function — function to call when the animation has completed or a Spine event occurred. ⚠️ track is 1-based; passed to spine unchanged.

title: steam.matchmaking_get_lobby_owner
text: steam.matchmaking_get_lobby_owner(lobby_id: string): string Returns the current lobby owner. There always one lobby owner - if the current owner leaves, another user in the lobby will become the owner automatically. It is possible (but rare) to join a lobby just as the owner is leaving, thus entering a lobby with self as the owner. You must be a member of the lobby to access this. lobby_id — The Steam ID of the lobby to get the owner of. id — Id of owner

Persona information for other lobby members (name, avatar, etc.) is automatically received and accessible via the ISteamFriends interface. The current user must be in the lobby to retrieve the Steam IDs of other users in that lobby. lobby_id — The Steam ID of the lobby to get the owner of. count — Number of users in the lobby

title: steam.user_stats_download_leaderboard_entries
text: steam.user_stats_download_leaderboard_entries(leaderboard: string, request: ELeaderboardDataRequest, start: number, end: number) Asks the Steam back-end for a set of rows in the leaderboard. This call is asynchronous, with the result returned in a listener callback with event set to LeaderboardScoresDownloaded_t. LeaderboardScoresDownloaded_t will contain a handle to pull the results from GetDownloadedLeaderboardEntries(). You can ask for more entries than exist, and it will return as many as do exist. k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobal requests rows in the leaderboard from the full table, with nRangeStart & nRangeEnd in the range [1, TotalEntries] k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobalAroundUser requests rows around the current user, nRangeStart being negate e.g. DownloadLeaderboardEntries( hLeaderboard, k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobalAroundUser, -3, 3 ) will return 7 rows, 3 before the user, 3 after k_ELeaderboardDataRequestFriends requests all the rows for friends of the current user https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamUserStats#DownloadLeaderboardEntries

title: steam.user_stats_store_stats
text: steam.user_stats_store_stats(): boolean Store the current data on the server. Will get a callback when set and one callback for every new achievement If the callback has a result of k_EResultInvalidParam, one or more stats uploaded has been rejected, either because they broke constraints or were out of date. In this case the server sends back updated values. The stats should be re-iterated to keep in sync. https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamUserStats#StoreStats

title: mpeg API
text: defold / extension-videoplayer-mpeg mpeg Functions to play MPEG1 videos

title: mpeg.close
text: mpeg.close(handle: number) Close an opened video. This will release an memory allocated by the videoplayer. handle — The video handle to close.

title: mpeg.decode
text: mpeg.decode(handle: number, seconds: number) Advance the internal timer by seconds and decode video/audio up to this time. handle — The video handle to decode. seconds — Number of seconds to advance.

title: mpeg.get_frame
text: mpeg.get_frame(handle: number): buffer Get the video frame buffer. The video frame buffer will be updated when decode() is called and enough data has been decoded to produce a frame. handle — The video handle to get frame buffer for. frame — The decoded video frame buffer or nil if no video frame buffer is available. The ownership of the buffer is not transferred to the caller.

title: mpeg.get_info
text: mpeg.get_info(handle: number): table Get information about an opened video. handle — The video to get info for. info — Video information

title: mpeg.open
text: mpeg.open(video: buffer | string): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Open a video for decoding. video — The video data as a buffer or string. Ownership of the buffer is not transferred. handle — Returns video handle. Use in subsequent calls. err — Error message if video failed to open.

title: mpeg.rewind
text: mpeg.rewind(handle: number) Rewind video to the beginning. handle — The video handle to rewind.

title: mpeg.seek
text: mpeg.seek(handle: number, time: number, seek_exact: boolean) Seek to the specified time. Will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. handle — The video handle to seek on. time — Time to seek to. seek_exact — If value is true the function will seek to the exact time, otherwise it will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. Exact seeking can be slow, because all frames up to the seeked one have to be decoded on top of the previous intra frame. Defaults to false.

title: mpeg.write
text: mpeg.write(handle: number, data: string): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Write data to the internal stream buffer of a video started with stream(). Use the streaming_buffer_bytes_remaining and streaming_buffer_capacity to determine how much data to write to the buffer. handle — The video handle to write to. data — Bytes with stream data. bytes_written — The number of written bytes or nil if writing failed. error — Error message if writing failed for some reason.

Calling this function with auto_finish_transactions set will be ignored and a warning is printed. The transaction.state field must equal iapc.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED. transaction — transaction table parameter as supplied in listener callback

title: iapc.list

title: defarmy API
text: dev-masih / defarmy defarmy Groups game objects (soldiers) into armies, places them in a built-in or customized pattern, and moves and rotates each army as a group. Create an army with army_create and a soldier for each game object with soldier_create, then call soldier_move from each soldier's update and apply the position and rotation it returns.

title: defarmy.army_create
text: army_create(army_center_position: Vector3, army_initial_rotation: Quaternion, member_padding: number, is_sticky: boolean, army_pattern: Hash, pattern_func?: PatternFunc): number Creates a group of game objects (an army) with the given member padding and pattern, and returns its id. PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED requires pattern_func, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. Any value outside PATTERN fails an assert. army_center_position — The army's center position. army_initial_rotation — The army's initial rotation. member_padding — The distance between members. is_sticky — Whether members are glued to their places in the army, rather than following them. It shows most while the army rotates. army_pattern — One of PATTERN. pattern_func — Builds the rows for PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED.

title: defarmy.army_debug_draw
text: army_debug_draw(army_id: number, debug_color: Vector4) Draws an army's center and facing for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:. Call it every frame to keep it shown. army_id — The army's id. debug_color — The color of the lines.

title: defarmy.army_members
text: army_members(army_id: number): number[] Returns the ids of the soldiers in an army. The list is the army's own, so editing it edits the army. army_id — The army's id.

title: defarmy.army_remove
text: army_remove(army_id: number) Removes an army and releases its members, which stay as soldiers in no army. army_id — The army's id.

title: defarmy.army_update_pattern
text: army_update_pattern(army_id: number, army_pattern: Hash, pattern_func?: PatternFunc) Changes an army's pattern and rearranges its members at once. PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED requires pattern_func, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. army_id — The army's id. army_pattern — One of PATTERN. pattern_func — Builds the rows for PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED.

title: defarmy.army_update_position
text: army_update_position(army_id: number, army_center_position: Vector3) Moves an army's center. army_id — The army's id. army_center_position — The new center position.

title: defarmy.army_update_rotation
text: army_update_rotation(army_id: number, army_rotation: Quaternion) Rotates an army. army_id — The army's id. army_rotation — The new rotation.

title: defarmy.army_update_stickiness
text: army_update_stickiness(army_id: number, is_sticky: boolean) Changes whether an army's members are glued to their places in it. army_id — The army's id. is_sticky — Whether members are glued to their places, rather than following them.

title: defarmy.PATTERN
text: PATTERN: { BOTTOM_TO_TOP_SQUARE: Hash; TOP_TO_BOTTOM_SQUARE: Hash; TRIANGLE: Hash; RHOMBUS_TALL: Hash; RHOMBUS_SHORT: Hash; CUSTOMIZED: Hash; } The army patterns army_create and army_update_pattern take. The five named patterns place the soldiers in built-in shapes. CUSTOMIZED takes its rows from the pattern_func passed beside it.

title: defarmy.soldier_create
text: soldier_create(position: Vector3, initial_direction: Vector3, army_id?: number): number Creates a soldier and returns its id, joining it to an army when army_id is given. position — The soldier's current position. initial_direction — The direction the soldier's game object faces at zero rotation. Every rotation soldier_move returns is relative to it. army_id — The army to join.

title: defarmy.soldier_debug_off
text: soldier_debug_off(soldier_id: number) Turns off a soldier's debug marks. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

title: defarmy.soldier_debug_on
text: soldier_debug_on(soldier_id: number, debug_color: Vector4) Turns on a soldier's debug marks: each soldier_move call then posts draw_line to @render: to mark the position the soldier is heading for with a cross. soldier_id — The soldier's id. debug_color — The color of the marks.

title: defarmy.soldier_join_army
text: soldier_join_army(soldier_id: number, army_id: number) Moves a soldier into an army, out of the army it was in. soldier_id — The soldier's id. army_id — The army's id.

title: defarmy.soldier_leave_army
text: soldier_leave_army(soldier_id: number) Takes a soldier out of its army and rearranges the members left. A soldier in no army is left as it is. At v1 the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier was the army's last member, so call army_remove instead in that case. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

title: defarmy.soldier_move
text: soldier_move(soldier_id: number, current_position: Vector3, speed: number, threshold?: number): LuaMultiReturn<[ Vector3, Quaternion ] | [ undefined, undefined ]> Calculates a soldier's next position and rotation, moving it toward its place in its army. A soldier in no army keeps current_position. Returns undefined for both values once the soldier is removed: const [position, rotation] = defarmy.soldier_move(id, go.get_position(), speed). soldier_id — The soldier's id. current_position — The soldier's current position. speed — How far the soldier moves this call. threshold — The distance from its place within which the soldier counts as placed. Defaults to 1.

title: defarmy.soldier_remove
text: soldier_remove(soldier_id: number) Removes a soldier completely, rearranging the army it was in. soldier_move then returns undefined for both values. At v1 the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier was the army's last member, so call army_remove first in that case. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

title: defarmy.PatternFunc
text: PatternFunc type PatternFunc = (total_count: number) => number[]

title: defgraph API
text: dev-masih / defgraph defgraph Builds a world map as a graph of nodes and routes that can change at any time, draws it for debugging, and moves game objects along it with a built-in pathfinder. Add nodes with map_add_node and join them with map_add_route, start each game object with move_initialize, then call move_player from its update and apply the position and rotation it returns. MoveData MoveResult

title: defgraph.debug_draw_map_nodes
text: debug_draw_map_nodes(is_show_ids?: boolean) Draws every node for one frame, by posting draw_line and, for the ids, draw_text to @render:. A node with no route is drawn as a triangle, a dead end as a cross and an intersection as a square. Call it every frame to keep it shown. is_show_ids — Whether to draw each node's id beside it. Defaults to false.

title: defgraph.debug_draw_map_routes
text: debug_draw_map_routes() Draws every route for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:: two-way routes in one color, and one-way routes in another with a square near the end they run to. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

title: defgraph.debug_draw_player_move
text: debug_draw_player_move(movement_data: MoveData, color: Vector4, is_show_intersection?: boolean) Draws the rest of a game object's path for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:. Nothing is drawn while the game object stands still for want of a route. Call it every frame to keep it shown. movement_data — The movement data from move_initialize or move_player. color — The color of the path. is_show_intersection — Whether to mark each point on the path with a cross. Defaults to false.

title: defgraph.debug_set_properties
text: debug_set_properties(node_color?: Vector4, two_way_route_color?: Vector4, one_way_route_color?: Vector4, draw_scale?: number) Sets the colors and the scale the debug_draw functions draw with. A nil keeps a value's current setting, and each starts at the default stated on it. node_color — The color of the nodes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(1, 0, 1, 1). two_way_route_color — The color of two-way routes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(0, 1, 0, 1). one_way_route_color — The color of one-way routes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(0, 1, 1, 1). draw_scale — The size of the node marks. Defaults to 5.

title: defgraph.map_add_node
text: map_add_node(position: Vector3): number Adds a node at a position and returns its id. The position's z is ignored. A node with no route takes no part in routing, so remove one that is no longer used. position — The node's position.

title: defgraph.map_add_route
text: map_add_route(source_id: number, destination_id: number, is_one_way?: boolean) Adds a route between two nodes, both ways unless is_one_way is true. A route from a node to itself is ignored, and an unknown id fails an assert. A one-way route is a little cheaper to path through when the other way is never needed. source_id — The node the route starts at. destination_id — The node the route ends at. is_one_way — Whether the route runs from source_id to destination_id only. Defaults to false.

title: defgraph.map_remove_node
text: map_remove_node(node_id: number) Removes a node and every route attached to it. An unknown id fails an assert. node_id — The node's id.

title: defgraph.map_remove_route
text: map_remove_route(source_id: number, destination_id: number, is_remove_one_way?: boolean) Removes the route between two nodes, both ways unless is_remove_one_way is true. An unknown id fails an assert. source_id — The node the route starts at. destination_id — The node the route ends at. is_remove_one_way — Whether to remove only the way from source_id to destination_id. Defaults to false.

title: defgraph.map_set_properties
text: map_set_properties(settings_gameobject_threshold?: number, settings_path_curve_tightness?: number, settings_path_curve_roundness?: number, settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner?: number, settings_allow_enter_on_route?: boolean) Sets the module's path and movement settings, which every move_initialize call falls back to for a setting it is not given. A nil keeps a setting's current value, and each starts at the default stated on it. settings_gameobject_threshold — The distance within which a game object counts as on a route or at a point. Use a larger value for faster game objects; the smallest useful value is 1. Defaults to 1. settings_path_curve_tightness — How tight a turn on the path is; the smallest useful value is 2. Defaults to 4. settings_path_curve_roundness — How round a turn on the path is. 0 gives no curves and ignores the tightness and the corner distance, and a higher value costs more processing, most of all while nodes move. Defaults to 3. settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner — The farthest from its corner a turn may start. Defaults to 10. settings_allow_enter_on_route — Whether a game object may enter the map partway along a route, rather than only at a node. Defaults to true.

title: defgraph.map_update_node_position
text: map_update_node_position(node_id: number, position: Vector3) Moves an existing node, and the routes attached to it with it. An unknown id fails an assert. node_id — The node's id. position — The node's new position.

title: defgraph.move_initialize
text: move_initialize(source_position: Vector3, destination_list: number[], route_type?: Hash, initial_face_vector?: Vector3, settings_gameobject_threshold?: number, settings_path_curve_tightness?: number, settings_path_curve_roundness?: number, settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner?: number, settings_allow_enter_on_route?: boolean): MoveData Starts a game object moving from its position through a list of destination nodes, and returns the movement data move_player takes. Each setting it is not given falls back to the value map_set_properties set. To change the destinations, call it again and replace the old movement data with the result. source_position — The game object's current position. destination_list — The destination node ids, in order. With an empty list the game object stands still and move_player reports no destination_id. route_type — One of ROUTETYPE. Defaults to ROUTETYPE.ONETIME. initial_face_vector — The direction the game object faces at zero rotation. Without it, move_player returns no rotation. settings_gameobject_threshold — The distance within which the game object counts as on a route or at a point. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_tightness — How tight a turn on the path is. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_roundness — How round a turn on the path is, 0 for no curves. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner — The farthest from its corner a turn may start. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_allow_enter_on_route — Whether the game object may enter the map partway along a route. Defaults to the map_set_properties value.

title: defgraph.move_player
text: move_player(current_position: Vector3, speed: number, move_data: MoveData): LuaMultiReturn<[ MoveData, MoveResult ]> Moves a game object one step along its path toward its current destination, and returns the movement data and the result of the move: const [data, result] = defgraph.move_player(go.get_position(), speed dt, move). Keep the returned movement data in place of the one passed in. When the map has changed since the last call, the path is found again first. result.rotation is undefined unless move_initialize was given an initial_face_vector. current_position — The game object's current position. speed — How far the game object moves this call, its speed already multiplied by dt. move_data — The movement data from move_initialize or the last move_player.

title: defgraph.MoveData.destination_index
text: destination_index: number The 1-based index of the current destination in destination_list. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to defgraph unchanged.

title: defgraph.MoveData.destination_list
text: destination_list: number[] The destination node ids, the same list move_initialize was given.

title: defgraph.MoveData.path_index
text: path_index: number The 1-based index of the next point on the path, or 0 while the game object stands still because the map has no route or destination_list is empty. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to defgraph unchanged.

title: defgraph.MoveData.route_type
text: route_type: Hash The ROUTETYPE the game object moves by.

title: defgraph.MoveResult.destination_id
text: destination_id: number The node id of the current destination.

title: defgraph.MoveResult.is_reached
text: is_reached: boolean Whether the game object is at its destination. With more than one destination it reads true on reaching each one, then false again while destination_id moves on to the next.

title: defgraph.MoveResult.position
text: position: Vector3 The game object's next position.

title: defgraph.MoveResult.rotation
text: rotation: Quaternion | undefined The game object's next rotation around z, relative to the initial_face_vector passed to move_initialize. undefined when move_initialize was given none.

title: defgraph.ROUTETYPE
text: ROUTETYPE: { ONETIME: Hash; SHUFFLE: Hash; CYCLE: Hash; } How move_initialize takes a game object through more than one destination. ONETIME visits them in order and stops at the last, SHUFFLE visits them in random order without stopping, and CYCLE visits them in order and starts over after the last. With one destination they all behave the same.

title: light_and_shadows.constants API
text: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · constants light_and_shadows.constants The light options the render script forwards into shader uniform constants. Scripts such as light_setting.script and sun.script write them, and light.update and the render script read them every frame. Vector fields are mutated in place (constants.fog.x = 20); assigning a new value to a field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only. LightEntry

title: light_and_shadows.constants.ambient
text: ambient: Vector4 The ambient color, added after every light source is blended. w is the maximum value of each final color component.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.cam_look_at_position
text: cam_look_at_position: Vector3 The point the camera looks at, the center of the shadow projection. light.update copies it from light.cam_look_at.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.cam_position
text: cam_position: Vector4 The camera world position, which the shader uses for specular light. light.update copies it from light.cam_position.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.cam_z
text: cam_z: number The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point. light.update copies it from light.cam_z.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.clear_color
text: clear_color: Vector4 The color that clears the default render target, which is the background color. RGB in 0..1.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.far_z
text: far_z: number The camera far Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera is true.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.focus_range
text: focus_range: number How wide the depth-of-field focus zone is. light_and_shadows.dof sets it from focus_range.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.fog_color
text: fog_color: Vector4 The fog color, usually the clear color. w is the fog density from 0 to 1, where 0 is the densest.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.fog
text: fog: Vector4 The minimum and maximum Z in camera view space between which the fog starts and ends, in x and y.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.color
text: color: Vector4 The color. w is the power after distance attenuation.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.direction
text: direction?: Vector4 The spotlight direction; w above 0 turns the spotlight on. light_and_shadows.update sends a zero vector when it is absent.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.distance
text: distance: number The squared distance from the point the camera looks at.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.position
text: position: Vector4 The world position. w carries the spotlight smoothness.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.power
text: power: number The power before distance attenuation.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.lights
text: lights: LightEntry[] The light sources, their world positions and colors. Only the first light_and_shadows.max_lights reach the shader; missing ones are sent as zero vectors.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.near_z
text: near_z: number The camera near Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera is true.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.shadow_color
text: shadow_color: Vector4 The inverted shadow color, subtracted where shadows fall. light_and_shadows.update sets w to 1 when light_and_shadows.shadow is on and 0 when it is off.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.sun_color
text: sun_color: Vector4 The sun color.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.sun_dir
text: sun_dir: Vector3 The sun direction, used for shadow casting with a perspective projection.

title: light_and_shadows.constants.sun_position
text: sun_position: Vector4 The sun position, the one light source that casts shadows.

title: light_and_shadows.light API
text: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · light light_and_shadows.light The light sources manager. It keeps the list of point light sources and the camera position, and each frame writes the sorted sources and the camera values into light_and_shadows.constants. light_setting.script calls set_color and update, and a scene controller calls set_position as its camera moves. Assigning a new value to a field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only. LightSource

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows API
text: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · light_and_shadows light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows Real-time shadows from one light source, the sun, and many point light sources, wired into a render script. Call init(self) from the render script's init, update(self) from its update, and draw_upscaled(self) after drawing the world when a post effect is on (see light_and_shadows/render/default.render_script, the lines marked -- L_S Injection). The settings fields are read every frame. Vector fields are mutated in place; assigning a new value to any other field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only: (light_and_shadows as { fxaa: boolean }).fxaa = true. SizedRenderTarget DofOptions

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.blur_power
text: blur_power: number How strong the blur is, 1 to 10. The default is 2.5.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.blur_resolution
text: blur_resolution: number How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed. The default is 2.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.blur
text: blur: boolean Whether the game scene is blurred, so an unblurred GUI can be drawn on top. It uses the same render target as upscaling. The default is false.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.depth_bias
text: depth_bias: number The shadow depth bias. Too high a bias detaches shadows from their objects; too low a bias causes shadow acne. The default is 0.0004.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.discard_threshold
text: discard_threshold: number The alpha below which the sprite shader discards semitransparent pixels. The default is 0.5.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.dof
text: dof(enable: boolean, options?: DofOptions) Turns depth of field on or off. enable — true turns depth of field on. options — The depth-of-field options. Omitted, every setting keeps its value.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.DofOptions.blur_power
text: blur_power?: number How strong the blur effect is, 2 to 10. Omitted, blur_power keeps its value.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.DofOptions.blur_resolution
text: blur_resolution: number How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed; 1 to 2 is enough. dof copies it with no fallback, so it is required: an options table without it leaves blur_resolution nil and the next update fails.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.DofOptions.focus_range
text: focus_range?: number How wide the focus zone is, 0.1 to 4. Omitted, focus_range in light_and_shadows.constants keeps its value.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.DofOptions.upscale
text: upscale?: boolean Whether to upscale the main render target. dof sets upscale to false when it is omitted.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.draw_upscaled
text: draw_upscaled(self: object) Blurs the main render target when depth of field or blur is on, then draws it to the screen, with FXAA when fxaa is on. Call it after the world is drawn to the main render target. The render script's self.predicates must carry upscale. self — The render script instance.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.focus
text: focus: Vector4 The depth-of-field focus position, in z.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.fxaa
text: fxaa: boolean Whether FXAA anti-aliasing is applied to the final image. The default is false.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera
text: get_far_near_z_from_camera: boolean Whether the reference render script reads the near and far Z planes from the camera component into light_and_shadows.constants. Set it to false to set near_z and far_z by hand. The default is true.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.init
text: init(self: object) Sets up the shadow map, the orthographic shadow projection and the render constants on the render script. Call it from the render script's init. self — The render script instance.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.max_lights
text: max_lights: number How many point light sources the shader processes at once, at most 16. The default is 8.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.mix
text: mix: boolean Whether depth of field is on. dof sets it. The default is false.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.polygon_offset
text: polygon_offset: { factor: number; units: number; } The polygon offset applied while drawing the shadow map. Raise it to reduce shadow acne; lower it if shadows detach from their casters.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.render_shadows
text: render_shadows(self: object) Draws every object tagged shadow into the shadow map. update calls it while shadow is on. The render script's self.predicates must carry shadow, shadow_local, shadow_instanced, shadow_instanced_billboard, shadow_instanced_textured, shadow_skinned_instanced and shadow_skinned. self — The render script instance.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.render_target
text: render_target(name: string, w: number, h: number, no_depth?: boolean): SizedRenderTarget Returns the render target named name, creating it with a color buffer and, unless no_depth is set, a depth texture. A target that exists at another size is resized. name — The render target name, also its key in rt_list. w — The width in pixels. h — The height in pixels. no_depth — true creates the target without a depth buffer.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.rt_list
text: rt_list: LuaTable<string, SizedRenderTarget> Every render target render_target created, keyed by name.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.set_orthographic_projection
text: set_orthographic_projection(proj_w: number, proj_h: number, near_z?: number, far_z?: number) Sets an orthographic shadow projection, used for directional light. init sets one. proj_w — The width of the area the shadow is projected on. proj_h — The height of the area the shadow is projected on. near_z — The near clipping plane. The default is -500. far_z — The far clipping plane. The default is 500.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.set_perspective_projection

Experimental. fov — The field of view in radians. The default is 3.14 / 1.5. aspect — The aspect ratio. The default is 1. near_z — The near clipping plane. The default is 50. far_z — The far clipping plane. The default is 500.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.shadow
text: shadow: boolean Whether the sun casts shadows. The default is true.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.update_light
text: update_light(self: object) Writes the sun, the point light sources, the ambient and fog values and the camera values from light_and_shadows.constants into the render constants. update calls it. self — The render script instance.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.upscale
text: upscale: boolean Whether the main render target is upscaled. When on, every object is first rendered to a render target no larger than the project settings size, which is then placed on the screen with linear scaling. Add light_and_shadows/props/render_target_quad.go to the main scene to use it. The default is false.

title: light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.zoom
text: zoom: number The zoom update computed for upscaling, 1 when upscale is off.

title: light_and_shadows.light.attenuation_coefficient
text: attenuation_coefficient: number Divides a source's squared distance from the camera focus point before it scales the source's power.

title: light_and_shadows.light.cam_look_at
text: cam_look_at: Vector3 The point the camera looks at, set by set_position. Light sources are sorted by their distance from it.

title: light_and_shadows.light.cam_position
text: cam_position: Vector3 The camera world position, set by set_position.

title: light_and_shadows.light.cam_view
text: cam_view: Quaternion The camera rotation, set by set_position. A source with rotate set turns to it.

title: light_and_shadows.light.cam_z
text: cam_z: number The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point that depth of field needs. Set it here or with set_position's cam_z.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.current_value
text: current_value?: Vector4 The color sent to the shader, its w attenuated by distance. update creates it from nothing when it is absent.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.direction
text: direction: Vector4 The spotlight direction. w is the cone angle in radians; 0 or less turns the spotlight off.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.id
text: id?: Hash The game object id, as bulb.script stores it.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.num
text: num: number A positive number keeps the source out of the distance sort and always visible; the default is -1.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.position
text: position: Vector4 The world position. w carries the spotlight smoothness, from 0 (soft) to 1 (hard).

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.rotate
text: rotate?: boolean When true, update rotates the game object to the camera rotation, as a billboard.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.static_spot
text: static_spot?: boolean When true, update never reads the game object's rotation for the spotlight direction again.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.static
text: static?: boolean When true, update never reads the game object's world position again.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.timer
text: timer?: number A timer bulb.script stores; update does not read it.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.value
text: value: Vector4 The color in x, y, z. w is the power update attenuates by distance; bulb.script sets it to 1 / power.

title: light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.y_offset
text: y_offset?: number Added to the world Y position each frame.

title: light_and_shadows.light.list

title: light_and_shadows.light.set_color
text: set_color(fog_color?: Vector4, fog?: Vector4, ambient?: Vector4, clear_color?: Vector4) Sets the base light uniform constants in light_and_shadows.constants. An omitted value leaves its constant as it is. It also posts clear_color to @render: with clear_color, or fog_color when that is omitted. fog_color — The fog color in RGB; w is the fog density. fog — The minimum and maximum Z in camera view space where the fog begins and ends. ambient — The ambient color. clear_color — The color that clears the default render target, which is the background color.

title: light_and_shadows.light.set_position
text: set_position(cam_rotation: Quaternion, cam_look_at_position: Vector3, cam_position: Vector3, cam_z?: number) Sets the camera rotation, the point the camera looks at, and the camera position. cam_rotation — The camera rotation. cam_look_at_position — The point the camera looks at. cam_position — The camera world position. cam_z — The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point, for depth of field. title: light_and_shadows.light.top_v

title: light_and_shadows.light.update
text: update(self: object, dt: number) Prepares the constants for the render script: updates each source's position and spotlight direction from its game object, sorts the sources by distance from the point the camera looks at into light_and_shadows.constants.lights, attenuates their power, and copies the camera values. Call it from update. self — Unused. dt — Unused.

title: node_repeat API
text: Dragosha / defold-sprite-repeat · node_repeat node_repeat GUI box node texture repeat (tiling) shader helper: reads a box node's atlas animation and drives the repeat material's constants. NodeRepeatAnimation RepeatFrame

title: node_repeat.create
text: create(node_or_string: Opaque<"node"> | string, animation_id: Hash | string | undefined, atlas_path: Hash | string): NodeRepeatAnimation Reads an atlas animation's frames for a GUI box node that uses the repeat material, and returns a handle that applies them. Call it from a GUI script. Apply the repeat material to the node first, and disable sprite trim mode for the atlas images: every frame must have exactly 8 UV values, or this asserts. Walks the atlas animation's frame list, so it needs Defold 1.12.3 or later. node_or_string — The box node, or its id. animation_id — The atlas animation to read. title: ainpc API
text: elefant-ai / player2-ai-npc-defold ainpc AI NPCs for Defold through the Player2 desktop app: chat completions, spawned NPCs to talk to, and a stream of their responses.

title: ainpc.chat_completion
text: chat_completion(body: Body | string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Requests a chat completion. A string is sent as one user message: the extension pastes it into {"messages":[{"content":"<text>","role":"user"}]} without escaping, so text holding a quote, a backslash or a newline makes invalid JSON. Pass a body with a messages list to send arbitrary text. body — The request body, or the text of one user message. on_reply — Called with the completion. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

title: ainpc.npc_chat
text: npc_chat(npc_id: string, body: Body, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Sends a message to a spawned NPC. npc_id — The NPC to talk to. body — The message, such as the sender_message, sender_name and game_state_info the upstream example sends. on_reply — Called with the chat reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails. npc_chat(game_id: string, npc_id: string, body: Body | string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Sends a message to a spawned NPC, given as a body or as text. game_id — Accepted but not sent: the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. npc_id — The NPC to talk to. body — The message body, or text sent as { sender_message = text, sender_name = "" }. on_reply — Called with the chat reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

title: ainpc.npc_kill
text: npc_kill(npc_id: string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Removes a spawned NPC. npc_id — The NPC to remove. on_reply — Called when the NPC is removed. on_fail — Called when the request fails. npc_kill(game_id: string, npc_id: string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Removes a spawned NPC. game_id — Accepted but not sent: the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. npc_id — The NPC to remove. on_reply — Called when the NPC is removed. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

title: ainpc.npc_responses
text: npc_responses(on_receive: ReplyCallback, on_finish: (self: unknown) => void, on_fail: FailCallback): number Opens the stream of NPC responses. Without a game_id the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. on_receive — Called with each chunk the stream delivers, decoded as JSON when it parses, otherwise as text. on_finish — Called when the stream ends, after on_fail when it failed. on_fail — Called when the stream fails. The stream id, for {@link ainpc.stop_npc_responses}. npc_responses(game_id: string, on_receive: ReplyCallback, on_finish: (self: unknown) => void, on_fail: FailCallback): number Opens the stream of NPC responses for a game. game_id — The game whose responses to stream; it replaces {game_id} in the request path. on_receive — Called with each chunk the stream delivers, decoded as JSON when it parses, otherwise as text. on_finish — Called when the stream ends, after on_fail when it failed. on_fail — Called when the stream fails. The stream id, for {@link ainpc.stop_npc_responses}.

title: ainpc.npc_spawn
text: npc_spawn(body: Body, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Spawns an NPC. body — The NPC definition, such as the name, short_name, character_description, system_prompt and voice_id the upstream example sends. on_reply — Called with the spawn reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails. npc_spawn(game_id: string, body: Body | string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Spawns an NPC from a body given as a table or as JSON text. game_id — Accepted but not sent: the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. This form is the only one that takes the body as JSON text. body — The NPC definition, or JSON text sent as it is. on_reply — Called with the spawn reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

title: ainpc.stop_npc_responses
text: stop_npc_responses(stream_id: number) Stops a stream opened by {@link ainpc.npc_responses}. An id that names no open stream is ignored. stream_id — The id npc_responses returned.

title: mic.get_permission_status

title: mic.get_rms

title: mic.is_recording

title: mic.request_permission
