title: defwin API
text: HalfstarDev / DefWin defwin A Defold extension for advanced window features on Windows. Custom window shapes, window transparency, lock aspect ratio for resize, hook for custom function of close button, and flashing of the taskbar button.

title: defwin.cancel_close
text: defwin.cancel_close() Cancel an in-progress close attempt. Until this is called again on a future close, further attempts to close the window will not re-trigger the listener or restart the delay.

title: defwin.fit_grow
text: defwin.fit_grow(ratio?: number) Fit the window to the given aspect ratio by only growing the size in one direction. ratio — The aspect ratio to fit to (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio from the display size in game.project is used.

title: defwin.fit_horizontal
text: defwin.fit_horizontal(ratio?: number) Fit the window to the given aspect ratio by resizing only the width. ratio — The aspect ratio to fit to (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio from the display size in game.project is used.

title: defwin.fit_screen
text: defwin.fit_screen() Reposition and resize the window so that no part of it is outside of the screen.

title: defwin.fit_shrink
text: defwin.fit_shrink(ratio?: number) Fit the window to the given aspect ratio by only shrinking the size in one direction. ratio — The aspect ratio to fit to (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio from the display size in game.project is used.

title: defwin.fit_vertical
text: defwin.fit_vertical(ratio?: number) Fit the window to the given aspect ratio by resizing only the height. ratio — The aspect ratio to fit to (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio from the display size in game.project is used.

title: defwin.flash
text: defwin.flash(taskbar: boolean, caption: boolean, count?: number, timeout?: number) Flash the window a limited number of times. taskbar — Should the taskbar button flash caption — Should the window caption flash count — How many times to flash (default 1) timeout — Time between flashes, in seconds (default platform cursor blink rate)

title: defwin.get_caption_color
text: defwin.get_caption_color(): vmath.vector4 Get the opaque color of the window caption. color — (r, g, b, 1) with r, g, b in [0.0, 1.0]

title: defwin.get_dark_mode_preference
text: defwin.get_dark_mode_preference(): bool | nil Get the preference of the current user for dark mode or light mode. preference — ´true´ if dark mode is preferred, ´false´ if light mode is preferred, and ´nil´ if the preference is unknown

title: defwin.hide_progress
text: defwin.hide_progress() Hide the progress bar on the taskbar button, until a new value or state is set.

title: defwin.lock_ratio
text: defwin.lock_ratio(ratio?: number) Lock the aspect ratio of the window when the user drags its border. ratio — The aspect ratio to lock (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio of the default resolution in game.project is used.

title: defwin.pause_progress
text: defwin.pause_progress() Pauses the progress bar on the taskbar button, turning it yellow until a new value or state is set.

title: defwin.prevent_sleep
text: defwin.prevent_sleep(enable: boolean) Keep the window active to prevent the system from going to sleep while enabled. enable — Prevent sleep if true, let system handle activity on false

title: defwin.quit
text: defwin.quit() Quit the game, respecting the configured close delay and sound fade-out settings.

title: defwin.request_quit
text: defwin.request_quit() Request to quit the game, behaving as if the user pressed the close button or Alt+F4. Triggers the close listener and delay handling.

title: defwin.reset_alpha
text: defwin.reset_alpha() Remove the window transparency, restoring the original opaque window.

title: defwin.set_alpha_color
text: defwin.set_alpha_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number): boolean Set which color should be rendered transparent by the window, and removes the window border. The transparent areas will also be click-through. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the render clear color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

title: defwin.set_alpha
text: defwin.set_alpha(alpha: number) Set the transparency of the whole window, including the border. Can't be used together with set_alpha_color. alpha — Opacity in [0.0, 1.0]. 0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque.

title: defwin.set_border_color_none
text: defwin.set_border_color_none() Set the window border color to be transparent.

title: defwin.set_border_color
text: defwin.set_border_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number) Set window border color. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the default color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

title: defwin.set_borderless
text: defwin.set_borderless(enable: boolean) Remove or restore the window border. enable — true to remove the window border, false to restore it

title: defwin.set_caption_color
text: defwin.set_caption_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number) Set window caption color. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the default color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

title: defwin.set_caption_text_color
text: defwin.set_caption_text_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number) Set window caption text color. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the default color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

title: defwin.set_close_delay
text: defwin.set_close_delay(delay?: number) Set the time after a close request until the game exits automatically. delay — Time in seconds before the game exits. 0 closes as soon as the close button is pressed. Pass nil for no automatic close, leaving the close listener fully in control.

title: defwin.set_close_listener
text: defwin.set_close_listener(listener: function) Set a listener that is called instead of quitting the game when the close button is pressed. listener — Called when a close is requested. Pass nil to clear the listener and restore default close behaviour.

title: defwin.set_close_sound_fadeout
text: defwin.set_close_sound_fadeout(enable: boolean) If enabled and a close delay is set, the master sound group gain is faded out over the delay duration until shutdown. enable — true to enable the sound fade-out on close

title: defwin.set_corners_default
text: defwin.set_corners_default() Set the corner style of the window frame to the default.

title: defwin.set_corners_not_rounded
text: defwin.set_corners_not_rounded() Set the corner style of the window frame to not rounded.

title: defwin.set_corners_rounded
text: defwin.set_corners_rounded() Set the corner style of the window frame to rounded, if available.

title: defwin.set_corners_rounded_small
text: defwin.set_corners_rounded_small() Set the corner style of the window frame to slightly rounded, if available.

title: defwin.set_dark_mode
text: defwin.set_dark_mode(enable: boolean) Set the window border style to dark mode or light mode. enable — Set to dark mode on true, and to light mode on false

title: defwin.set_image_buffer
text: defwin.set_image_buffer(bytes_string: string, width: number, height: number, flip?: boolean): boolean Use an image instead of the default window contents, with pixels outside the image left transparent. bytes_string — Raw RGBA pixel data, e.g. from buffer.get_bytes(buf, hash("rgba")) width — Width of the image buffer in pixels height — Height of the image buffer in pixels flip — If true, the rows are flipped vertically (default false) success — true if the image buffer was applied successfully

title: defwin.set_minimum_window_size
text: defwin.set_minimum_window_size(width: number, height?: number) Set the minimum size a window is allowed to have when resized. width — Minimum width in pixels. height — Minimum height in pixels.

title: defwin.set_progress_error
text: defwin.set_progress_error() Set the progress bar on the taskbar button to an error state, turning it red.

title: defwin.set_progress_load
text: defwin.set_progress_load() Set the progress bar on the taskbar button to an indeterminate loading state.

title: defwin.set_progress
text: defwin.set_progress(value: number) Set the progress bar on the taskbar button. value — Progress in [0.0, 1.0]

title: defwin.set_rtl_layout
text: defwin.set_rtl_layout(enable: boolean) Set window bar layout to right-to-left, affecting buttons, title, and icon. enable — Set window to RTL layout on true, and to LTR layout on false

title: defwin.set_tool_window
text: defwin.set_tool_window(enable: boolean) Turns the window into a tool window. Tool windows are not shown on taskbar and Alt-Tab, and have no minimize and maximize buttons or icon. enable — Set to tool window on true, and back to normal window on false

title: defwin.start_drag
text: defwin.start_drag() Start dragging the window along the cursor. Must be paired with repeated calls to update_drag() to have any effect.

title: defwin.start_flash
text: defwin.start_flash(taskbar: boolean, caption: boolean, until_focused: boolean, timeout?: number) Start flashing the window until manually stopped or until the window regains focus. taskbar — Should the taskbar button flash caption — Should the window caption flash until_focused — If true, focusing the window stops the flash. If false, it flashes until stop_flash() is called. timeout — Time between flashes, in seconds (default platform cursor blink rate)

title: defwin.stop_drag
text: defwin.stop_drag() Stop dragging the window along the cursor.

title: defwin.stop_flash
text: defwin.stop_flash() Stop the window from flashing. As the current flash cycle still completes, it can take a few seconds to disappear.

title: defwin.unlock_ratio
text: defwin.unlock_ratio() Remove the aspect ratio lock set by lock_ratio.

title: defwin.update_drag
text: defwin.update_drag() Update one frame of the window drag started with start_drag(). Should be called every frame (e.g. from an on_input or update callback) while dragging is active.

title: nakama.socket.matchmaker_add

title: nakama.socket.matchmaker_remove

title: live_unbundler.get_modules_download_progress
text: get_modules_download_progress(module_names: string | string[]): liveupdater_download_progress Byte-based progress for a module or a set of modules, with a per-resolution breakdown in the low/high fields. Shared dependency archives are counted once per set; an archive identical in both manifests counts toward the resolution counted first (for RES_BOTH that is lowres — the pass that actually downloads it). Anchored to the download queue: an archive counts as downloaded when nothing for it is pending, so the result reaches 100 exactly when the set's downloads drain. For by_request modules that were not requested yet, the future queue content is predicted from the same rules enqueue_modules uses; that prediction can dip for a moment while a shared archive is remounted to its highres copy, it recovers on the next mount.

title: dissolve_fx API
text: indiesoftby / defold-dissolve-fx dissolve_fx A dissolve effect for sprites. Add a noise and a ramp image to the sprite's atlas and set dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material as the sprite's material, then call init from the script's init. The noise drives the dissolve and the ramp colors its burning edge.

title: dissolve_fx.find_uvrect
text: find_uvrect(sprite_url: string | Hash | Url, image_id: string, scale_mode?: ScaleMode): LuaMultiReturn<[ number, number, number, number ]> Finds an image in the sprite's atlas and returns its uv rect in texture space as four values: center x, center y, width and height: const [x, y, w, h] = dissolve_fx.find_uvrect("#sprite", "noise"). Upstream asserts that image_id is a string, that the atlas holds the image, and that the image is not trimmed (trim mode off, 8 uvs). With scale_mode, the width and height are also divided by the size of the sprite's current animation, so the vertex shader can map the noise from local positions. sprite_url — The sprite component. image_id — The image's id in the sprite's atlas. scale_mode — How the width and height are scaled to the sprite. Upstream asserts stretch or cover. When omitted, they are left in texture space.

title: dissolve_fx.init
text: init(sprite_url: string | Hash | Url, noise_image: string, ramp_image: string, noise_scale_mode?: ScaleMode) Sets the sprite's noise_uvrect and ramp_uvrect from the two images in its atlas. The sprite must use the dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material material. The effect is then driven by the sprite's dissolve.z property, the size of the burning edge, and dissolve.w, from 0 to 1, through go.set and go.animate: go.animate("#sprite", "dissolve.w", go.PLAYBACK_LOOP_PINGPONG, 1, go.EASING_LINEAR, 3). sprite_url — The sprite component with the dissolve material. noise_image — The noise image's id in the sprite's atlas. ramp_image — The ramp image's id in the sprite's atlas. noise_scale_mode — How the noise is scaled to the sprite. Defaults to stretch.

title: dissolve_fx.ScaleMode
text: ScaleMode type ScaleMode = "stretch" | "cover"

text: indiesoftby / defold-pointer-lock pointer_lock Mouse lock state and a virtual in-game cursor. Add pointer_lock/pointer_lock.script to the bootstrap collection: it locks the cursor on a click and unlocks it on key_esc, and keeps locked current. The cursor fields are plain module fields; assigning one goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only: (pointer as { cursor_visible: boolean }).cursor_visible = true.

title: pointer_lock.cursor_y

title: pointer_lock.DISPLAY_HEIGHT
text: DISPLAY_HEIGHT: number The display.height project setting, read once when the module loads.

title: pointer_lock.DISPLAY_WIDTH
text: DISPLAY_WIDTH: number The display.width project setting, read once when the module loads.

title: pointer_lock.locked
text: locked: boolean Whether the pointer is locked. Read-only for a project: pointer_lock.script sets it, and update_lock_state copies the window's mouse lock into it. Starts false.

title: pointer_lock.transform_input
text: transform_input<A extends { x?: number; y?: number; }>(action_id: Hash | undefined, action: A): LuaMultiReturn<[ Hash | undefined, A & { x: number; y: number; } ]> Converts on_input arguments into the virtual in-game cursor system: sets action.x and action.y to the cursor position, on the same table it returns, and returns undefined as the action id unless the pointer is locked and the cursor is visible. Call it first in on_input: [action_id, action] = pointer.transform_input(action_id, action).

title: pointer_lock.update_cursor_position
text: update_cursor_position(action: { dx: number; dy: number; }) Moves the virtual cursor by the action's dx and dy, clamped to the display size. Pass it a pointer-movement action, which carries both.

title: splitmix64.dice
text: splitmix64.dice(roll: number, type: number): LuaMultiReturn<[table, number]> Roll one or more dice of the given type. Returns a table of individual rolls and the total sum. roll — Number of dice to roll (must be > 0). type — Dice type (splitmix64.D4, splitmix64.D6, splitmix64.D8, splitmix64.D10, splitmix64.D12, splitmix64.D20, or splitmix64.D100). rolls — Table of individual roll results. total — Sum of all rolls.

title: splitmix64.new_instance
text: splitmix64.new_instance(seed?: number | string): userdata Creates a new RNG instance with independent state. Optional seed (number or string) for reproducibility. seed — Optional seed for the new instance. rng — RNG instance with methods random, randomseed, state, randomchoice, weightedchoice, toss, dice, shuffle. Same API as the module but with isolated state.

title: splitmix64.randomchoice
text: splitmix64.randomchoice(t: table): any Returns a random value from array t. If the array is empty an error is raised. t — Array of values to choose from. value — Random element from the array.

title: splitmix64.random
text: splitmix64.random(m?: number, n?: number): number When called without arguments, returns a uniform pseudo-random real number in the range [0,1). When called with an integer number m, splitmix64.random returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [1, m]. When called with two integer numbers m and n, splitmix64.random returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [m, n].

title: splitmix64.randomseed
text: splitmix64.randomseed(x: number | string) Sets x as the "seed" for the pseudo-random generator: equal seeds produce equal sequences of numbers. Accepts a number or a string (decimal representation of uint64) for full 64-bit precision. x — Seed value as number or string (e.g. \"18446744073709551615\" for full uint64 range).

title: splitmix64.shuffle
text: splitmix64.shuffle(t: table, inplace?: boolean): table Shuffles an array using the Fisher-Yates algorithm. Returns a shuffled copy of the array, or if inplace is true, shuffles the original array in-place and returns it. t — Array to shuffle. inplace — If true, shuffle the array in-place instead of creating a copy. Defaults to false. result — The shuffled array (a new table, or the same table if inplace is true).

title: splitmix64.state
text: splitmix64.state(): string Returns the current internal state x as a string. Use this to save/restore state or pass to randomseed for full 64-bit precision (Lua double cannot represent all uint64 values). state — Current state as decimal string.

title: splitmix64.toss
text: splitmix64.toss(): number Toss a coin. Returns 0 or 1. value — Returns 0 or 1.

title: splitmix64.weightedchoice
text: splitmix64.weightedchoice(t: table): any Takes table t where keys are choices and values are weights. Returns a random key. Keys are sorted deterministically (numbers first, then strings lexicographically) before selection, so the result is reproducible for the same seed. Weights must be >= 0. If all weights are 0 or a weight is negative, an error is raised. t — Table of key-weight pairs. key — Random key chosen by weight.

title: decore.apply_component
text: apply_component(entity: entity, component_id: string, component_data?: unknown | undefined): entity Add component to entity. If component not exists, it will be created with default values If component already exists, plain table data is merged into it An object (table with a metatable, like event or promise) replaces the component as a whole To refresh system filters, call world:addEntity(entity) after this function When a new component key is introduced, the entity shape token is derived so the system-membership cache stays valid. Prefer this over direct assignment for filter-relevant keys. component_data — if nil, create component with default values

title: event API
text: Insality / defold-event event The Event module, used to create and manage events. Allows to subscribe to events and trigger them. event_logger event promise_cancelled_context promise queue_event_data queue

title: event.create
text: create(callback?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): event Generate a new event instance. This instance can then be used to subscribe to and trigger events. The callback function will be called when the event is triggered. The callback_context parameter is optional and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function. Usually, it is used to pass the self instance. local e = event.create() local e = event.create(function(self) print("ok") end, self) callback — The function to be called when the event is triggered. Or the event instance to subscribe. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. A new event instance.

title: event.clear
text: clear() Remove all callbacks subscribed to the event, effectively resetting it. on_click_event:clear()

title: event.is_empty
text: is_empty(): boolean Check if the event has no subscribed callbacks. local is_empty = on_click_event:is_empty() True if the event has no subscribed callbacks

title: event.is_subscribed
text: is_subscribed(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): LuaMultiReturn<[boolean, number | undefined]> Determine if a specific callback is currently subscribed to the event. The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback. local is_subscribed = on_click_event:is_subscribed(callback, self) callback — The callback function in question. Or the event instance to check. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. True if the callback is subscribed to the event Index of callback in event if subscribed (return first found index)

title: event.subscribe_once
text: subscribe_once(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a callback for a single trigger. After the first trigger the callback is automatically unsubscribed. on_click_event:subscribe_once(function(self) print("one-time click!") end, self) callback — The function or event to run once. callback_context — Same as subscribe. True if subscribed

title: event.subscribe
text: subscribe(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a callback to the event or other event. The callback will be invoked whenever the event is triggered. The callback_context parameter is optional and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function. If the callback with context is already subscribed, the warning will be logged. local function callback(self) print("clicked!") end on_click_event:subscribe(callback, self) -- Subscribe an event to another event event_1 = event.create(callback) event_2 = event.create() event_2:subscribe(event_1) -- Now event2 will trigger event1 callback — The function to be executed when the event occurs. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. True if event is subscribed (Will return false if the callback is already subscribed)

title: event.trigger
text: trigger(...args: unknown[]): unknown Trigger the event, causing all subscribed callbacks to be executed. Any parameters passed to trigger will be forwarded to the callbacks. The return value of the last executed callback is returned. The event:trigger(...) can be called as event(...). on_click_event:trigger("arg1", "arg2") -- The event can be triggered as a function on_click_event("arg1", "arg2") ...args — Any number of parameters to be passed to the subscribed callbacks. Result of the last triggered callback

title: event.unsubscribe
text: unsubscribe(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Remove a previously subscribed callback from the event. The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback. If there is no callback_context provided, all callbacks with the same function will be unsubscribed. on_click_event:unsubscribe(callback, self) callback — The callback function to unsubscribe. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. If not provided, will unsubscribe all callbacks with the same function. True if event is unsubscribed

title: event.is_event
text: is_event(value: unknown): boolean Check if the table is an event instance. if event.is_event(my_value) then my_value:trigger() end

text: is_cancelled: boolean

title: event.promise_cancelled_context.on_cancel
text: on_cancel: event

title: event.promise._reject_cancel_children
text: reject_cancel_children() Reject pending child promises when a settled promise is cancelled.

title: event.promise.append
text: append(task: ((value: unknown) => unknown) | promise): promise Append a task to this promise's internal sequence without reassigning. The task may return a value or a promise. If task is a promise, the pipeline waits for it to finish and adopts its result. The incoming value is not forwarded into task (same as append(function() return task end)). Returns self for chaining. Almost similar to promise = promise:next(task), but without reassigning the promise. pipeline:append(step1) pipeline:append(step2) pipeline:append(step3) local last = pipeline:tail() print("Is going to check status of", last:is_pending())

title: event.promise.cancel
text: cancel() Cancel in-progress work in this promise chain. A pending promise is rejected with the cancelled reason and on_cancel runs. A settled promise is left as-is; pending descendants linked via next / append / adopt are still rejected, and they trigger the shared on_cancel. If nothing is still pending, this is a no-op. my_promise:cancel()

title: event.promise.catch
text: catch(on_rejected: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach a rejection handler to the promise. Equivalent to next(nil, on_rejected). load_data():catch(function(err) print("Failed:", err) end) on_rejected — Handler called when promise is rejected. context — The context to call the handler with. A new promise representing the result of the handler.

title: event.promise.finally
text: finally(on_finally: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach a handler that is called regardless of whether the promise is resolved or rejected. The handler is called with the resolved value or rejection reason. When context is provided, it is passed as the first argument. The handler return value is ignored. load_data():finally(function() hide_loading_spinner() end) on_finally — Handler called when promise is finished (resolved or rejected). context — The context to call the handler with. A new promise that resolves/rejects with the same value/reason as the original.

title: event.promise.is_cancelled
text: is_cancelled(): boolean Check if the shared cancel_context was cancelled. True if the promise chain was cancelled.

title: event.promise.is_finished
text: is_finished(): boolean Check if the promise is finished (either resolved or rejected). True if the promise is finished.

title: event.promise.is_pending
text: is_pending(): boolean Check if the promise is in pending state. True if the promise is pending.

title: event.promise.is_rejected
text: is_rejected(): boolean Check if the promise is in rejected state. True if the promise is rejected.

title: event.promise.is_resolved
text: is_resolved(): boolean Check if the promise is in resolved state. True if the promise is resolved.

title: event.promise.next
text: next(on_resolved?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | promise | event | undefined, on_rejected?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | promise | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach resolve and reject handlers to the promise. Returns a new promise that will be resolved or rejected based on the handlers' return values. load_data():next(function(data) return process(data) end):next(display):catch(show_error) on_resolved — Handler called when promise is resolved. If nil, value passes through. on_rejected — Handler called when promise is rejected. If nil, rejection passes through. context — The context to call the handlers with. A new promise representing the result of the handlers.

title: event.promise.on_cancel
text: on_cancel: event Event for cancellation cleanup subscriptions (shared across the promise chain)

text: clear() Remove all events and handlers from this queue instance, effectively resetting it. my_queue:clear()

title: event.queue.clear_events
text: clear_events() Clear all pending events in this queue. my_queue:clear_events()

title: event.queue.get_events

title: event.queue.has_subscribers
text: has_subscribers(): boolean Check if this queue instance has no subscribed handlers. if my_queue:has_subscribers() then my_queue:push(data) end True if the queue instance has subscribed handlers

title: event.queue.is_empty
text: is_empty(): boolean Check if this queue has no pending events. if my_queue:is_empty() then return end True if the queue has no pending events

title: event.queue.is_subscribed
text: is_subscribed(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): LuaMultiReturn<[boolean, number | undefined]> Check if a handler is subscribed to this queue instance. local ok = my_queue:is_subscribed(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to check. context — The context that was passed when subscribing. True if handler is subscribed Index of handler if subscribed

title: event.queue.process_next
text: process_next(event_handler?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Process exactly one queued event with a specific handler (subscribers will NOT be called). If the handler returns non-nil the event will be removed from the queue. local handled = my_queue:process_next(function(data) return handle(data) end) event_handler — Specific handler or event to process the event. If this function returns non-nil, the event will be removed from the queue. context — The context to be passed to the handler. True if the head event was handled and removed

title: event.queue.process
text: process(event_handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined) Process all events in this queue immediately. Subscribers will not be called in this function. Events can be handled and removed in event handler callback. If event is handled, it will be removed from the queue. my_queue:process(function(self, data) return handle(data) end, self) event_handler — Specific handler or event to process the events. If this function returns non-nil, the event will be removed from the queue. context — The context to be passed to the handler.

title: event.queue.push
text: push(data: unknown, on_handle?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined) Push a new event to the queue. The event will exist until it's handled by a subscriber. If there are already subscribers for this queue instance, they will be called immediately. If multiple subscribers handle the event, all subscribers will still be called. The on_handle callback will be called for each subscriber that handles the event. my_queue:push(save_data) my_queue:push(save_data, function() print("saved!") end) data — The data associated with the event. on_handle — Callback function or event to be called when the event is handled. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the on_handle function when the event is handled.

title: event.queue.subscribe_once
text: subscribe_once(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a handler until it handles one event. The handler is invoked for each event in the queue until it returns non-nil (handles an event) then it is automatically unsubscribed and will not be invoked again, even if more events remain in the queue. my_queue:subscribe_once(function(self, data) return process(data) end, self) handler — The handler function or event to be called when an event is pushed. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the handler function. True if handler was subscribed successfully

title: event.queue.subscribe
text: subscribe(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a handler to this queue instance. When an event is pushed to this queue, the handler will be called. If there are already events in the queue, they will be processed immediately. Return a non-nil value from the handler to mark the event as handled and remove it from the queue. local function on_save(self, data) do_save(data) return true end my_queue:subscribe(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to be called when an event is pushed. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the handler function. True if handler was subscribed successfully

title: event.queue.unsubscribe
text: unsubscribe(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Unsubscribe a handler from this queue instance. my_queue:unsubscribe(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to unsubscribe. context — The context that was passed when subscribing. True if handler was unsubscribed successfully

title: printer.Printer.print

Wrap a style name in braces to switch style ({red}), use {/} to return to the default style, {n} for a line break and {image:name} for an image. str — The text to print. source — A source added with add_source_style. Its style is copied over the default style and becomes this text's base style, which {/} returns to. true when the new text starts printing; false when text was still printing, so the new text did not start. print then calls instant_appear, which reveals that text at once only when the effective style of the symbol currently appearing has can_skip set to true; otherwise it keeps printing.

text: bind_save_state(table_key_id: string, table_reference: LuaTable): LuaTable Binds a table reference as a part of the game state. When the game state is saved, all table references will be saved. This is a main function to use to save your game state. You can bind multiple tables to different parts of the game state. After binding, the table_reference will be updated with the saved data if it exists. local game_state = { level = 1, money = 100 } saver.bind_save_state("game", game_state) -- If we have previously saved game state, the game_state will be changed to the saved data print(game_state.level) -- 5 (if it was saved before) table_key_id — The table key to set the value for. table_reference — The table reference to bind to the game state. Default is the file name specified in the game.project file. true if the game state was deleted successfully, false otherwise.

Used only at desktop platforms and if game started from the Defold Editor. local project_folder = saver.get_current_game_project_folder() print(project_folder) -- "/Users/user/projects/my_game" The absolute path to the current game project folder. title: saver.saver.get_save_path
text: get_save_path(filename?: string | undefined): string Returns the absolute path to the game save folder. If a file name is provided, the path to the file in the game save folder is returned. Filename supports subfolders. local folder_path = saver.get_save_path() print(folder_path) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/" local file_path = saver.get_save_path("data.json") print(file_path) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/data.json" local file_path_2 = saver.get_save_path("profiles/profile1.json") print(file_path_2) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/profiles/profile1.json" filename — The name of the file to get the path for. Can contain subfolders. If nil, returns the folder path. The absolute path to the game save folder, or the path to the file in the game save folder if a file name is provided.

title: saver.saver.get_save_version
text: get_save_version(): number Returns the current save version of the game state. The save version is used to check if the game state is older than the current version. The save version increments when the game state is saved. local save_version = saver.get_save_version() print(save_version) The current save version of the game state.

title: saver.saver.init
text: init(config?: saver_config | undefined) Initialize the Saver module. Should be called at the start of your game to set up the module. Call it after saver.set_migrations if you are using migrations. This function loads the game state from a file and starts the autosave timer. If the game state file does not exist, a new game state is created. saver.init() config — Configuration table.

Contains the file name and extension. format — Optional format override (json, lua, serialized). If not specified, format will be detected from paths extension. The data loaded from the file. Filename supports subfolders. local data = { score = 100, level = 1 } -- Save the data to the game save folder saver.save_file_by_name(data, "data.json") data — The lua table to save to the file. filename — The name of the file to save the data to. Can contain subfolders. format — Optional format override (json, lua, serialized, binary) true if the file was saved successfully, false otherwise.

title: saver.saver.save_file_by_path
text: save_file_by_path(data: LuaTable, path: string, format?: string | undefined): boolean Saves the specified data to a file at the specified path. The data format is chosen by file path extension. local data = { score = 100, level = 1 } -- Get project path works on build from the Defold Editor only local project_path = saver.get_current_game_project_folder() -- Use path to the resources folder local file_path = saver.get_save_path(project_path .. "/resources/data.json") saver.save_file_by_path(data, file_path) data — The lua table to save to the file. path — The absolute path to save the file to. Contains the file name and extension. Extension can be empty, .json or .lua format — Optional format override (json, lua, serialized, binary). If not specified, format will be detected from paths extension or data type. true if the file was saved successfully, false otherwise.

text: set_logger(logger_instance?: saver_logger | LuaTable | undefined) File format enum (mirrors saver_internal.FORMAT) Customize the logging mechanism used by Defold Saver. You can use Defold Log library or provide a custom logger. local log = require("log.log") local saver = require("saver.saver") saver.set_logger(log.get_logger("saver")) logger_instance — A logger object that follows the specified logging interface, including methods for trace, debug, info, warn, error. Pass nil to remove the default logger.

title: saver.saver.set_migrations
text: set_migrations(migrations_table: ((game_state: saver_game_state, logger: saver_logger) => undefined)[]) Sets the list of migrations to apply after loading the game state manually with saver.apply_migrations() function. Migrations are used to update the game state in case of changes to the game state structure. Migrations are applied in order. Each migration should be a function that takes the game state as a parameter and returns the updated game state. local migrations = { -- Migration 1 function(game_state, logger) -- Assume we have new level_data field in the game state and we need to move level and score to it game_state.game.level_data = { level = game_state.game.level, score = game_state.game.score } game_state.game.level = nil game_state.game.score = nil return game_state }, -- Migration 2 function(game_state, logger) -- Just an example, multiply the score by 1000. For example we changed our score system game_state.game.level_data.score = game_state.game.level_data.score 1000 return game_state } } saver.set_migrations(migrations) saver.init() saver.bind_save_state("game", game_state) saver.apply_migrations() migrations_table — Array of migration functions

title: tweener API
text: Insality / defold-tweener tweener A tweener module to manage tweening operations. Tween functions are based on the Defold timer.delay function. Use tweener.tween to create a tween, and tweener.ease to get the result of an easing function. You can track the final call of tween by last parameter of the callback function. tween

title: tweener.cancel
text: cancel(tween?: tween | undefined): boolean Cancel a previous running tween. tween — the tween handle returned by tween function if the tween was active, false if the tween is already cancelled / complete

title: tweener.ease
text: ease(easing_function: easing_function, from: number, to: number, time: number | undefined, time_elapsed: number): number Returns the result of an easing function. time — The duration of the tween in seconds, default is 1 time_elapsed — current time [0 .. t - from] The result of easing

title: tweener.is_active
text: is_active(tween: tween): boolean Check if a tween exists tween — the tween handle returned by tween function if the tween is active, false if the tween finished

title: tweener.is_paused
text: is_paused(tween: tween): boolean Check if a tween is paused tween — the tween handle returned by tween function true if the tween is active and paused, false if the tween is running

title: tweener.set_pause
text: set_pause(tween: tween, is_paused: boolean) Sets the pause on a running tween. tween — the tween handle returned by tween function is_paused — the tween paused state

title: tweener.tween
text: tween(easing_function: easing_function, from: number, to: number, time: number | undefined, callback: (value: number, is_end: boolean, time_elapsed: number, time_total: number) => void, update_delta_time?: number | undefined): tween Starts a tweening operation. Return a tween object to manage the tween. easing_function — The easing function to use from — The starting value to tween from to — The target value to tween to time — The duration of the tween in seconds, default is 1 callback — The callback function to call on each update update_delta_time — Default is 1/60, the time between updates A new created tween state

title: druid.druid_instance.set_blacklist
text: set_blacklist(blacklist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined): druid_instance Set blacklist components for input processing. If blacklist is set, the listed components and their descendants are skipped on the input step. An empty list and nil both deny nobody. Descendants created later still match. The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. The filter owner is not affected by its own filter, to filter a widget itself set the filter from the outside: the gui script or the parent widget. blacklist_components — The array of component to blacklist, nil to clear it The Druid instance

title: druid.druid_instance.set_style
text: set_style(style?: LuaTable | undefined): druid_instance Set a style of Druid instance. Pass nil to reset to the default style. The style is applied to the components created after this call, already created components keep their style. style — The Druid style table The Druid instance itself for chaining

title: druid.druid_instance.set_whitelist
text: set_whitelist(whitelist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined): druid_instance Set whitelist components for input processing. If whitelist is set, only the listed components and their descendants receive input. An empty list allows none. Pass nil to clear the whitelist (all components receive input). Descendants created later still match, no need to call this again. The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. The filter owner is not affected by its own filter, so a widget can restrict its children and keep its own on_input working. whitelist_components — The array of component to whitelist, nil to clear it The Druid instance

Unlike druid.get_widget(), the instance is returned as is, without cross-context events wrapping, so from a game object script you should only use its plain functions, not the GUI related ones. local instance = druid.get_druid("gui_widget") instance:set_style(my_style) -- Should be set before creating widgets gui_url — GUI url or string of component name near current script The registered Druid instance or nil if not registered

This allows using only druid_widget.gui_script for GUI files and call this widget functions from Game Object script file. Widget class here is your lua file for the GUI scene (widgets in Druid) msg.url(nil, nil, "gui_widget") -- current game object msg.url(nil, object_url, "gui_widget") -- other game object widget_class — The class of the widget to return gui_url — GUI url or string of component name near current script params — Additional parameters to pass to the widget's init function template — The GUI template name used by the widget nodes The new created widget,

title: panthera.play_detached
text: play_detached(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options | undefined) Play animation as a child of the current animation state, allowing multiple animations to run independently and simultaneously. This creates a detached animation that runs in parallel with the main animation state without affecting it. The child animation will be automatically cleaned up when it completes. animation_state — The parent animation state object animation_id — The ID of the animation to play as a detached child options — Options for the detached animation playback

title: panthera.play_tweener
text: play_tweener(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options_tweener | undefined) Play animation with easing support using tweener. Allows for non-linear animation playback with custom easing functions. animation_state — The animation state object animation_id — The ID of the animation to play options — Options including easing function, speed, and callbacks

title: panthera.play
text: play(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options | undefined) Play an animation with specified ID and options. One timer drives the whole tree, each tick finishes the running clips before starting new ones. animation_state — The animation state object returned by create_go or create_gui animation_id — The ID of the animation to play options — Options for the animation playback

title: panthera.reload_animation
text: reload_animation(animation_path?: string | undefined) Reload animations from JSON files, useful for development and debugging. The animations loaded from Lua tables will not be reloaded. Animation will be reloaded only at desktop. animation_path — Specific animation to reload. If omitted, all loaded animations are reloaded

title: panthera.set_logger
text: set_logger(logger_instance?: panthera_logger | LuaTable | undefined) Customize the logging mechanism used by Panthera Runtime. You can use Defold Log library or provide a custom logger. logger_instance — A logger object that follows the specified logging interface. Pass nil to use empty logger

title: panthera.set_time
text: set_time(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, time: number, event_callback?: ((event_id: string, node: Opaque<"node"> | undefined, string_value: string, number_value: number) => void) | undefined): boolean Set the current time of an animation. This function stops any currently playing animation. animation_state — The animation state object returned by create_go or create_gui. animation_id — The ID of the animation to modify. time — The target time in seconds to which the animation should be set. True if animation state was set successfully, false if animation can't be set

title: panthera.stop
text: stop(animation_state: panthera_animation): boolean Stop a currently playing animation. The animation will be stopped at current time. animation_state — The animation state object to stop True if animation was stopped, false if animation is not playing

title: iapm API
text: itzmiadm / Myket-IAP-Defold iapm Functions and constants for doing Myket in-app purchases.

title: iapm.buy
text: iapm.buy(id: string) Start a purchase for a Myket one-time product. id — product to buy

title: iapm.finish
text: iapm.finish(transaction: table) Consume a product transaction. Call this only for consumable products and only after content delivery succeeds. Calling iapm.finish is required for a consumable transaction if auto_finish_transactions is disabled in project settings. Calling this function with auto_finish_transactions enabled is ignored and a warning is printed. The transaction.state field must equal iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED. Calling this for a transaction whose type is subs is ignored. transaction — transaction table parameter as supplied in listener callback

title: iapm.list
text: iapm.list(ids: table, callback: function) Get details for the requested Myket one-time products and subscriptions. ids — table (array) of identifiers to get products from callback — result callback taking the following parameters

title: iapm.REASON_UNSPECIFIED
text: iapm.REASON_UNSPECIFIED unspecified error reason

title: iapm.REASON_USER_CANCELED
text: iapm.REASON_USER_CANCELED user canceled reason

title: iapm.restore
text: iapm.restore(): boolean Restore owned, unconsumed products and active subscriptions. Results are sent to the listener registered with set_listener. Subscriptions are never consumed. success — value is true if current store supports handling restored transactions, otherwise false.

title: iapm.set_listener
text: iapm.set_listener(listener: function) Set the callback function to receive purchase transaction events. listener — listener callback function. Pass an empty function if you no longer wish to receive callbacks.

title: iapm.set_public_key
text: iapm.set_public_key(public_key: string): boolean Set or replace the Base64-encoded Myket application public key used for local SHA1withRSA purchase-signature verification. Call this before set_listener, buy, or restore. Prefer the iap.public_key game.project setting so the key is available while pending purchases are processed. public_key — The application public key from the Myket developer panel. valid — true when the value is a valid Base64-encoded RSA public key; false otherwise.

title: iapm.subscribe
text: iapm.subscribe(id: string) Start a purchase for a Myket subscription. The result is delivered to the listener registered with set_listener. Subscriptions are never consumed, regardless of the auto_finish_transactions setting. An error is delivered when the installed Myket client does not support subscriptions. id — subscription product identifier

title: iapm.TRANS_STATE_FAILED
text: iapm.TRANS_STATE_FAILED transaction failed state

title: iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED
text: iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED transaction purchased state

title: iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASING
text: iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASING transaction purchasing state This is an intermediate mode followed by TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED. Store provider support dependent.

title: iapm.TRANS_STATE_RESTORED
text: iapm.TRANS_STATE_RESTORED transaction restored state This is only available on store providers supporting restoring purchases.

title: iapm.TRANS_STATE_UNVERIFIED
text: iapm.TRANS_STATE_UNVERIFIED transaction unverified state, requires verification of purchase

text: voronoi.get_debug_image(diagram: userdata): userdata Rasterizes the current diagram into an RGB buffer matching the context dimensions. diagram — Generated diagram context. image — Buffer with a uint8 rgb stream containing three components per pixel.

title: voronoi.get_delauney_edges
text: voronoi.get_delauney_edges(diagram: userdata): table Returns the Delauney edges produced by the upstream jcv_delauney iterator. Each entry contains edge, sites, and pos fields matching jcv_delauney_edge. The upstream spelling "delauney" is preserved in the Lua function name. diagram — Generated diagram context. edges — Array of Delauney edge tables.

title: voronoi.get_edges
text: voronoi.get_edges(diagram: userdata): table Returns every diagram edge. Each edge contains sites, pos, and vertices. sites contains two 1-based input indices, with 0 denoting the clipping boundary. pos contains two { x, y } endpoints. vertices contains two 1-based indices into get_vertices(), with 0 denoting an invalid endpoint. diagram — Generated diagram context. edges — Array of edge tables. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged.

title: voronoi.get_num_sites
text: voronoi.get_num_sites(diagram: userdata): number Returns diagram.numsites, the number of unique generated sites. This may be smaller than the input count when points are duplicated. diagram — Generated diagram context. count — Number of unique generated sites.

title: voronoi.get_num_vertices
text: voronoi.get_num_vertices(diagram: userdata): number Returns diagram.numvertices, the number of unique Voronoi vertices. diagram — Generated diagram context. count — Number of unique vertices.

title: voronoi.get_site
text: voronoi.get_site(diagram: userdata, index: number): table Returns the generated site for a 1-based original input index. The site has the same fields as entries returned by get_sites(). diagram — Generated diagram context. index — 1-based original input point index. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged. site — Site table for the requested input point.

title: voronoi.get_sites
text: voronoi.get_sites(diagram: userdata): table Returns every generated site. A site contains p, index, boundary, edges, and the convenience field area. The p field is { x, y }; index is the 1-based original input index; boundary reports whether the cell touches the clipping boundary; and edges contains counter-clockwise edge tables. diagram — Generated diagram context. sites — Array of site tables. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged.

title: voronoi.get_vertices
text: voronoi.get_vertices(diagram: userdata): table Returns all unique Voronoi vertices as { x, y } point tables. Edge vertex indices refer to this array. diagram — Generated diagram context. vertices — Array of point tables.

title: voronoi.relax
text: voronoi.relax(diagram: userdata) Moves every input point toward the average of its site and cell vertices, then regenerates the diagram. diagram — Generated diagram context.

title: gamepush.core.platform API
text: megalanthus / defold-gamepush · platform gamepush.core.platform GamePush platform: which platform the game runs on, its capabilities and calls into its native SDK.

title: gamepush.core.platform.call_native_sdk
text: call_native_sdk(method: string, parameters?: unknown, callback?: (result: unknown) => void): unknown Calls a method of the platform's native SDK, or reads one of its objects or fields. Raises when the method is not a non-empty string. An error comes back as { error = "..." }. method — The dotted path to the method, object or field, for example "feedback.canReview". var=path saves the result in a JS variable, var:method calls a method of a saved object. parameters — The method's argument, or a list of its arguments. Functions cannot be passed. Ignored when the path names an object or a field. callback — Receives the result when the method returns a promise. The result, or nothing when a callback is given.

title: minit API
text: Minit-Games / minit-defold minit Publishes an HTML5 game to the Minit platform. Each call talks to the window.minit runtime the host injects into the page, through html5.run. Call loading_done once the game is ready to show and report_result once when it ends. Outside an HTML5 build every call prints or returns a fixed result, so each is safe to call anywhere. ReportResultOptions

title: minit.get_config_value
text: get_config_value(key: string, default_value?: string): string Reads a game config value from the page URL's query parameters (?difficulty=hard). Declare each key the game reads in the config array of its meta.json. The key userData is reserved and always returns the default. Outside an HTML5 build it returns the default. key — The query parameter to read. default_value — The value returned when the key is absent or reserved. Defaults to "". Upstream names this parameter default.

title: minit.get_device_tier
text: get_device_tier(): "low" | "medium" | "high" | "unknown" Returns the player's device tier. ?deviceTier= set to low, medium, high or unknown wins; next comes the host's window.minit.deviceTier when it is one of the four; otherwise it returns "unknown", which is also its result outside an HTML5 build.

title: minit.get_motion_quality
text: get_motion_quality(): "full" | "reduced" Returns the effects quality to run at. ?motionQuality=full or ?motionQuality=reduced wins; next comes the host's window.minit.motionQuality when it is one of the two; otherwise it returns "reduced" when prefers_reduced_motion returns true, else "full". Outside an HTML5 build it returns "full".

title: minit.get_user_data
text: get_user_data(): string | undefined Returns this player's single stored slot, which report_result writes through its user_data option. Reads the host's window.minit.userData, else the ?userData= URL parameter when the host injected none, else returns undefined. A stored empty value returns "", distinct from undefined. Outside an HTML5 build it returns undefined.

title: minit.is_viewable
text: is_viewable(): boolean Returns whether the game is visible to the player right now: the host's window.minit.isViewable() when it has one, else whether document.visibilityState is visible. It reads the value again on every call. Outside an HTML5 build it returns true.

title: minit.loading_done
text: loading_done() Signals the host that the game is booted and ready to show. The host keeps the game hidden until this is called. Outside an HTML5 build it prints loadingDone.

title: minit.on_viewable_change
text: on_viewable_change(fn: (viewable: boolean) => void): () => void Calls fn each time the game's viewability changes, starting from its value at subscribe time, and returns a function that unsubscribes fn. Lua polls the value every 0.25 s, so a change arrives up to about 250 ms late. Subscribing the same fn again returns its existing unsubscribe, and unsubscribing twice is safe. An error fn raises is printed and does not stop the other subscribers. The poll runs on a timer that belongs to the script that subscribed last and stops with it, so subscribe from a script that outlives the subscription and unsubscribe in its final. Outside an HTML5 build fn is never called and the returned function does nothing. fn — Gets true when the game becomes viewable and false when it stops.

title: minit.prefers_reduced_motion
text: prefers_reduced_motion(): boolean Returns whether the player or the operating system prefers reduced motion. ?reducedMotion=1 or ?reducedMotion=true forces true and ?reducedMotion=0 or ?reducedMotion=false forces false; next comes the host's window.minit.prefersReducedMotion when it is a boolean; otherwise it returns whether the browser matches the prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query, or false when the browser cannot tell. Outside an HTML5 build it returns false.

title: minit.report_result
text: report_result(score: number | string, options?: ReportResultOptions) Submits the game's final result. Call it exactly once, when the game ends: the host ignores a repeat call, and the SDK warns about it. A higher score ranks better by default. For a time-sorted game (resultSorting fastestTime or slowestTime in meta.json) the score is in seconds, never milliseconds, and fractions are allowed. Outside an HTML5 build it prints the score. score — The result, as a number or a string. options — The caption, delay and stored slot to send with the result.

title: minit.ReportResultOptions.delay
text: delay?: number How many milliseconds the host waits before showing the result screen.

title: minit.ReportResultOptions.flavor_text
text: flavor_text?: string A short caption for the host's result screen and feed. Past 64 characters, counted as a JS string so an emoji counts 2, the SDK warns and the platform cuts it to 64.

title: minit.ReportResultOptions.user_data
text: user_data?: string Writes this player's single stored slot, which get_user_data reads back. Omit it to leave the slot unchanged; "" is a valid write.

title: minit.should_show_tutorial
text: should_show_tutorial(): boolean Returns whether to run the first-play tutorial. ?tutorial=1 or ?tutorial=true forces it on and ?tutorial=0 or ?tutorial=false forces it off; otherwise it returns false only when the host reports that the player has played the game before. Outside an HTML5 build it returns true.

title: mpeg.gui_video API
text: Morgerion / defold-mpeg · gui_video mpeg.gui_video Plays an MPEG1 or AV1 video on a GUI box node, optionally with its sound. It is built on the mpeg native extension. Call init from the GUI script's init, update from its update and final from its final, passing the script's self: the module keeps each player on it. Map /mpeg/video_yuv.material in the GUI scene as video_yuv to convert frames on the GPU instead of the CPU. CommonOptions

title: mpeg.gui_video.are_finished

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.blend_frames

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.field

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.gain

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.gui_url

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.loop

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.max_lag

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.node

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.playback_fps

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.sound_resource
text: sound_resource?: string | Hash The sound resource the sound component plays. Its data is replaced with the decoded track. Defaults to /mpeg/video_sound.wavc; two videos with sound at once each need their own copy.

title: mpeg.gui_video.CommonOptions.texture_key

It shows the first frame at once and, with sound, decodes the whole audio track and starts it. Throws when the video, its material or its node cannot be used. self — The GUI script's self, which holds the player. options — The node, the video and how to play it.

title: mpeg.gui_video.update
text: update(self: object, dt: number, field?: string) Advance one video player. It moves by dt scaled by its playback speed or, while its sound plays, to the sound's position. A non-looping video that ends with stop_on_last_frame keeps its last frame and is finished. self — The GUI script's self. dt — The game frame's time step, in seconds. field — The player's field. Defaults to the single-video field.

title: mpeg.close
text: mpeg.close(handle: number) Close an opened video. This will release an memory allocated by the videoplayer. handle — The video handle to close.

title: mpeg.decode_audio
text: mpeg.decode_audio(video: buffer | string): LuaMultiReturn<[string, table | string]> Decode the whole MPEG audio track of a video, or of an audio-only MPEG file, into a 16-bit stereo PCM WAV file in memory, ready for resource.set_sound() or resource.create_sound_data(). Uses its own decoder, so an opened video handle is not affected. video — The video data as a buffer or string. wav — The WAV file, or nil if the video has no audio track. info — Table with samplerate, channels, duration (exact, in seconds) and decode_ms, or an error message if wav is nil.

title: mpeg.decode
text: mpeg.decode(handle: number, seconds: number): boolean Advance the internal timer by seconds and decode video/audio up to this time. handle — The video handle to decode. seconds — Number of seconds to advance. has_new_frame — Returns true if decode produced at least one new video frame.

title: mpeg.get_frame_serial
text: mpeg.get_frame_serial(handle: number): number Get a monotonically increasing serial number for decoded video frames. handle — The video handle to query. serial — The serial number of the latest decoded frame.

title: mpeg.get_frame
text: mpeg.get_frame(handle: number): buffer Get the video frame buffer. The video frame buffer will be updated when decode() is called and enough data has been decoded to produce a frame. handle — The video handle to get frame buffer for. frame — The decoded video frame buffer or nil if no video frame buffer is available. The ownership of the buffer is not transferred to the caller.

title: mpeg.get_info
text: mpeg.get_info(handle: number): table Get information about an opened video. handle — The video to get info for. info — Video information

title: mpeg.get_time
text: mpeg.get_time(handle: number): number Get the current playback time of a video. Same as get_info().time, without creating a table. handle — The video handle to query. time — Current playback time in seconds.

title: mpeg.open
text: mpeg.open(video: buffer | string, options: table): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Open a video for decoding. MPEG1 (.mpg) or AV1 in an IVF file (.ivf), recognized by its header. video — The video data as a buffer or string. Ownership of the buffer is not transferred. options — Optional video settings. loop loops the video. format is "rgb" (default, frames converted to RGB on the CPU) or "yuv" (packed YUV planes for the video_yuv shader). decode_ahead (AV1, default true) decodes on a worker thread into a queue. threads (AV1) sets the decoder threads, by default 1 up to 1080p, 2 up to 1440p and 4 above. audio (MPEG1) makes this decoder decode the audio track too, but the samples are not played - use decode_audio() and a sound component for sound. handle — Returns video handle. Use in subsequent calls. err — Error message if video failed to open.

title: mpeg.rewind
text: mpeg.rewind(handle: number) Rewind video to the beginning. handle — The video handle to rewind.

title: mpeg.seek
text: mpeg.seek(handle: number, time: number, seek_exact: boolean) Seek to the specified time. Will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. handle — The video handle to seek on. time — Time to seek to. seek_exact — If value is true the function will seek to the exact time, otherwise it will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. Exact seeking can be slow, because all frames up to the seeked one have to be decoded on top of the previous intra frame. Defaults to false.

title: mpeg.write
text: mpeg.write(handle: number, data: string): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Write data to the internal stream buffer of a video started with stream(). Use the streaming_buffer_bytes_remaining and streaming_buffer_capacity to determine how much data to write to the buffer. handle — The video handle to write to. data — Bytes with stream data. bytes_written — The number of written bytes or nil if writing failed. error — Error message if writing failed for some reason.

title: rtcapture API
text: Morgerion / defold-rtcapture rtcapture Capture of arbitrary render targets and of the default framebuffer. Reads COLOR0 of a render target given by a render script, or the screen itself, and returns raw RGB8/RGBA8 pixels as a Defold buffer, or a PNG or JPEG in memory or written to a file. Binding and readback use the portable DMSDK graphics API only, with no backend specific code.

title: rtcapture.cancel_all
text: rtcapture.cancel_all(): number Drop every pending capture request. No callbacks are invoked. count — How many requests were dropped.

title: rtcapture.cancel
text: rtcapture.cancel(request_id: number): boolean Drop a pending capture request. Its callback is never invoked, because cancelling was the caller's own decision. Everything the request owned is released immediately. request_id — The id returned by capture. cancelled — True when a pending request with that id was found and removed.

title: rtcapture.capture_sync
text: rtcapture.capture_sync(target: number, options: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Read the given target immediately instead of waiting for post render. Takes the same options as capture and returns the same result table, only as a direct return value. Use it where no further post render will happen - the save written from the final() of a game script when the window is closing is the case this exists for, since a queued request there would never run. A render target still has to be captured from the render script that owns it and in the frame it was drawn; the screen framebuffer can be captured from anywhere. target — The value returned by render.render_target(), or rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT. options — The same options capture accepts. result — The same result table capture passes to its callback, or nil when the request was rejected outright. error — Error code when the request was rejected, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the request was rejected, otherwise nil.

title: rtcapture.capture
text: rtcapture.capture(target: number, options: table, callback: function): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string, string]> Queue a readback of the given render target. The readback runs in the post-render phase of the current frame, so call this from the render script that owns the target and in the same frame the target was drawn. The extension does not own the target and cannot detect that it was deleted or resized after the request. target — The value returned by render.render_target(), or rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT for the main screen framebuffer. The screen can be captured from any script; a render target must come from the render script that owns it. options — format - "raw" (default) for pixels in a Defold buffer, "hold" to keep the pixels inside the extension and get a frame_id for encode, "png" or "jpeg". Use "hold" to spread a capture over two frames: the frame that reads pays for the readback only, and the downscale and the encoding happen on the next frame, without a multi megabyte buffer travelling through Lua in between. max_width - target width of the resulting image. The extension picks the integer box filter factor itself, because only it knows the size of the region it read. Rounding is down, with a minimum of 1, so the result can be slightly wider than asked: 3840 with max_width = 600 gives 640. Without this option the image keeps the size of the region that was read. path - encoded formats only. When given, the image is written to that file and is not copied into a Lua string. The file is written through path .. ".tmp" and only then replaces the destination. channels - 4 for RGBA8 or 3 for RGB8 with alpha discarded. Defaults to 4, or to 3 for JPEG, which cannot store alpha anyway. PNG keeps alpha losslessly for four channels and writes a true 24bpp PNG for three. quality - JPEG only, 1..100, default 85. subsampling - JPEG only, "444", "422" or "420", default "420". Use "444" for text and interface, where chroma subsampling produces coloured fringes. progressive - JPEG only, default false. Encodes noticeably slower and decodes slower, with little size benefit for local previews. optimize - JPEG only, default false. Optimized Huffman tables cost encoding time. alpha_mode - JPEG from four channels. "discard" (default) ignores alpha, so transparent areas keep whatever colour they hold. "composite" blends onto background first. background - table with r, g, b in 0..255, used by alpha_mode = "composite". Defaults to black. x, y, width, height - rectangle to read, with the origin in the top left corner of the target, matching the orientation of the returned image. x and y default to 0; width and height default to the rest of the target. A rectangle that leaves the target is rejected, never clamped. flip_y - flip rows vertically, false by default. The default was measured: on the OpenGL adapter ReadPixels already returns top-down rows. tag - any Lua value, returned unchanged in the result so a caller can correlate the result with its own request. callback — Called from post-render with one result table. request_id — Monotonic id of the accepted request, or nil when the request was rejected. error — Error code when the request was rejected, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the request was rejected, otherwise nil.

title: rtcapture.debug_target
text: rtcapture.debug_target(target: number, label?: string): table Identify an arbitrary render target without reading its pixels. Call it from the render script that owns the target, in the same frame, so the handle is guaranteed to be alive. target — The value returned by render.render_target(). label — Name used in the log line so several targets can be told apart. info — Contains label, handle, handle_hex, color0_width, color0_height and adapter.

title: rtcapture.decode_jpeg
text: rtcapture.decode_jpeg(data: string, options?: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Decode JPEG bytes into a Defold buffer. Synchronous, and callable from any script. The header is validated before anything is allocated dimensions, data precision and colour space are checked first, and images above 64 million pixels are refused. JPEG stores no alpha, so a four channel result is always fully opaque. data — Binary JPEG data. options — channels - 4 for RGBA8 (default) or 3 for RGB8. image — Contains width, height, channels, byte_size, decode_ms and buffer, a Defold buffer whose single stream is rgba of UINT8 x4, or rgb of UINT8 x3. nil when decoding failed. error — Error code when decoding failed, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when decoding failed, otherwise nil.

title: rtcapture.encode
text: rtcapture.encode(frame_id: number, options: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Downscale and encode a frame that a format = "hold" capture left inside the extension. This is the second phase of a capture spread over two frames. The frame stays held after encoding, so the same shot can be encoded more than once - to compare formats, for example - and is freed by release_frame. Compositing is not available here the held pixels have already been converted, so alpha_mode = "composite" only works at capture time. frame_id — The frame_id from the result of the held capture. options — format (required, "png" or "jpeg"), path, max_width, quality, subsampling, progressive, optimize and tag - the same meaning they have in capture. result — The same result table shape as capture, with downscale_ms, encode_ms, write_ms and total_ms filled for this phase. nil when the call was rejected. error — ERR_NO_HELD_FRAME when no frame with that id is held, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the call was rejected, otherwise nil.

title: rtcapture.get_capabilities
text: rtcapture.get_capabilities(): table Report what the extension can currently do on the installed graphics adapter. Only verified capabilities are listed; stages that are not implemented yet do not appear as fields. capabilities — Contains available, adapter ("opengl", "vulkan", "directx", ...) and debug_target.

title: rtcapture.get_render_target_size
text: rtcapture.get_render_target_size(target: number): LuaMultiReturn<[number, number]> Report the size of the COLOR0 attachment of the given render target, so calling code can compute a rectangle without repeating the parameters the render script created the target with. target — The value returned by render.render_target().

title: rtcapture.invalidate_render_targets
text: rtcapture.invalidate_render_targets(): number Declare that every render target handed to the extension so far is gone. Call this right after recreating render targets, for example when the window was resized. The extension cannot detect this on its own - the public DMSDK has no way to test whether a handle is still alive. Requests made before the call stay in the queue and complete with ERR_RENDER_TARGET_DESTROYED rather than reading through a dead handle, so every accepted request still gets exactly one answer. Requests for rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT are unaffected. affected — How many pending requests will now fail.

title: rtcapture.release_frame
text: rtcapture.release_frame(frame_id?: number): boolean Free the frame held by a format = "hold" capture. Call it once the frame has been encoded, or when the encoding is abandoned - otherwise a full screen frame stays in the memory of the extension until the next held capture replaces it. Only one frame is held at a time. frame_id — The id to free. Without it the currently held frame is freed, whatever its id. released — True when a frame was actually freed.

title: rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT
text: rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT Pass as the capture target to read the main screen framebuffer instead of a render target. Its value is 0, the same one render.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT uses in a render script.

title: rtcapture.set_debug_logging
text: rtcapture.set_debug_logging(enabled: boolean) Enable the detailed capture log. Off by default. The log line reports the raw first pixel before conversion, the viewport before and after the readback, and per stage timings.
