title: flow.layout API
text: Pause-Games / flow · layout flow.layout Flow's flexbox layout pass, which computes the position and size of every element in a tree.

title: flow.layout.compute
text: compute(node: Flow_Element, x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number) Compute layout for a node tree. Writes layout.x/y/w/h to every node in the tree recursively, using bottom-left origin coordinates. Algorithm: 1. Measure all regular (non-overlay) children to sum fixed sizes and flex_grow weights. 2. Distribute remaining free space according to justify_content. 3. Place each child along the main axis, applying align_items / align_self on the cross axis. 4. Recurse into each child. 5. Layout overlay children (popup, bottom_sheet) at full parent bounds as a final pass. node — The root element to compute layout for x — Left edge of the available area in layout space (px) y — Bottom edge of the available area in layout space (px) w — Available width in pixels h — Available height in pixels

title: flow.navigation.gui API
text: Pause-Games / flow · gui flow.navigation.gui The gui_script adapter that renders the current Flow screen and animates transitions between screens.

title: flow.navigation.gui.build_tree
text: build_tree(adapter: LuaTable): Flow_Element | undefined Build (or rebuild) the UI element tree for the current navigation state. When a transition is active, renders both from and to trees and applies alpha or offset_x according to the transition type and eased progress. Transition types: "fade" — cross-fade: from_tree.alpha fades out, to_tree.alpha fades in "slide_left" — to slides in from the right: from moves left, to comes from right "slide_right" — to slides in from the left: from moves right, to comes from left Returns nil and clears adapter.tree when the stack is empty. adapter — The adapter instance The UI tree to pass to the renderer

title: flow.navigation.gui.clear_rebuild_flag
text: clear_rebuild_flag(adapter: LuaTable) Clear the rebuild flag. Called after build_tree() has been invoked. adapter — The adapter instance

title: flow.navigation.gui.destroy
text: destroy(adapter: LuaTable) Remove all navigation listeners and clean up the adapter. Call this in gui_script final() to prevent leaking event handlers. adapter — The adapter instance created by M.new()

title: flow.navigation.gui.invalidate
text: invalidate(adapter: LuaTable) Invalidate the adapter so the next build_tree() call regenerates the tree. adapter — The adapter instance

title: flow.navigation.gui.needs_rebuild
text: needs_rebuild(adapter: LuaTable): boolean Return true when the adapter's tree needs to be rebuilt. adapter — The adapter instance True when adapter.needs_rebuild is set

title: flow.navigation.gui.new
text: new(navigation: Flow_Navigation): LuaTable Create a new GUI adapter instance bound to the given navigation router. Registers listeners for "changed", "transition_begin", and "transition_complete" so the adapter stays in sync with navigation state automatically. navigation — The navigation facade (flow/navigation/init.lua) The adapter object with all M methods mixed in

title: flow.navigation.gui.save_scroll_state
text: save_scroll_state(adapter: LuaTable, tree: Flow_Element, options?: LuaTable | undefined) Save the current scroll offsets from a UI tree into the navigation params. Typically called just before a tree rebuild so that scroll position is preserved. adapter — The adapter instance tree — The UI tree to extract scroll state from options — Optional {screen_id=...} to target a specific screen

title: flow.navigation.gui.update
text: update(adapter: LuaTable, dt: number): boolean Advance the active transition by dt seconds. Updates transition.progress and requests an adapter rebuild each frame. When progress reaches 1.0, calls navigation.complete_transition() to signal that the transition is done and clear the busy flag. adapter — The adapter instance dt — Delta time in seconds since the last frame True when the transition just completed this frame

title: flow.navigation.messages API
text: Pause-Games / flow · messages flow.navigation.messages Routes Flow's navigation messages, such as push, pop and replace, to the navigation stack.

title: flow.navigation.messages.on_message
text: on_message(message_id: Hash | string, message?: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable): boolean Map of all supported message ids keyed by operation name. Message id for navigation.push — payload: {id, params?, options?} Message id for navigation.pop — payload: {result?, options?} Message id for navigation.replace — payload: {id, params?, options?} Message id for navigation.reset — payload: {id, params?, options?} Message id for navigation.back — payload: {result?, options?} Message id for navigation.invalidate — no payload required Handle an incoming Defold message and dispatch it to the navigation module. Returns true when the message was a recognized navigation message and was handled. Returns false for all other messages so callers can chain additional handlers. Supported message payloads: PUSH/REPLACE/RESET: { id = "screen_id", params = {}, options = {} } POP/BACK: { result = {}, options = {} } INVALIDATE: no payload needed message_id — The incoming Defold message id hash, or raw string in test environments message — The incoming Defold message payload True when the message was handled by navigation

title: flow.navigation.proxy API
text: Pause-Games / flow · proxy flow.navigation.proxy Loads and enables each Flow screen's collection proxy as the navigation stack changes.

title: flow.navigation.proxy.attach
text: attach(nav?: Flow_Navigation | undefined, opts?: Flow_ProxyAttachOptions | undefined): LuaTable Attach the collection proxy runtime to a navigation instance. Registers "preload" and "changed" event listeners so proxies are managed automatically as screens are navigated. When opts.sync_existing is true (the default), immediately preloads all already-registered screens with preload=true, and syncs the current active proxy if a screen is already on the stack. nav — The navigation module; defaults to flow/navigation/init opts — Options overriding DEFAULTS The runtime instance (call :detach() to clean up)

title: flow.navigation.proxy.detach
text: detach(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable) Remove all navigation event listeners and clean up the runtime. Call this in your bootstrap script's final() function to prevent leaked listeners after the script is destroyed. self — The runtime instance created by M.attach()

title: flow.navigation.runtime API
text: Pause-Games / flow · runtime flow.navigation.runtime Flow navigation for a plain .script, such as a gameplay controller with a collection proxy.

title: flow.navigation.runtime.final
text: final(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable) Clean up the navigation runtime for a non-GUI script. Detaches the proxy runtime (if any) to remove event listeners. Call this from the .script final() lifecycle function. self — The .script self table initialized by M.init()

title: flow.navigation.runtime.init
text: init(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, config?: Flow_RuntimeConfig): LuaTable Initialize navigation for a non-GUI script. Registers screens, optionally attaches the collection proxy runtime, and navigates to the initial screen if specified. Stores state in self.navigation and self.navigation_runtime so it can be accessed from on_message() and cleaned up in final(). self — The .script self table config — Configuration options The navigation_runtime state table stored on self

title: flow.navigation.runtime.on_message
text: on_message(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, message_id: Hash | string, message?: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, sender?: Url): boolean Handle an incoming Defold message and route it to navigation. Delegates to navigation_messages.on_message() which dispatches push/pop/replace/reset/back/invalidate messages. Returns true when the message was consumed by navigation. self — The .script self table message_id — The incoming message id hash, or raw string in test environments message — The incoming message payload sender — The sender's msg.url() (unused, for Defold API compat) True when the message was handled by navigation

title: flow.ui API
text: Pause-Games / flow · ui flow.ui Flow's gui_script renderer: mounts onto a script's self, renders an element tree to runtime GUI nodes and routes input to it.

title: flow.ui._set_layout_space_unsafe
text: set_layout_space_unsafe(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, space: string) Internal: switch between "window" and "gui" layout spaces. In "window" mode, layout is computed in physical pixels and nodes are scaled back to GUI space via scale_x/scale_y. This gives pixel-perfect rendering on high-DPI displays. Not intended for direct consumer use. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer space — "window" for physical pixels, anything else for GUI units

title: flow.ui.get_size
text: get_size(): LuaMultiReturn<[number, number]> Return the logical GUI display size (same as the [display] settings). Exposed on the module so external code can query the design resolution. Logical display width in pixels Logical display height in pixels

title: flow.ui.hit_test
text: hit_test(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, x: number, y: number): Flow_Element | undefined ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Perform a point hit-test against the current element tree. Coordinates must be in GUI space (as received from on_input action.x/y). Returns the deepest hittable element whose layout bounds contain the point, or nil if nothing was hit. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer x — X coordinate in GUI space y — Y coordinate in GUI space The hit element, or nil

title: flow.ui.mount
text: mount(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, opts?: Flow_MountOptions) Initialize the renderer state on a gui_script self table. Must be called once in gui_script init() before any other ui calls. Creates self.ui with an empty node cache, redraw flag, and debug toggle. self — The gui_script self table to mount onto opts — Options table

title: flow.ui.on_input
text: on_input(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, action_id: Hash | undefined, action: { x?: number; y?: number; pressed?: boolean; released?: boolean }): boolean Route a Defold input action to the appropriate element. Handles touch press/move/release, scroll wheel, and drag gestures. Call this from gui_script on_input(); returns true if the input was consumed. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer action_id — The Defold action id hash (e.g. hash("touch")) action — The Defold action table with x, y, pressed, released fields True if the input was consumed and should not propagate

title: flow.ui.register
text: register(type_name: string, def: LuaTable): LuaTable Register a custom element type definition. Every element type string ("box", "text", "button", etc.) must be registered before it can appear in a UI tree. The definition describes how to create, update, and interact with the corresponding Defold GUI node. Required fields in def: create_node(el) -> userdata — creates and returns a new gui node Optional fields in def: apply(self, el, node, alpha) — update node visuals each frame is_visible(el) -> boolean — custom visibility check is_hittable(el) -> boolean — custom hit-test eligibility is_scroll_container -> boolean — marks element as scroll root clips_children -> boolean — node is used as parent for children capture_descendant_hits -> boolean — returns self instead of child on hit is_backdrop_click_target -> boolean — receives backdrop click events get_text_anchor(el) -> "left"|"center"|"right" — text pivot anchor for positioning hover_begin(self, el, deps) — called when pointer enters element hover_end(self, el, deps) — called when pointer leaves element press_begin(self, el, deps) — called when element is pressed press_update(self, el, is_hot, deps) — called while dragging over element press_end(self, el, activated, deps) — called on release on_wheel(self, el, delta, deps) — called on mouse wheel on_drag_start(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called when drag begins on_drag_move(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called each drag frame on_drag_end(self, el, action, t, deps) — called when drag ends update_anim(el, dt, deps) -> bool,bool — per-frame animation tick render_extras(self, el, prefix, alpha, deps) — render auxiliary nodes collect_extra_keys(el, prefix, keys, deps) — declare extra cached node keys get_child_extra_offset_y(el) -> number — additional Y offset for children type_name — The element type string (e.g. "box", "scroll") def — Renderer definition table; must contain create_node The registered def, same reference as the argument

title: flow.ui.render_if_size_changed
text: render_if_size_changed(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, tree?: Flow_Element | undefined): boolean Re-render only if the display size has changed since the last render pass. Cheaper than M.update() — no redraw-flag check, just a size comparison. Returns true when a re-render was performed. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer tree — The element tree to render; falls back to self.ui.tree True if a re-render was performed

title: flow.ui.render
text: render(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, tree: Flow_Element, w?: number | undefined, h?: number | undefined) Force a full layout + render pass using the given tree and dimensions. Bypasses redraw gating — always re-computes and re-applies all nodes. Prefer M.update() for normal frame rendering; use M.render() when you need to guarantee an immediate re-render (e.g. after a window resize event detected in on_input). self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer tree — The element tree to render w — Available width in pixels (nil/0 = use GUI size) h — Available height in pixels (nil/0 = use GUI size)

title: flow.ui.request_redraw
text: request_redraw(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable) Request a renderer redraw so the next M.update() call triggers a full re-render. Call this whenever the data driving the UI tree changes and you want the screen to reflect the new state immediately. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer

title: flow.ui.request_tree_redraw
text: request_tree_redraw(tree?: Flow_Element | undefined) Request a redraw for an element tree so renderer_core.update() re-renders it. Use this when you hold a reference to a tree and want to force a re-layout without going through the full renderer self table. tree — The root element to flag for redraw; no-op if nil

title: flow.ui.set_debug
text: set_debug(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, enabled: boolean): boolean Enable or disable debug logging for input and hit-testing. When enabled, every touch press emits debug logs through flow.log under the ui.input context. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer enabled — True to enable debug output, false to disable The new debug state

title: flow.ui.update_animations
text: update_animations(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, dt: number): boolean ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Advance all per-element animations by one frame (dt seconds). Iterates the current tree and calls each element's update_anim handler. Requests a redraw when at least one element is still animating. Call this every frame from gui_script update() before M.update(). self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer dt — Delta time in seconds since the last frame True if at least one animation is still running

title: flow.ui.update
text: update(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, tree?: Flow_Element | undefined): boolean Update the renderer: re-layout and re-apply all nodes if the tree or display size has changed since the last frame. Internally delegates to renderer_core.update() with the full dependency bundle. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer tree — The element tree to render; may be nil (no-op) True if a re-render was performed this frame

title: fake_real_glass API
text: paweljarosz / defold-fake-real-glass fake_real_glass A multipass glass rendering library for Defold with screen-space double refraction, thickness-based distortion, optional color absorption and local cubemap reflection probes. Supports lighting from Defold light components and configurable reflection modes that update probes every frame, capture once or use pre-rendered cubemaps. Includes a reusable Lua render module, glass materials and example scenes with glass spheres, a wine glass and planar mirror reflections. Integrates with custom render pipelines and requires Defold 1.14.0 or newer. FakeRealGlassProbeModeTable FakeRealGlassConstantBuffer FakeRealGlassProbeFace FakeRealGlassOptions FakeRealGlassState FakeRealGlassMessage FakeRealGlassDrawParams

title: fake_real_glass.create
text: create(options?: FakeRealGlassOptions): FakeRealGlassState Create the per-render-script state for the fake glass pipeline. This allocates Lua-side state immediately. Screen-sized render targets are created by resize() and recreated automatically when sizes change. The returned table is intended to be stored by one render script instance. It tracks probe settings, render targets, and the constant buffer used when drawing visible glass objects. options — Optional module setup overrides for tags, probe defaults, and materials.

title: fake_real_glass.draw
text: draw(glass: FakeRealGlassState | undefined, params: FakeRealGlassDrawParams) Run the fake glass passes for the current frame. The host render script should: 1. draw its normal opaque world to the default framebuffer 2. call this function before GUI rendering This function may: 1. re-render the six probe faces 2. capture the opaque scene into scene_rt 3. capture the glass back faces into backface_rt 4. draw the visible front-face glass to the default framebuffer glass — Module state previously returned by create(). params — Per-frame camera, target-size, clear-buffer, and world-redraw inputs.

title: pigeon.send_to
text: send_to(url: Url | string | hash | Opaque<"userdata">, message_id: MessageId, message?: LuaTable): boolean Equivalent to Defold built-in msg.post. Sends a message of given message_id with an optional data in message table to a specified url. Accepts the same target forms as msg.post: a url userdata, a url-like string (e.g. "/gui#hud" or "#fragment"), or a hash game object id (e.g. the id returned by factory.create or go.get_id). Additionally, Pigeon checks in runtime if message is correct if defined. url — @Target's url, url-like string, or game object hash id. message_id — @Defold message_id string or hashed. It will be prehashed anyway. message — @Optional message table to check. @True if data is correct and send succesfully, false otherwise.

title: pigeon.send
text: send(message_id: MessageId, message?: LuaTable): boolean Send a message of given message_id with given message table to all subscribed subscribers. Additionally, Pigeon checks in runtime if message is correct if defined. If the message has a hook attached, it will be called immediately. message_id — @Defold message_id string or hashed. It will be prehashed anyway. message — @Optional definition message table to check before sending. @True if data is correct and send succesfully, false otherwise.

Can be a single message as string or hash or a table containing messages as strings or hashes. callback — @Optional callback function to be called everytime, when sending subscribed message(s). text: bridge.multiplayer.on(event_name: string, callback: function) Subscribe to multiplayer events. Use the bridge.EVENT_NAME.MULTIPLAYER constants. The callback receives: multiplayer_state_changed - state string (see bridge.MULTIPLAYER_STATE) multiplayer_room_left - reason string (see bridge.ROOM_LEAVE_REASON) multiplayer_room_updated - room table multiplayer_player_joined - player table multiplayer_player_left - player table multiplayer_player_updated - player table multiplayer_host_changed - new host player table or nil multiplayer_message_received - message table { type, data, from } multiplayer_sync_state_received - world table (see set_sync_state) callback — function(, data)

It arrives in the multiplayer_message_received event as { type, data, from }. data — Optional message data (any JSON-compatible value). options — Optional { to }, where to is "all", "others" (default), "host" (see bridge.MULTIPLAYER_TARGET), a player id or a table of player ids.

title: bridge.multiplayer.set_sync_state
text: bridge.multiplayer.set_sync_state(state: table) Set the local game world. When the room is entered with syncState, the host sends its world to the other players up to updatesPerSecond times a second (1-10, default 10) and they get it in the multiplayer_sync_state_received event. The server keeps the last world - a new host gets it in the same event and goes on from it. Works outside a room too, e.g. to set the starting world before create_room. Reset to an empty table when the room is left. state — The whole world (JSON-compatible), up to 64 KB.

text: s-kania / def-behavior-tree def_behavior_tree Event-driven behavior trees for NPC logic. Register node templates once with registerTemplates, create a tree over a payload with new, and call run: each node moves on only when the one before it reports success or failure, and a tree can start from any node id, so an active node saved with a game can be resumed on load. title: def_behavior_tree.new
text:
new

(config: { tree_name: string; payload: P; rng?: (this: void, range_start: number, range_end: number) => number; }): BehaviorTree

Creates a tree that runs a registered tree template over a payload. Register the templates with registerTemplates first. config — tree_name names a tree under the templates' TREES, payload is passed to every task callback, and rng returns a whole number between its two arguments for Random and RandomWithChances; it defaults to math.random. new(config: { tree_name: string; payload?: undefined; rng?: (this: void, range_start: number, range_end: number) => number; }): BehaviorTree Creates a tree that runs a registered tree template with no payload, so its task callbacks receive undefined. Register the templates with registerTemplates first. config — tree_name names a tree under the templates' TREES, and rng returns a whole number between its two arguments for Random and RandomWithChances; it defaults to math.random.

title: astar.set_costs
text: astar.set_costs(costs: table, map_id[optional]: number) Set costs for walkable tiles on your world table. This table keys determine the walkable area. Table's sum must be the astar.DIRECTION_FOUR or astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT. costs — Table of costs for directions. map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0.

title: astar.set_map
text: astar.set_map(world: table, map_id[optional]: number) Set your map data. Setting new map data reset the current cache. world — Your tilemap data. Keep it simple as much as you can. map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0.

title: astar.setup
text: astar.setup(map_width: number, map_height: number, direction: number, allocate: number, typical_adjacent: number, cache[optional]: boolean, use_zero[optional]: boolean, map_vflip[optional]: boolean, map_id[optional]: number) Initial setup. You have to setup the astar before calling any other methods. map_width — Width of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap. map_height — Height of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap. direction — Movement direction (astar.DIRECTION_FOUR or astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT) astar.DIRECTION_FOUR - on a square grid that allows 4 directions of movement using Manhattan distance. astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT - on a square grid that allows 8 directions of movement using Euclidean distance. allocate — How many states should be internally allocated at a time. This can be hard to get correct. The higher the value, the more memory Patfinder will use. If you have a small map (a few thousand states?) it may make sense to pass in the maximum value. This will cache everything, and MicroPather will only need one main memory allocation. For a chess board, allocate would be set to 8x8 (64) If your map is large, something like 1/4 the number of possible states is good. If your state space is huge, use a multiple (5-10x) of the normal path. "Occasionally" call astar.reset_cache() to free unused memory. typical_adjacent — Used to determine cache size. The typical number of adjacent states to a given state. (On a chessboard, 8.) Higher values use a little more memory. cache[optional] — Turn on path caching. Uses more memory (yet again) but at a huge speed advantage if you may call the pather with the same path or sub-path, which is common for pathing over maps in games. Default is true use_zero[optional] — Toggle start index 0 or 1 for tables and tile positions. Also you can set it by call astar.use_zero(). Default is false map_vflip[optional] — Flips the map vertically. This doesn't flip the coordinates. Also you can set it by call astar.map_vflip(). Default is false map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0.

title: astar.solve_near
text: astar.solve_near(start_x: number, start_y: number, max_cost: number, map_id[optional]: number): LuaMultiReturn<[number, number, table]> Finds the neighbours according to a given cost. start_x — Start tile X. start_y — Start tile Y. max_cost — Maximum cost for finding neighbours. map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0. near_result — Result code (astar.SOLVED, astar.NO_SOLUTION, astar.START_END_SAME). near_size — Size of the found neighbours. nears — Table with x and y coordinates. First value is the given start point.

title: astar.solve
text: astar.solve(start_x: number, start_y: number, end_x: number, end_y: number, map_id[optional]: number): LuaMultiReturn<[number, number, number, table]> Solves the path. start_x — Start tile X. start_y — Start tile Y. end_x — End tile X. end_y — End tile Y. map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0. result — Result code (astar.SOLVED, astar.NO_SOLUTION, astar.START_END_SAME). size — Size of the path. total_cost — Total cost of the path. path — Table with x and y coordinates. First value is the given start point.

title: water API
text: selimanac / defold-stylized-water-shader water A stylized water shader: animated wave surfaces, foam, sparkles, refraction and reflection, set through shader constants. A game object script calls init once with the camera, sun and water objects, then update(dt) and update_camera() every frame. The render script calls render_init(self) at the end of its init, after which self.predicates holds the water predicate, and render_update(self, state, self.predicates, draw_options_world) in its update (see water/render/water.render_script). The shader needs exclude_gles_sm100 = 1 under [shader] in game.project. Every setter writes a shader constant the next render_update uploads, and every getter returns the stored values as separate values. RenderScriptSelf Predicates RenderState

title: water.render_init
text: render_init(self: RenderScriptSelf) Adds the water predicate to self.predicates, creates the scene render target at self.state.width by self.state.height with a color and a depth buffer, and creates the two constant buffers render_update draws with, all stored on self. Call it at the end of the render script's init, once self.predicates and self.state are set. Afterwards self.predicates types as Predicates, which render_update takes. From a defineRenderScript init, call it on the state init returns, which is merged onto self. self — The render script instance.

title: water.render_update
text: render_update(self: object, state: RenderState, predicates: Predicates, draw_options_world: render.DrawOptions) Draws the model predicate into the scene render target, then draws model and the water to the default render target, sampling the scene's depth and color for edge foam and refraction. It needs render_init to have run on the same self, and raises otherwise. Call it from the render script's update after the world view and projection are set. self — The render script instance render_init ran on. state — The render state: the window size and the clear values. predicates — The render script's predicates; pass self.predicates, which holds the water predicate render_init added. draw_options_world — The draw options for the world, used for the scene pass.

text: set_density_params(distance_density: number, depth_density: number) Sets how the color fades with distance and blends with depth. distance_density — How quickly the color fades to the far color: 0.01 very slow, 0.1 normal, 0.5 quick. depth_density — How quickly the color moves from the shallow color to the deep color with water depth.

title: water.set_edge_foam_color
text: set_edge_foam_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the edge foam color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_edge_foam_params
text: set_edge_foam_params(depth_scale: number, noise_strength: number, edge_softness: number, alpha: number) Sets the foam drawn where the water meets other geometry, based on water depth. depth_scale — How quickly the foam fades with depth; lower values give more foam. noise_strength — The noise distortion strength, about 0.2 to 0.5. edge_softness — The edge blend softness, about 0.02 to 0.15. alpha — The overall foam opacity, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_edge_foam_type
text: set_edge_foam_type(type: 0 | 1) Sets how the edge foam is drawn. It also prints SET and the type on every call. type — 0 draws a solid color, 1 a texture.

title: water.set_far_color
text: set_far_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the water color far from the camera, which the surface fades to with distance. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_foam_params
text: set_foam_params(scale: number, speed: number, noise_scale: number, contribution: number) Sets the foam's look and animation. scale — The foam texture tiling; lower values give bigger foam patches. speed — The animation speed. noise_scale — The normal map distortion: 0 none, 0.5 moderate, 1 heavy. contribution — The overall foam visibility: 0 no foam, 0.5 subtle, 1 full.

title: water.set_lod_params
text: set_lod_params(sparkle_distance: number, foam_distance: number) Sets the level-of-detail distances beyond which effects are simplified. sparkle_distance — The distance beyond which sparkles are skipped, saving eight texture samples, 0 to 500. The default is 100. foam_distance — The distance beyond which a simplified foam is drawn, saving three texture samples, 0 to 500. The default is 150.

title: water.set_reflection_params
text: set_reflection_params(strength: number, fresnel_power?: number) Sets the cubemap reflection. The reflection samples the cubemap bound to the water material's reflection_cubemap sampler; this module binds none. strength — The reflection intensity: 0 off, 0.5 moderate, 1 strong. fresnel_power — How much stronger the reflection is at grazing angles, 1 to 5: 1 the same at every angle, 3 natural, 5 very strong. Defaults to 3.

title: water.set_refraction_params
text: set_refraction_params(strength: number, chromatic_aberration?: number) Sets the screen-space refraction. strength — The refraction intensity: 0 off, 0.5 moderate, 1 strong. chromatic_aberration — The color separation: 0 off, 0.5 subtle, 1 strong. Defaults to 0.

title: water.set_shallow_color
text: set_shallow_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the water color in shallow areas. The shader always uses an alpha of 1. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_skybox_cubemap
text: set_skybox_cubemap(cubemap_path: string) Prints a warning and does nothing else. cubemap_path — The cubemap texture path, for example /main/skybox.cubemap.

title: water.set_sparkle_color
text: set_sparkle_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the sparkle tint color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_sparkle_params
text: set_sparkle_params(scale: number, speed: number, exponent: number, enabled?: number) Sets the sparkle (glitter) effect. scale — The sparkle texture tiling. speed — The animation speed. exponent — The sharpness: 1000 many soft sparkles, 10000 medium, 100000 very few, very sharp ones. enabled — 0 disables sparkles and 1 enables them. When omitted, the current value is kept.

title: water.set_sun_color
text: set_sun_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the sun light color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

title: water.set_sun_direction
text: set_sun_direction(x: number, y: number, z: number) Sets the directional light direction. init and update_sun overwrite it with the direction from the water object to the sun. x — The X component of the normalized direction. y — The Y component of the normalized direction. z — The Z component of the normalized direction.

title: water.set_sun_params
text: set_sun_params(exponent: number) Sets the sharpness of the sun's specular highlight. exponent — The highlight sharpness: 100 big and soft, 1000 medium, 10000 tiny and sharp.

title: water.set_wave_normal_params
text: set_wave_normal_params(scale: number, speed: number) Sets the animated normal map that adds ripple detail to the surface. scale — The normal map tiling: 5 large ripples, 10 medium, 20 tiny. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 slow, 1 normal, 2 fast.

title: water.set_wave1
text: set_wave1(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Sets the first wave layer. direction — The wave direction in radians, 0 to 2π: 0 east, π/2 north, π west, 3π/2 south. amplitude — The wave height: 0.1 to 0.5 gentle, 0.5 to 1 medium, 1 to 2 rough, above 2 a storm. wavelength — The distance between wave peaks: 10 to 20 choppy, 20 to 40 ocean waves, above 40 long gentle swells. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 to 1 slow, 1 to 3 moderate, 3 to 5 fast, above 5 very fast.

title: water.set_wave2
text: set_wave2(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Sets the second wave layer, with the same ranges as set_wave1. direction — The wave direction in radians, 0 to 2π. amplitude — The wave height: 0.1 to 0.5 gentle, 0.5 to 1 medium, 1 to 2 rough, above 2 a storm. wavelength — The distance between wave peaks: 10 to 20 choppy, 20 to 40 ocean waves, above 40 long gentle swells. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 to 1 slow, 1 to 3 moderate, 3 to 5 fast, above 5 very fast.

title: water.update_camera
text: update_camera() Re-reads the camera world position and its near and far Z planes. Call it every frame.

title: water.update_sun
text: update_sun() Re-reads the sun position, which moves the light and recomputes the sun direction from the water object, replacing any direction set_sun_direction wrote.

title: water.update
text: update(dt: number) Advances the wave time by dt times the time speed init stored, unless the timer is paused. Call it every frame. dt — The frame time in seconds.

title: tile_raycast API
text: selimanac / defold-tile-raycast tile_raycast Ray Casting in tiled worlds using DDA algorithm.

title: tile_raycast.BOTTOM
text: BOTTOM: number The ray hit the bottom side of the tile.

title: tile_raycast.cast
text: cast(from_x: number, from_y: number, to_x: number, to_y: number): LuaMultiReturn<[ false ] | [ true, number, number, number, number, number, number, number ]> Casts a ray through the tile map and reports the first target tile it hits. A miss returns false alone, so check hit before reading the other values. Before setup, it logs an error and returns nothing. from_x — X coordinate of the ray start. from_y — Y coordinate of the ray start. to_x — X coordinate of the ray end. to_y — Y coordinate of the ray end. hit, then on a hit: tile_x, tile_y, array_id (index in the tile table), tile_id, intersection_x, intersection_y and side (LEFT, RIGHT, TOP or BOTTOM). ⚠️ tile_x is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. ⚠️ tile_y is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. ⚠️ array_id is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged.

title: tile_raycast.get_at
text: get_at(tile_x: number, tile_y: number, tile_id: number) Sets the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its writer under this name and its reader as {@link tile_raycast.set_at}, the reverse of what its documentation describes. tile_x — Tile X coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_y — Tile Y coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_id — Tile ID to set.

title: tile_raycast.LEFT
text: LEFT: number The ray hit the left side of the tile.

title: tile_raycast.reset
text: reset() Clears all tile and tile map data.

title: tile_raycast.RIGHT
text: RIGHT: number The ray hit the right side of the tile.

title: tile_raycast.set_at
text: set_at(tile_x: number, tile_y: number): number Returns the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its reader under this name and its writer as {@link tile_raycast.get_at}, the reverse of what its documentation describes. tile_x — Tile X coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_y — Tile Y coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. The tile ID at that coordinate.

title: tile_raycast.setup
text: setup(tile_width: number, tile_height: number, tilemap_width: number, tilemap_height: number, tiles: number[], target_tiles: number[]) Sets up the tile map to cast rays through, replacing any previous one. tile_width — Width of a single tile. tile_height — Height of a single tile. tilemap_width — Number of tiles horizontally in the tile map. tilemap_height — Number of tiles vertically in the tile map. tiles — One-dimensional table of tile IDs, row by row. target_tiles — IDs of the tiles a ray stops at, such as walls.

title: tile_raycast.TOP
text: TOP: number The ray hit the top side of the tile.

title: wave API
text: selimanac / defold-wave wave Wave simulation that floats, pitches and rolls game objects on a water surface.

title: wave.add_gameobject
text: add_gameobject(instance: SceneGameObjectAddress | Hash | Url, float_offset: number, water_base_y: number, sample_distance: number, rotation_smoothing?: number, use_world_transform?: boolean, forward?: Vector3): number Add a floating game object to the wave simulation. The model must face -Z in its unrotated state: wave sampling, pitch, roll and movement all assume it. To face another way at runtime, call set_yaw after registration, or pass the matching forward. instance — The game object. float_offset — Vertical offset from the water surface. water_base_y — Y coordinate of the flat water plane. sample_distance — Probe offset used to compute the pitch and roll normals. rotation_smoothing — SLERP factor: 0 or omitted disables rotation, 1 snaps instantly. use_world_transform — true for objects nested under another moving object, false for root objects. forward — World-space direction the model's nose faces at registration. Default is vmath.vector3(0, 0, -1). The floater ID used by every later call, or 0 on error such as exceeded capacity.

title: wave.get_wave1_height
text: get_wave1_height(pos_x: number, pos_z: number, time: number): number Sample the wave 1 height at a world position, at the simulation's current time. pos_x — World X. pos_z — World Z. time — Required by the runtime; the sample uses the simulation's own clock instead. The wave height.

title: wave.get_wave2_height
text: get_wave2_height(pos_x: number, pos_z: number, time: number): number Sample the wave 2 height at a world position, at the simulation's current time. pos_x — World X. pos_z — World Z. time — Required by the runtime; the sample uses the simulation's own clock instead. The wave height.

title: wave.init
text: init(wave1_direction: number, wave1_amplitude: number, wave1_wavelength: number, wave1_speed: number, wave2_direction: number, wave2_amplitude: number, wave2_wavelength: number, wave2_speed: number, time_speed: number, gameobject_capacity: number) Initialize the wave simulation. Call it once before any other wave function, with the same parameters the water shader uses. wave1_direction — Wave 1 direction (0.0 to 2.0, multiplied by π internally). wave1_amplitude — Wave 1 height in world units. wave1_wavelength — Wave 1 distance between peaks. wave1_speed — Wave 1 animation speed. wave2_direction — Wave 2 direction (0.0 to 2.0). wave2_amplitude — Wave 2 height in world units. wave2_wavelength — Wave 2 distance between peaks. wave2_speed — Wave 2 animation speed. time_speed — Global time multiplier. gameobject_capacity — Pre-allocated entity table size (for example 256), fixed at init time.

title: wave.is_pause
text: is_pause(): boolean Whether the wave update loop is paused. true when paused.

title: wave.move
text: move(id: number, max_speed: number, speed_factor: number) Begin moving a floater forward at up to max_speed, accelerating by speed_factor per second. id — Floater ID. max_speed — Target and maximum speed in world units per second. speed_factor — Acceleration factor; higher ramps up faster.

title: wave.pause
text: pause(state: boolean) Pause or resume the wave update loop without removing entities. state — true to pause, false to resume.

title: wave.set_yaw
text: set_yaw(id: number, yaw: number) Override the yaw (heading) of a floater, for steering such as a boat turning. id — Floater ID. yaw — Yaw in radians.

title: wave.shutdown
text: shutdown() Shut down the wave simulation and free all resources. The extension finalizer calls it automatically; call it yourself only to reinitialize.

title: wave.stop
text: stop(id: number) Stop a floater. Its target speed becomes 0 and it decelerates smoothly by its speed factor. id — Floater ID.

title: wave.update_wave1
text: update_wave1(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Live-update the wave 1 parameters. Call it in sync with the water shader's wave 1 update to keep visuals and physics aligned. direction — Wave direction. amplitude — Wave height. wavelength — Distance between peaks. speed — Animation speed.

title: wave.update_wave2
text: update_wave2(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Live-update the wave 2 parameters. Call it in sync with the water shader's wave 2 update to keep visuals and physics aligned. direction — Wave direction. amplitude — Wave height. wavelength — Distance between peaks. speed — Animation speed.

title: xmath.clamp
text: xmath.clamp(value_or_out: number | vector3 | vector4, value_or_min: number | vector3 | vector4, min_or_max: number | vector3 | vector4, max: number | vector3 | vector4): number Clamp input value in range [min, max]. For numbers, pass (value, min, max) and returns the clamped number. For vectors, pass (v_in_place, value, min, max) to modify v_in_place. min and max can be numbers or matching vector types. value_or_out — For numbers, the value to clamp. For vectors, the output vector to store the result. value_or_min — For numbers, the minimum value. For vectors, the value to clamp. min_or_max — For numbers, the maximum value. For vectors, the minimum value. max — For vectors only, the maximum value. result — For number inputs, returns the clamped number. For vector inputs, modifies v_in_place and returns nothing.

Ignored if x is a vector3. z — Euler angle around the z-axis in degrees. Ignored if x is a vector3.

title: xmath.lerp
text: xmath.lerp(t_or_out: number | vector3 | vector4 | quaternion, n1_or_t: number | vector3 | vector4 | quaternion, n2_or_v1: number | vector3 | vector4 | quaternion, v2: vector3 | vector4 | quaternion): number Linearly interpolate between two numbers, vectors, or quaternions. For numbers, pass (t, n1, n2) and returns the interpolated number. For vectors/quaternions, pass (v_in_place, t, v1, v2) to modify v_in_place. t_or_out — For numbers, the interpolation factor. For vectors/quaternions, the output value to store the result. n1_or_t — For numbers, the start value. For vectors/quaternions, the interpolation factor. n2_or_v1 — For numbers, the end value. For vectors/quaternions, the start value. v2 — For vectors/quaternions only, the end value. result — For number inputs, returns the interpolated number. For vector/quaternion inputs, modifies v_in_place and returns nothing.

title: ump API
text: tocaRepo / defold-androidextension-ump ump Google User Messaging Platform consent API for Android. The table is absent on other platforms.

title: ump.can_request_ads
text: ump.can_request_ads(): boolean UMP ad-request eligibility. Check after the current update callback. Before then, this can reflect consent stored from an earlier session. allowed — True when UMP allows ad requests.

title: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO
text: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO 0; IAB TCF value says GDPR does not apply.

title: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN
text: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN -1; IAB TCF GDPR applicability value missing or invalid.

title: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES
text: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES 1; IAB TCF value says GDPR applies.

title: ump.get_consent_status
text: ump.get_consent_status(): number Google consent status: 0 unknown, 1 not required, 2 required, 3 obtained. Returns -1 before the consent-information object exists. Status 3 does not distinguish personalized from non-personalized advertising. status — UMP consent status or -1 if unavailable.

title: ump.get_gdpr_applies
text: ump.get_gdpr_applies(): number Read IABTCF_gdprApplies from Android default preferences after a successful UMP update. This is a GDPR applicability signal, not a country code or vendor consent. value — ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO, ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES, or ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN if missing or invalid.

title: ump.get_privacy_options_state
text: ump.get_privacy_options_state(): number Diagnostic state of the latest privacy-options form. state — One of ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_NOT_SHOWN, ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_SHOWING, ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED, or ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_ERROR.

title: ump.get_purpose_consents
text: ump.get_purpose_consents(): string Read the raw IABTCF_PurposeConsents bit string from Android default preferences. Call after a successful UMP update or privacy-options callback. The third character represents TCF Purpose 3 consent. value — Raw purpose-consent bit string, or nil if unavailable.

title: ump.get_request_state
text: ump.get_request_state(): number Diagnostic state of the latest consent information update and form. Prefer the request callback to polling this value. state — One of ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING, ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING, ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE, or ump.REQUEST_STATE_FAILED.

title: ump.initialize_mobile_ads_sdk
text: ump.initialize_mobile_ads_sdk() Legacy, nonfunctional export. Its required Java method is absent from this extension. Do not call it. If using the Defold AdMob extension, call admob.initialize() after the UMP flow instead.

title: ump.is_privacy_options_required
text: ump.is_privacy_options_required(): boolean Whether UMP requires a privacy-options entry point. Returns false before consent information is available. required — True when a privacy-options entry point is required.

title: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED
text: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED 2; privacy-options form closed without a UMP error.

title: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_ERROR
text: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_ERROR 3; privacy-options form failed.

title: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_NOT_SHOWN
text: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_NOT_SHOWN 0; initial privacy-options state.

title: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_SHOWING
text: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_SHOWING 1; privacy-options request in progress.

title: ump.request_consent_info_update
text: ump.request_consent_info_update(test_device: boolean, test_device_hashed_id: string, callback?: function, defer_form?: boolean) Request fresh consent information and show a consent form if required. Call on every launch. The callback runs on the Defold update thread after the update and any required form finish unless defer_form is true. In deferred mode the callback runs after the information update, before any form opens; call show_consent_form_if_required to finish the flow. A successful callback means no UMP error, not consent to personalized ads. test_device — Enable UMP debug mode and force EEA geography for the registered test device. test_device_hashed_id — Hashed test device ID. Pass an empty string when test_device is false. callback — Called when the update and any required form finish. defer_form — Pause after the information update so an application notice can precede a required form. Defaults to false.

title: ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE
text: ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE 1; update and form step finished without a UMP error.

title: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FAILED
text: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FAILED 2; information update or form failed.

title: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING
text: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING 3; update succeeded and the form step is waiting or in progress.

title: ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING
text: ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING 0; initial state or consent information update in progress.

title: ump.reset_consent_information
text: ump.reset_consent_information() Clear UMP consent information for testing if its object has been created. Start a new request afterward. Diagnostic request/form states are not reset by this call.

title: ump.show_consent_form_if_required
text: ump.show_consent_form_if_required(callback?: function) Continue a successful deferred consent-information update. Check was_consent_form_required() to decide whether to show an application notice first. Call only once, after that notice has closed. The callback runs after the required form closes or fails, or immediately if no form is required. Advertising must wait for this callback. callback — Called when the form step finishes.

title: ump.show_privacy_options_form
text: ump.show_privacy_options_form(callback?: function) Open the UMP privacy-options form in response to user input. Check is_privacy_options_required() first. A successful callback means the form closed without an error, not that the user granted consent. callback — Called after the privacy-options form is dismissed or fails.

title: ump.was_consent_form_required
text: ump.was_consent_form_required(): boolean Whether the latest successful information update found a required normal consent form. Resets when a new update starts. May remain true if that form later fails. required — True if the latest successful update required a form.

title: asobi.client.create
text: create(host: string, port?: number, use_ssl?: boolean): Client Creates a client for an asobi server, with its realtime connection. Nothing connects until realtime.connect is called. host — The server's host name. port — The server's port. Defaults to 8084. use_ssl — Whether to use https and wss. Defaults to false.

title: asobi.client.quick_start
text: quick_start(opts: QuickStartOptions): Client Signs a guest in, connects and queues for a match in one call, registering every handler before it connects. The sign-in runs asynchronously, so the client returns at once; use create and the realtime connection directly for entity sync or custom match state. opts — The server, the mode and the callbacks. The client, for disconnecting later or reaching the rest of the API.

title: asobi.device API
text: widgrensit / asobi-defold · device asobi.device Guest device credentials: a stable device id and secret that a game generates once, saves, and presents to guest sign-in on every launch, so the same pair resumes the same player. DeviceOptions

title: asobi.device._base64
text: base64: (bytes: string) => string Internal. The standard base64 encoder generate uses, exposed for upstream's encoder test.

title: asobi.device.clear
text: clear(opts?: Pick<DeviceOptions, 'app' | 'file'>) Erases the saved pair, so the next load_or_create mints a new guest. The server account is not deleted. Pass the same save file used to sign in. opts — The save file.

title: asobi.device.DeviceOptions.app
text: app?: string The save file's application name, passed to sys.get_save_file. Defaults to "asobi".

title: asobi.device.DeviceOptions.device_id
text: device_id?: string A fixed device id, used in place of a random one.

title: asobi.device.DeviceOptions.file
text: file?: string The save file's name, passed to sys.get_save_file. Defaults to "guest_device".

title: asobi.device.DeviceOptions.random_bytes
text: random_bytes?: (n: number) => string Returns n random bytes from a stronger source than the default, which uses the browser's crypto on HTML5 and a seeded math.random elsewhere. It must return at least 32 bytes when asked for 32.

title: asobi.device.generate
text: generate(opts?: Pick<DeviceOptions, 'random_bytes' | 'device_id'>): LuaMultiReturn<[ device_id: string, device_secret: string ]> Generates a new device id and secret without saving them. The secret is standard base64 of 32 random bytes, the shape the server requires. opts — The random byte source and a fixed device id. The device id and the device secret.

title: asobi.device.load_or_create
text: load_or_create(opts?: DeviceOptions): LuaMultiReturn<[ device_id: string, device_secret: string ]> Loads the saved device id and secret, or generates a pair and saves it on first run. Outside the engine it generates a pair without saving. On HTML5 a pair saved in the older save format is replaced, since web builds writing it all minted the same id. opts — The save file, the random byte source and a fixed device id. The device id and the device secret.

title: asobi.http API
text: widgrensit / asobi-defold · http asobi.http The asobi REST transport. Each verb sends a JSON request to the client's server with its access token, refreshes the token pair once and retries on a 401 outside /auth/, and calls back with the decoded body or an error. A project reaches it as client.http, and every asobi.api. module sends through it. HttpError

title: asobi.http._build_url
text: build_url(client: unknown, path: unknown, query: unknown): string Internal. Joins the client's base_url, the path and the query string: every verb calls it.

title: asobi.http._error
text: error(body: unknown, status: unknown): HttpError Internal. Shapes a failed response's body into an HttpError: handle_response calls it.

title: asobi.http._handle_response
text: handle_response(response: unknown, callback: unknown) Internal. Decodes a response's body and calls back with it, or with an error for a status of 400 or more or a body that is not JSON: request calls it.

title: asobi.http._headers
text: headers(client: unknown): Record<string, string> Internal. The JSON content type and, while the client holds an access token, its bearer header: request calls it.

title: asobi.http._is_auth_path
text: is_auth_path(path: unknown): boolean Internal. Whether a path is an /auth/ route, which never refreshes: request calls it.

title: asobi.http._refresh_and_retry
text: refresh_and_retry(client: unknown, method: unknown, path: unknown, url: unknown, data: unknown, callback: unknown) Internal. Refreshes the token pair through client.auth.refresh and replays the request, or calls back with auth_expired: request calls it.

title: asobi.http._request
text: request(client: unknown, method: unknown, path: unknown, url: unknown, data: unknown, callback: unknown, retried: unknown) Internal. Sends one request and, on a 401 outside /auth/ while the client holds a refresh token, refreshes once and replays it: every verb calls it.

title: asobi.http._urlencode
text: urlencode(str: unknown): string Internal. Url-encodes a value after tostring: build_url and asobi.api.auth's unlink_provider call it.

title: asobi.http.delete
text: delete(client: Client, path: string, callback?: HttpCallback) Sends a DELETE with no body to the client's base_url plus path. client — The client to send as. path — The path, from its leading /. callback — Receives the decoded body, or the error. delete(client: Client, path: string, body: Payload | undefined, callback?: HttpCallback) Sends a DELETE to the client's base_url plus path, with a JSON body when one is given. client — The client to send as. path — The path, from its leading /. body — The body. callback — Receives the decoded body, or the error.

title: asobi.http.get
text: get(client: Client, path: string, query?: HttpQuery, callback?: HttpCallback) Sends a GET to the client's base_url plus path. client — The client to send as. path — The path, from its leading /. query — The query string. callback — Receives the decoded body, or the error.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.code
text: code?: string The server's machine-readable error code, empty when it sent none. Absent when the token refresh after a 401 failed, and when the body was not JSON.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.details
text: details?: unknown The details the server sent with the error.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.error
text: error: string The server's message, HTTP <status> when it sent none, auth_expired when the token refresh after a 401 failed, or invalid_response when the body was not JSON.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.fields
text: fields?: unknown The per-field errors a form-validation route sends.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.raw
text: raw?: string The first 200 characters of a body that was not JSON.

title: asobi.http.HttpError.status_code
text: status_code: number The HTTP status code, 401 when the token refresh after a 401 failed.

title: asobi.http.post
text: post(client: Client, path: string, body?: Payload, callback?: HttpCallback) Sends a POST with a JSON body to the client's base_url plus path. client — The client to send as. path — The path, from its leading /. body — The body. Defaults to {}. callback — Receives the decoded body, or the error.

title: asobi.http.put
text: put(client: Client, path: string, body?: Payload, callback?: HttpCallback) Sends a PUT with a JSON body to the client's base_url plus path. client — The client to send as. path — The path, from its leading /. body — The body. Defaults to {}. callback — Receives the decoded body, or the error.

title: asobi.realtime API
text: widgrensit / asobi-defold · realtime asobi.realtime The realtime connection a client creates as client.realtime: one websocket that authenticates the session, carries matchmaking, matches, worlds, chat, votes and extension calls, and keeps a registry of the entities the server syncs. Realtime RealtimeEvents WorldAck JoinOptions ListOptions MatchmakerOptions RpcError

A name RealtimeEvents does not list raises an error, and handlers for one event run in the order they were registered. The reply to a request made with a callback goes to that callback rather than to an event. event — The event. callback — The handler.

title: asobi.realtime.Realtime.rpc
text: rpc(method: string, params?: Payload, callback?: (result: Payload | undefined, err: RpcError | string | undefined) => void) Calls a server extension's RPC method. text: wavedash.EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED Fired once per purchase made while the game is running (in-game paywall, game page, gift, another tab), plus, at launch, once per consumable still unfulfilled. Payload: { purchaseId, contentIdentifier, type, fulfilled, purchasedAt, receiptJwt }. Durables arrive with fulfilled true, already granted. For a consumable, grant it, then call fulfill_purchase_async(purchaseId); until then it's redelivered every launch, so dedupe on purchaseId if you persist grants.

title: wavedash.fulfill_purchase_async
text: wavedash.fulfill_purchase_async(purchase_id: string): function Mark a consumable purchase fulfilled once the grant is saved, so it stops being redelivered. A game's backend can do the same with POST /api/purchases/{purchaseId}/fulfill and the purchase's receiptJwt; both are idempotent, so calling either or both is safe. Resolves with a status in data: FULFILLED, ALREADY_FULFILLED (also success), or NOT_FOUND (unknown or refunded: don't grant it). This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'fulfillPurchase' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine. response — Returns { status } in data. (Note: Only if called from within a coroutine)

title: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_FULFILLED

title: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND
text: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND fulfill_purchase_async status: unknown purchase, or it was refunded. Don't grant it.

title: defold/asset-pbr
text: A base metallic-roughness PBR material with vertex and fragment shaders under /defold-pbr. The shaders read glTF material data populated by the model component and light data from Defold's built-in light components. Assign /defold-pbr/pbr.material to any model that should use the shader. Include pbr_lighting.glsl from an extension shader to add its own lighting terms. Models draw through a render script that sets the camera view and projection with render and camera. The material applies to model components.

title: defold/assets-defold
text: Official Defold logo images in PNG and SVG: the plain logo, the logo with "Defold" text, and the "Made with Defold" logo. Each comes in several color variants and widths of 64, 128, 160 and 320 pixels plus a high-resolution original. Use the images under /assets-defold, for example on a splash screen. Ask the Defold Foundation for permission before using other logo versions.

title: defold/codepad
text: A browser-based Defold code editor with live preview and console, usable as a stand-alone page or embedded in another web page. It includes an HTML5 template, static web resources, attachable go.script and gui.gui_script files, and the codepad.codepad Lua module. Set codepad/template.html as the HTML5 template. Add /codepad/bundle_resources/ to Bundle Resources. Require codepad.codepad from a script. Forward codepad.init(self, scenes), codepad.update(self, dt) and codepad.on_message(...) from the script's lifecycle functions. It runs only in a browser and talks to the page through html5. Each editable scene is loaded through a collectionproxy.

title: defold/defold-pbr
text: A work-in-progress PBR core with shaders, a material, a reference render script and the defold-pbr/core Lua module. Editor scripts generate environment lighting assets from .hdr files and extract .glb content into Defold collections. Attach /defold-pbr/core.script to a game object to create the PBR context. Require defold-pbr/core to call functions such as set_environment, add_light_point and set_camera_world. In the render script, pass get_constants() to the model draw call and wrap it in enable_textures() and disable_textures(). The module builds its constant buffer and binds textures with render, and reads texture handles with resource.

title: defold/defwarez-shared
text: Shared DEFWAREZ files: the defwarez-shared/defwarez Lua module, a render script, a font, an atlas, input bindings and a mock collection for local testing. Require defwarez-shared/defwarez from a game script. Report progress with functions such as add_score, set_score and player_done. The module reads the defwarez.live setting with sys. It posts results to the host with msg, or to the mock collection when not live.

title: defold/extension-android
text: An example native extension for Android that combines C++, .java sources, a .jar, a prebuilt static library and Android resources. On Android it registers the androidnative Lua module with functions such as vibrate, getraw and multiply; other platforms get a stub extension with no module. Build the project for Android. Check that androidnative is not nil before calling it, as the example menu GUI script does. See the java_src and lib_src build scripts for how the .jar and .a files are produced.

title: defold/extension-automation-bridge
text: A debug-only native extension that exposes a local HTTP bridge for inspecting and controlling a running game: scene and element queries, input with receipts, screenshots and optional desktop video recording. A bundled Python wrapper drives the bridge, and an opt-in automation_bridge Lua module lets scripts call publish, emit, command and annotate. Install the Python wrapper with the extension's install.py. Inspect scenes, send input and take screenshots; these need no Lua setup. Set application_api = 1 under [automation_bridge] in game.project to enable the Lua module.

title: defold/extension-energy-saver
text: An energysaver.go game object with a script and a GUI dimmer that lower power use after a period of input inactivity. It reduces the frame rate, dims the screen by 50%, and finally disables rendering, each on its own configurable delay. Drag energysaver.go into the bootstrap collection. Tune its script properties. Set the is_energy_saving_allowed property with go.set to pause the savings temporarily, for example during cutscenes. The script drives sys (sys.set_update_frequency, sys.set_render_enabled), timer for the inactivity delays, and gui for the dimming overlay.

title: defold/extension-eos
text: A native extension wrapping the Epic Online Services SDK, bundling SDK libraries for Windows, Linux and macOS. It registers an eos Lua module with functions such as eos.init, eos.get_achievement_definitions and eos.get_stats_definitions. Do not rely on it yet: the upstream README marks the extension as work in progress and not ready for use, and gives no installation steps. See the example main.script, which calls eos.init with product, sandbox, deployment and client credentials before querying achievement and stats definitions.

title: defold/extension-fbinstant
text: A native extension for HTML5 builds that integrates the Facebook Instant Games API. It registers an fbinstant Lua module with functions such as fbinstant.initialize, fbinstant.start_game, fbinstant.get_player and fbinstant.show_rewarded_video. Configure the HTML5 section of game.project. Start from the engine HTML template and the example collections covering ads, context, leaderboards, payments and player data.

title: defold/extension-gamelift
text: A native extension that runs a Defold game server against the Amazon GameLift Server SDK, with prebuilt SDK libraries for Linux and macOS. It registers a gamelift Lua module with functions such as gamelift.init, gamelift.process_ready and gamelift.accept_player_session. The repository also contains an example client project. On the server, call gamelift.init with a port and listener functions for session start, process termination and health checks. Report readiness with gamelift.process_ready.

title: defold/extension-html5
text: An example native extension for the HTML5 platform showing plain C++ code, a prebuilt Emscripten library, inline JavaScript through EM_ASM, and an Emscripten JavaScript library. It registers an html5nativeext Lua module with demonstration functions such as html5nativeext.multiply, html5nativeext.fibonacci and html5nativeext.get_user_data. Build the project for HTML5; the repository is an example project rather than a packaged library. Call the module's functions as its main.script does, including polling html5nativeext.get_user_data for data set from the web page.

title: defold/extension-inappupdate
text: A placeholder for an Android in-app update extension built on the Play Core in-app updates feature. At this revision the native code is still the extension template: it registers a myextension Lua module whose only function, myextension.reverse, reverses a string. Expect no in-app update calls yet: the upstream README describes the Play Core feature but gives no installation steps. See the example script, which calls myextension.reverse and prints the result.

title: defold/extension-kaios
text: A native extension for KaiOS web builds. It provides a modified engine HTML template, maps the left softkey, right softkey and call keys to KEY_F1, KEY_F2 and KEY_MENU, and registers a kaios Lua module with kaios.exit, kaios.play_sound and kaios.stop_sound. Include the sound files with the bundle resources setting in game.project, since kaios.play_sound plays them through the JavaScript AudioContext. For KaiAds integration, use the separate extension-kaiads repository upstream points to.

title: defold/extension-lua-preprocessor
text: A Lua preprocessor that hooks into the Lua builder plugin system in bob, the Defold build tool. It strips or keeps code at build time based on --#IF, --#ELSE and --#ENDIF blocks that test the RELEASE, DEBUG or HEADLESS keywords. Use Defold 1.4.2 or higher. Wrap code in the conditional comment blocks. Write --DEBUG_ASSERT(...) to include an assert only in debug builds.

title: defold/extension-onetrust
text: A work-in-progress native extension for the OneTrust SDK that upstream describes as not working. On Android it registers an onetrust Lua module whose only function, onetrust.init, is currently an empty stub; other platforms get a null extension with no module. Guard the call with if onetrust then onetrust.init() end, as the example script does, since the module exists only on Android.

title: defold/extension-playintegrity
text: A placeholder repository for a Defold extension to integrate the Google Play Integrity API. At this revision it contains only a README and a license, with no extension code, Lua module, or example project. Expect nothing to use yet: no callable API is provided at this revision.

title: defold/extension-poco
text: A native extension that implements the Poco test automation API, so Python test scripts on a computer can dump the scene graph and send clicks, swipes and key events to a running game. It ships the poco.lua.defold-poco Lua server module and a native poco_helper module (dump, click, swipe, keyevent), plus a test project and Python example scripts. require('poco.lua.defold-poco') in a script or GUI script. Call poco:init_server(15004) in init. Call poco:server_loop() in update. Add custom functions the client can call with poco:set_dispatch_fn. poco:set_view_proj and poco:set_gui_view_proj take view projection matrices built with vmath, which default to the identity matrix.

title: defold/extension-profile-counters
text: An advanced example native extension that retrieves profiling data at runtime, with the counters available even in release builds. It registers a profile Lua module whose profile.get_properties returns a table of the latest counters. Call profile.get_properties() each update and print the result, as the example project's main.script does. Expect the regular profiler normally included in Defold to be removed, as upstream notes.

title: defold/extension-prometheus
text: Build-time Lua obfuscation using Prometheus, hooked into the Lua builder plugin system in bob, the Defold build tool. Scripts are obfuscated as they are built; the extension adds no Lua module for game scripts to call. Fork the repository, as upstream asks, add your fork's archive URL to game.project under [project] dependencies, then Fetch Libraries in the Defold editor. Put a Prometheus configuration file named prometheus.lua in the project root. Set disabled = 1 under a [prometheus] section in game.project to turn obfuscation off.

title: defold/extension-qrcode
text: A small native extension that encodes and decodes QR codes, using quirc for decoding. It registers a qrcode Lua module with qrcode.scan, which reads the text from an image buffer, and qrcode.generate, which returns a QR code image buffer and its side length. See the included example app, which scans camera images and creates QR codes; it depends on a camera extension that supports only macOS, iOS and Android. Both functions work on buffer objects: scan expects a first stream of UINT8 3 texels, and generate returns a data stream of UINT8 1.

title: defold/extension-resource-encryption
text: A build-time Bob plugin that encrypts resources in the game archive and a native runtime counterpart that registers a decryption function with the resource system. It uses the same XTEA algorithm as the engine but lets a project replace the default key or the algorithm itself. Fork the repository, add your fork's archive URL to game.project under [project] dependencies, then Fetch Libraries in the Defold editor. Change the key in both the Java plugin and src/plugin.cpp. Rebuild the plugin jar with build_plugin.sh after changing the build-time part. Expect no functions for scripts to call.

title: defold/extension-simpledata
text: A native extension that adds a .simpledata component type, editable in the editor and built by a Bob plugin. Each component holds preset fields such as name, f32, i32, v3 and an array_f32 list. It also serves as an example of adding a custom resource and component type. Add .simpledata components to game objects. Read single fields with go.get. Read the whole float array into a Lua table with simpledata.get_array_f32(url). Component fields are read through go (go.get), including indexed access to array_f32.

title: defold/extension-teal
text: Build-time support for Teal, a typed dialect of Lua. A Bob plugin compiles and type checks .tl files during the build, and an editor script registers a Teal language server. The native part is an empty extension. Use Defold 1.8.1 or later. Create a tlconfig.lua in the project root. Require .tl files from scripts and Lua modules as if they were .lua files.

title: defold/extension-texturepacker
text: A .tpatlas resource type for atlases exported from the TexturePacker tool, with an editor integration, a Bob build plugin, and a Defold exporter for TexturePacker. A .tpatlas works like a regular .atlas, including animations, but its images come from the exported .tpinfo file. Install the exporter in TexturePacker. Export a .tpinfo file. Create a Texture Packer Atlas in the editor and point it at that file. The skins example declares resource atlas properties and swaps a sprite image at runtime with go.set.

title: defold/extension-videoplayer
text: An example native extension that decodes .webm video into a buffer, with no sound support. Upstream marks it as an example not meant for production use. It registers a videoplayer Lua module with functions such as videoplayer.open, videoplayer.get_frame and videoplayer.update. Load the video with resource.load. Open it with videoplayer.open. Call videoplayer.update each frame and upload the frame buffer to a texture. The example loads the video and writes each frame with resource (resource.load, resource.set_texture); the frame is a buffer with one RGB stream, shown on a sprite.

title: defold/extension-vulkan
text: A native extension that adds a Vulkan graphics adapter, used when the device supports Vulkan and falling back to OpenGL otherwise. It links MoltenVK on macOS and iOS. It adds no functions for scripts to call. Enable shader.output_spirv, or builds fail to compile. To build with Vulkan only, exclude the OpenGL adapter through an application manifest.

title: defold/extension-webmonetization
text: An HTML5 native extension that integrates the Web Monetization JavaScript API, so a game can detect whether a player has an active payment stream. It registers a webmonetization Lua module with is_monetized, set_listener and EVENT constants for the stream state. Set payment_pointer in a [webmonetization] section of game.project. Call webmonetization.is_monetized() or register a listener with webmonetization.set_listener to react to payment events.

title: Authoring forked library types
text: Authoring forked library types Some Defold libraries ship no usable structured type source — no .script_api, no inline LuaLS (---@) annotations, and no README that documents the surface precisely enough to parse. The LuaLS, .script_api, and markdown front-ends all ingest a primary source and generate a declaration; a library with none of those has nothing to generate from. Its .d.ts must be written by hand — either forked from an existing hand-authored declaration or authored fresh — and vendored into the library's folder in the toolchain repo as first-party source. resolve then prints the vendored declaration into the consumer's project, the way it prints the generated lanes' declarations. Like the other lanes, adding such a library is data, not code: you add one fork to the library's library.json in its folder, packages/library-types/data/<version>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (the newest version-named folder), vendor the .d.ts into the folder's fork/, run the generation command, and commit the library's files. Every path a fork names is relative to the library folder, except apiDoc and fidelity, which are relative to packages/library-types/, where the tools write their reports. The toolchain's authored front-end (packages/cli/src/library/sync-authored-types.ts) is the reusable machinery; you touch config and fixtures, not the pipeline. This page is for library-type authors. Library data lives in the toolchain repo under packages/library-types/data/, so you add or change a library with a pull request there, not to defold-typescript/library-data. If you only want to use a vendored library in your own game, you need nothing here — just declare the dependency and run resolve. The bun commands on this page run from the toolchain root. Each tool reads and writes the library data under packages/library-types/data/ and writes its reports to api-doc/ and fidelity/ in packages/library-types/. The decision: fork, hand-author, or keep? Reach this lane only after ruling out the generated ones. Ask, in order: 1. Does upstream ship a .script_api? → it is a script_api target. 2. Does its Lua carry inline ---@ annotations? → it is a LuaLS target. 3. Does its README document the full surface precisely? → it may be a markdown target (gated on a fidelity comparison; a lossy README is a no-go and the library does not regenerate from markdown). 4. None of the above → it is an authored target, and you choose between fork, hand-author, and keep. A markdown no-go is a verdict on the markdown source, not on the ts-defold dependency. It says the README cannot regenerate the surface; it says nothing about where the surface should be maintained. That second question is this lane's, and a no-go library reaches question 4 with it still open — so run the cost model below on it exactly as you would on a library that never had a README at all. keep is a legitimate answer, but it has to be chosen, not inherited from the refusal. persist.persist and orthographic.camera are the worked examples. The cost model An authored .d.ts has no upstream source to regenerate from, so every future upstream API change is a manual edit to the vendored declaration. That is the standing cost. Weigh it against the gain of severing ts-defold: a first-party authored surface is authored-here, carries its own upstream repo/tag pin (not the shared ts-defold/library commit), and is maintained on the toolchain repo's own cadence rather than inherited from a third-party vendoring.
