The pin kind. refKind in the library's library.json says whether the pin is a release, a tag or a commit, and the docs page's adopt step follows it. It moves with the pin: api-surface-loader.test.ts reds when the asset-portal register records another kind at the same ref. The pin-refresh record. packages/library-types/pin-refresh.json states which members a bump added and removed, one entry per refresh, each tagged with the lane it belongs to (luals, script-api, or openapi). packages/cli/src/library/pin-refresh.test.ts checks every name it states against the surface that lane's own parser yields for the committed fixtures — buildTargetModel, committedScriptApiDoc, or parseOpenApi. Regenerating the fixtures without updating the record reds ci, so derive the new entry by diffing the old and new member names rather than from upstream release notes. A second key, deliberatelyUnmoved, records a pin you examined and chose to leave alone, and is guarded on its ref alone — so a note left standing after that pin later moves also reds. The guard deliberately does not check that the record is complete, nor its changedMembers and notes, which are prose. The compile-only surface proofs. The .test-d.ts files under each library folder's usage/ assert the emitted .d.ts by assigning from it, and pin the absence of non-public members with @ts-expect-error. A bump breaks them in both directions: a member that left the public surface fails the assignment, and a member upstream stopped marking @field private or @local makes its expect-error directive unused (TS2578). The second is the easy one to misread — check the old and new fixture annotations before assuming the emitter regressed, because dropping a private marker upstream is a real surface change and the declaration is then correct to emit. The generated docs artifacts. packages/docs/llms.txt, packages/docs/llms-full.txt, and the docs-site search and symbol indexes are committed, not built on demand. Regenerate them with bun run --cwd packages/docs-site build-indexes whenever the API-doc model changed. What a re-pin does not touch The corpus pin and a consumer's declared dependency are different things, and conflating them is the first mistake a repo-wide find-and-replace makes. Several CLI tests hardcode archive URLs and extracted-entry paths, and some of them pin exactly the corpus string. packages/cli/src/library-match.test.ts, packages/cli/src/resolve.test.ts and packages/cli/src/druid-resolve-e2e.test.ts all carry a druid version literal in consumer archive URLs, and it can equal the ref the registry entry holds. That collision is the reason a repo-wide find-and-replace is unsafe: one copy of the version must move with the bump (the registry entry, and the provenance assertions named above), and another must not. normalizeSourceId (packages/cli/src/library-match.ts) strips /archive/<ref>.zip and matches on the repo name alone, so a consumer fixture is version-independent either way — which cuts both ways. Rewriting its version leaves the suite green, so a green bun test is not evidence the rewrite was correct. The 1.2.3 fixtures in packages/cli/src/library-scene-materialize.test.ts and the later resolve.test.ts cases are consumer fixtures on the same footing and equally out of scope. Leave them alone. A corpus bump changes the data folder, the floors, the emitted artifacts and the docs indexes. It does not change what a test project declares in its game.project. Check the work Then re-run bun run upstream:library-check — the repo you bumped should now report as current, and the issue the workflow opened can be closed. Retiring a curated target A curated target is only needed while its upstream ships no types resolve can use. Once an upstream release ships a types/ folder that resolve accepts, every project on that release gets those files in place of the curated copy, and the curated copy only costs a pin, a parity floor and a re-pin per release. bun run upstream:shipped-types-check reads the newest release of every repo behind a curated target, across the authored, LuaLS, script_api and native lanes, and runs its types/ folder through the same selection and compile check resolve applies: The newest release is the newest tag by commit date, or the default branch head for a repo with no tags. Each repo reports accepted, rejected with the check's first error, or none. A repo it could not read reports unknown and exits the command non-zero. The Library upstream check workflow runs the same sweep weekly and opens one issue per accepted repo, titled retire curated types for <slug>: <ref> ships types. The issue lists the shipped files and every curated entry the repo backs. The issue retires nothing. Retirement is a reviewed change, as pixels was (toolchain commit a32a1972), that removes each listed entry's registry entry, the input the issue lists for it, its /api page, vendored upstream source and parity floor, along with the tests that named it. Before making it, weigh the projects left behind: a project still on a release before the one that ships types has no types/ folder to fall back on once the curated copy is gone. An upstream maintainer gets the curated files to commit with export-types, as Shipping types with a library describes.
